# Backend foundation Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Build the foundation of `metis-backend`: a Gradle build on Java 25, an empty Spring Boot core that builds as an image and answers its probes in the local stack, and a Java tool that runs thirteen checks, each proven red by its counter-tests, behind `./verify` and `./canary`.
**Architecture:** One Gradle build with two projects, `core` (the Spring Boot application) and `tools` (the command-line tool of the checks), and the included build `build-logic` with the one convention plugin both apply. Every check is a root task `check<Name>`; the tool runs them in order, judges what Gradle and JUnit do not (skipped tests, exact floors, mutants, unused code, language, the running image) and writes the record `reports/verify.json` and `reports/verify.md`. Each counter-test plants one defect in a copy of the tree and requires its check red for that defect.
**Tech Stack:** Gradle 9.8.1 (Kotlin scripts), Amazon Corretto 25, Spring Boot 4.1.1 (Spring Framework 7.0.9, Jackson 3.1.7, Tomcat 11.0.25), JUnit 6.1.3, PIT 1.30.0, JaCoCo 0.8.15, Error Prone 2.50.0 with NullAway 0.14.2 and JSpecify 1.0.1, ArchUnit 1.5.1, Spotless 8.10.4 with google-java-format 1.36.1, Checkstyle 14.3.0, Dependency Analysis 3.19.2, dependency-license-report 3.1.4, Trivy 0.75.0, gitleaks 8.30.1, hadolint 2.15.1, actionlint 1.7.12, Docker with Compose.
**Spec:** [the backend skeleton design](../specs/2026-10-14-backend-skeleton-design.md), section 12, the row "One, the foundation".

## Global Constraints

- Work in `/Users/mrpo/projects/metis/metis-backend`; every path and command of a task is relative to it, and nothing is created outside `/Users/mrpo/projects/metis`.
- Every shell that runs Gradle, `./verify` or `./canary` first runs `export GRADLE_USER_HOME=/Users/mrpo/projects/metis/.work/gradle JAVA_HOME=/opt/homebrew/opt/openjdk@21`: Homebrew's JDK 21 starts Gradle, and Gradle fetches Corretto 25 for the build and for its daemon.
- Nothing is installed system-wide: no Homebrew, no sudo. Docker Desktop answers on `/var/run/docker.sock`; Colima stays stopped.
- Every Gradle command of a task runs as `./gradlew --console=plain --max-workers=5 ...`: five is half of this machine's ten cores. In the repository the half is computed: test forks, PIT threads, and the workers `./verify` and `./canary` give Gradle.
- One heavy job at a time: a Gradle build, a PIT run, a Docker build or a counter-test.
- An Expected block holds lines of the trial run's output. Its seconds, seeds, tree stamps and memory are what that run measured; a new run prints its own, and the rest of each line must match.
- Never run `git add`, `git commit` or `git push`: the last step of each task adds its files to the ledger, and the owner commits.
- Base package `dev.metis`; root project `metis-backend`; projects `core` and `tools`; the included build `build-logic` holds the one convention plugin, `metis.java-conventions`, that both projects apply.
- The JDK is Amazon Corretto 25 (25.0.4.10.1 in the trial run), fetched by the toolchain resolver `org.gradle.toolchains.foojay-resolver-convention` 1.0.0.
- Every version is written once: in `gradle/libs.versions.toml`, in the plugins of `settings.gradle.kts`, or by Spring Boot 4.1.1's own list. Jackson 3.1.7 and Tomcat 11.0.25 are raised above what Boot manages, to the nearest releases without a known vulnerability, and the JUnit family is on 6.1.3 on every classpath through the catalog's `junit-bom`, since ArchUnit's engine needs that release.
- Licences: the allow-list `config/allowed-licenses.json` does not change. `checkLicense` passes a library that declares at least one allowed licence, so Logback (EPL-2.0 or LGPL-2.1-only), Jakarta Annotations (EPL-2.0 or GPL-2.0-only with the Classpath exception) and SLF4J (MIT, plus an entry the report cannot name) are used under their allowed licence. That is the decided policy of the app: GPL, AGPL and LGPL are refused only when they stand alone ([the dependency policy](../../architecture/decisions/dependency-policy.md), line 20).
- The runtime image takes the security fixes of one pinned Amazon Linux release, `2023.12.20261013`, so that every build installs the same packages. When the image scan turns red, bump it together with the digest of the base: in a container of the new base, `dnf --releasever=latest --showduplicates list --available system-release` shows the newest release, and `dnf --releasever=<release> -v repolist` must print the same repository as `latest`.
- The scanners that are not Gradle plugins run as images pinned by digest: `aquasec/trivy:0.75.0`, `zricethezav/gitleaks:v8.30.1`, `hadolint/hadolint:v2.15.1` and `rhysd/actionlint:1.7.12`, each with the digest the catalog holds; the image builds on `amazoncorretto:25-al2023` and runs on `amazoncorretto:25-al2023-headless`, both pinned by digest in `core/Dockerfile`.
- Every check is a root task `check<Name>` and a row of `Checks.ORDER`, the list of the spec in its order: format, compile, lint, language, architecture, deadcode, tooling, contract, trace, unit, integration, coverage, mutation, deps, secrets, image; plan one builds thirteen of them, and `./verify` refuses a check task the list lacks, in whatever project it is registered. The fast group is the first ten of the spec, format to unit, of which contract and trace come with plan three.
- The bars: 100% of the lines and branches of `core` and `tools`; every PIT mutant of the group STRONGER detected, none SURVIVED and none NO_COVERAGE; no test skipped, failed or aborted; the tests that pass equal `test-floor.json` exactly; every check has a counter-test or a reason in `NoCanary.REASONS`; every check but format, compile, deps and secrets fails when its judge leaves no facts.
- Compile: `-Xlint:all -Werror`; Error Prone with UnusedVariable, UnusedMethod, UnusedNestedClass and NullAway as errors; `NullAway:OnlyNullMarked`; every package has a `package-info.java` with `@NullMarked`.
- Lint: Checkstyle with `CyclomaticComplexity` at 10 and `FileLength` at 300 and nothing else; every escape hatch gives its reason and is counted in `config/debt.json`: a suppression anywhere in the code, a method left out of mutation testing, an annotation whose name holds `Generated`, an excused line of the language check, a class left out of coverage; the list of the classes left out keeps one class of every project at least.
- Dependencies: a Spring Boot starter stands, through a bundle of the Dependency Analysis plugin, for the libraries of it the code uses, named one by one; no project declares a library that a bundle names, since the plugin would never report it unused.
- Code, comments, test names, log messages and tool output are English. A comment is one line that says why and never cites a plan, a ruling, a task, a date or a line number; a deliberate shortcut says `ponytail: <ceiling>; <how to lift it>`.
- No abstraction without a second user: no interface with one implementation, no base class for one subclass, no setting for a value that never changes.
- Out of this plan: PostgreSQL, Flyway, the migration job, Testcontainers and the integration check; Spring Security; the modules `platform`, `workspace` and `delivery`; springdoc, the contract file and the contract and trace checks; Keycloak; the demo data and the restated-literal rule; the pinned copies and `docs.lock`; the relay; the latency budget of the image check.

## Review Focus

The five failure modes the spec implies that are easiest to miss, most likely first. Each one is pinned by a test of the task that owns the code; a reviewer checks that the test still fails when the guard it names is removed.

1. A test skipped, or one test more than the floor, passing the test judge as green: neither Gradle nor JUnit fails on either. Pinned by `TestReportsTest.aSkippedTestAFailedOneOrAPassCountOtherThanTheFloorIsRedAndTheFactsSayWhy` and `TestReportsTest.theFloorIsExactSoOneTestMoreThanItIsRedToo` (Task 10), and by the counter-tests unit-disabled and unit-floor.
2. A counter-test that "catches" its defect while the check is red for another reason, which hides a blind check. Pinned by `CanaryRunTest.aCheckRedForAnotherReasonOrGreenWhilePrintingTheTextDoesNotCatchTheDefect` and `CanaryRunTest.aCheckAlreadyRedBeforePlantingFailsAtOnceAndPlantsNothing` (Task 7).
3. A record that reads green while its rows come from different trees, from a tree git cannot list, or from a hand edit. Pinned by `ReportTest.oneRowOnAnUnknownTreeMakesTheSharedTreeUnknownAndPutsAWarningAboveTheTable`, `LedgerTest.aLedgerIsReadBackOnlyInTheShapeThisToolWritesWithSafeTextAndKnownChecks` (Task 5), `VerifyCommandTest.handEditsToTheReportDoNotSurviveAnAppendWhichReadsOnlyTheLedger` and `VerifyCommandTest.aFullRunThatGitCannotListForExitsOneAndSaysWhyAndARunOfSomeChecksDoesNot` (Task 6).
4. A `mutations.xml` that an earlier run left behind, judged as the report of this run. Pinned by `MutationsTest.theScopeIsWrittenForTheMutationTasksAndAReportOfAnEarlierRunIsRemoved` (Task 14).
5. An image whose JVM is not the first process, so the stop signal never reaches it and the platform kills it after the grace period. Pinned by `ImageCheckTest.aStopSignalThatDoesNotEndTheJvmInsideTheGracePeriodIsRed` (Task 17) and the counter-test image-shell-entrypoint.

### Task 1: The Gradle build and the proof that PIT runs on JUnit 6

The build: the Gradle 9.8.1 wrapper, the settings with the toolchain resolver, the one catalog of versions, lock files in strict mode, sha256 checksums of every artifact, the included build `build-logic` with the convention plugin `metis.java-conventions`, and the project `core`. The catalog holds every version of the plan, so no later task edits it. Then the one open question of the spec is settled before anything else: PIT 1.30.0 through the Gradle plugin, as it is, finds and runs JUnit 6 tests. A probe proves it: a weak test leaves both mutants of `Probe.twice` SURVIVED in `mutations.xml`, a strong test kills both. The probe is deleted at the end of the task.

```kotlin
plugins {
    java
    id("info.solidsoft.pitest")
}

val catalog = the<VersionCatalogsExtension>().named("libs")

// Half the cores, so that tests and mutation testing never take the whole machine.
val half = (Runtime.getRuntime().availableProcessors() / 2).coerceAtLeast(1)

    toolchain {
        languageVersion = JavaLanguageVersion.of(25)
        vendor = JvmVendorSpec.AMAZON

    lockAllConfigurations()
    lockMode = LockMode.STRICT

dependencies {
    implementation(platform(catalog.findLibrary("spring-boot-bom").get()))
    testImplementation(platform(catalog.findLibrary("junit-bom").get()))
    testImplementation("org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter-api")

    testRuntimeOnly("org.junit.platform:junit-platform-launcher")
}

tasks.withType<Test>().configureEach {
    useJUnitPlatform()
    maxParallelForks = half
}

pitest {

    junit5PluginVersion = catalog.findVersion("pitest-junit5").get().requiredVersion
    targetClasses = setOf("dev.metis.${project.name}.*")
    targetTests = setOf("dev.metis.${project.name}.*")
    mutators = setOf("STRONGER")
    threads = half
    outputFormats = setOf("XML", "HTML")
    timestampedReports = false
}
```

- [ ] **Step 5: Write a probe with a weak test**

The probe is no file of the repository: it lives for this task only. `--rerun` below makes PIT run even when the build cache holds the result of an earlier run of the same probe.

```sh
mkdir -p core/src/main/java/dev/metis/core core/src/test/java/dev/metis/core
cat > core/src/main/java/dev/metis/core/Probe.java <<'EOF'
package dev.metis.core;

final class Probe {

  private Probe() {}

  static int twice(int value) {
    return value * 2;
  }
}
EOF
cat > core/src/test/java/dev/metis/core/ProbeTest.java <<'EOF'
package dev.metis.core;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

class ProbeTest {

  @Test
  void twiceOfZeroIsZero() {
    assertThat(Probe.twice(0)).isZero();
  }
}
EOF
```

### Task 2: The core application: probes, JSON logs, graceful shutdown, virtual threads

The empty Spring Boot 4.1.1 application, compiled under the rules of the compile check from its first line: `-Xlint:all -Werror`, Error Prone with the unused-code patterns raised to errors, NullAway on `@NullMarked` packages. Tests run in a random order of classes and methods, with the seed printed so that a run can be repeated, and every test task cleans its reports first. Jackson 3.1.7 and Tomcat 11.0.25 replace the 3.1.5 and 11.0.24 that Spring Boot 4.1.1 manages: Trivy finds known vulnerabilities in both (Task 15 and Task 17 prove the scans clean).

**Files:**

- Test: `core/src/test/java/dev/metis/core/CoreApplicationTest.java`
- Test: `core/src/test/java/dev/metis/core/ProbesTest.java`
- Test: `core/src/test/java/dev/metis/core/ShutdownTest.java`
- Test: `core/src/test/java/dev/metis/core/TestEndpoints.java`
- Create: `core/src/main/java/dev/metis/core/package-info.java`
- Create: `core/src/main/java/dev/metis/core/CoreApplication.java`
- Create: `core/src/main/resources/application.yml`
- Modify: `build-logic/src/main/kotlin/metis.java-conventions.gradle.kts`
- Modify: `core/build.gradle.kts`
- Generated by a command of this task: `core/gradle.lockfile`, `gradle/verification-metadata.xml`

**Interfaces:**

- Consumes: the convention plugin and the catalog of Task 1.
- Produces: the class `dev.metis.core.CoreApplication` with `public static void main(String[] args)`; `application.yml` (name `metis-core`, no banner, virtual threads, ECS JSON logs on standard output); liveness and readiness at `/actuator/health/liveness` and `/actuator/health/readiness` answering `{"status":"UP"}` and nothing more; the discovery page `/actuator` naming the health endpoint alone; graceful shutdown. The actuator starter is a dependency of the run only, since no code uses it.

- [ ] **Step 1: Add the compile and test rules to the conventions, and the Spring Boot dependencies to core**

`build-logic/src/main/kotlin/metis.java-conventions.gradle.kts`:

```kotlin
import net.ltgt.gradle.errorprone.errorprone
import org.gradle.api.tasks.testing.logging.TestExceptionFormat

plugins {
    java
    id("net.ltgt.errorprone")
    id("info.solidsoft.pitest")
}

val catalog = the<VersionCatalogsExtension>().named("libs")

// Half the cores, so that tests and mutation testing never take the whole machine.
val half = (Runtime.getRuntime().availableProcessors() / 2).coerceAtLeast(1)

java {
    toolchain {
        languageVersion = JavaLanguageVersion.of(25)
        vendor = JvmVendorSpec.AMAZON
    }
}

dependencyLocking {
    lockAllConfigurations()
    lockMode = LockMode.STRICT
}

dependencies {
    implementation(platform(catalog.findLibrary("spring-boot-bom").get()))
    implementation(platform(catalog.findLibrary("jackson-bom").get()))
    constraints {
        for (tomcat in listOf("tomcat-embed-core", "tomcat-embed-el", "tomcat-embed-websocket")) {

// A new seed on every run, printed, so that a test that depends on another one shows, and the run can be repeated.
val testSeed = providers.gradleProperty("testSeed").getOrElse(System.nanoTime().toString())

tasks.withType<Test>().configureEach {
    useJUnitPlatform()
    maxParallelForks = half
    // Every check runs its tests anew and no old report stays; coverage pays by running them again.
    dependsOn("clean${name.replaceFirstChar(Char::uppercase)}")
    systemProperty("junit.jupiter.testclass.order.default", "org.junit.jupiter.api.ClassOrderer\$Random")
    systemProperty("junit.jupiter.testmethod.order.default", "org.junit.jupiter.api.MethodOrderer\$Random")
    systemProperty("junit.jupiter.execution.order.random.seed", testSeed)
    testLogging {
        exceptionFormat = TestExceptionFormat.FULL
    }
    doFirst {
        logger.lifecycle("Test order seed $testSeed: repeat it with -PtestSeed=$testSeed")
    }
}

pitest {
    pitestVersion = catalog.findVersion("pitest").get().requiredVersion
    junit5PluginVersion = catalog.findVersion("pitest-junit5").get().requiredVersion
    targetClasses = setOf("dev.metis.${project.name}.*")
    targetTests = setOf("dev.metis.${project.name}.*")
    mutators = setOf("STRONGER")
    threads = half
    outputFormats = setOf("XML", "HTML")
    timestampedReports = false
}
```

`core/src/test/java/dev/metis/core/ShutdownTest.java`:

```java
package dev.metis.core;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import static org.awaitility.Awaitility.await;

import java.net.URI;
import java.net.http.HttpClient;
import java.net.http.HttpRequest;
import java.net.http.HttpResponse;
import java.net.http.HttpResponse.BodyHandlers;
import java.time.Duration;
import java.util.concurrent.CompletableFuture;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.ExtendWith;
import org.springframework.boot.SpringApplication;
import org.springframework.boot.test.system.CapturedOutput;
import org.springframework.boot.test.system.OutputCaptureExtension;
import org.springframework.context.ConfigurableApplicationContext;

@ExtendWith(OutputCaptureExtension.class)
class ShutdownTest {

  @Test
  void aRequestInFlightFinishesWhenTheCoreStops(CapturedOutput output) throws Exception {
    ConfigurableApplicationContext context =
        SpringApplication.run(CoreApplication.class, "--server.port=0");
    TestEndpoints endpoints = context.getBean(TestEndpoints.class);
    int port = context.getEnvironment().getRequiredProperty("local.server.port", Integer.class);
    URI hold = URI.create("http://localhost:" + port + TestEndpoints.HOLD);
    try (HttpClient http = HttpClient.newHttpClient()) {
      CompletableFuture<HttpResponse<String>> answer =
          http.sendAsync(HttpRequest.newBuilder(hold).build(), BodyHandlers.ofString());
      endpoints.entered.await();
      Thread stopping = Thread.ofPlatform().start(context::close);
      await()
          .atMost(Duration.ofSeconds(10))
          .until(() -> output.getOut().contains("Commencing graceful shutdown"));
      endpoints.release.countDown();
      assertThat(answer.get().body()).isEqualTo(TestEndpoints.HELD);
      stopping.join();
    }
    assertThat(output.getOut()).contains("Graceful shutdown complete");
  }
}
```

`core/src/test/java/dev/metis/core/TestEndpoints.java`:

```java
package dev.metis.core;

import java.util.concurrent.CountDownLatch;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.GetMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RestController;

// The core has no endpoint of its own yet, so the tests of how it serves a request bring these.
@RestController
class TestEndpoints {

  static final String THREAD = "/test/thread";
  static final String HOLD = "/test/hold";
  static final String HELD = "held";

  final CountDownLatch entered = new CountDownLatch(1);
  final CountDownLatch release = new CountDownLatch(1);

  @GetMapping(THREAD)
  boolean servedOnAVirtualThread() {
    return Thread.currentThread().isVirtual();
  }

  @GetMapping(HOLD)
  String hold() throws InterruptedException {
    entered.countDown();
    release.await();
    return HELD;
  }
}
```

### Task 3: The tool, part one: processes and git

The project `tools` and the two edges of the tool to the machine: running a process, and asking git which files it would commit, their stamp and the commit. The stamp ports `treeOf` of the app's `verify.mjs`: a hash of the paths and contents of the files git lists, plus the count of uncommitted changes, or `unknown` when git cannot list the files.

```java
package dev.metis.tools;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThatThrownBy;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.io.UncheckedIOException;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.util.List;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.io.TempDir;

class ProcessesTest {

  @TempDir Path dir;

  @Test
  void runReturnsTheExitStatusAndBothStreamsInTheOrderTheyWereWritten() {
    Processes.Result result =
        Processes.run(dir, List.of("sh", "-c", "echo out; echo err >&2; exit 3"));
    assertThat(result).isEqualTo(new Processes.Result(3, "out\nerr\n"));
  }

  @Test
  void quietKeepsTheStandardOutputAloneAndAddsTheErrorsOnlyToAFailure() {
    Processes.Result success =
        Processes.quiet(dir, List.of("sh", "-c", "echo out; echo warning >&2"));
    assertThat(success).isEqualTo(new Processes.Result(0, "out\n"));
    Processes.Result failure =
        Processes.quiet(dir, List.of("sh", "-c", "echo out; echo fatal >&2; exit 3"));
    assertThat(failure).isEqualTo(new Processes.Result(3, "out\nfatal\n"));
    assertThat(Processes.quiet(dir, List.of("cat"))).isEqualTo(new Processes.Result(0, ""));
  }

  @Test
  void runStartsTheCommandInTheFolderItIsGiven() throws IOException {
    Files.writeString(dir.resolve("marker.txt"), "here\n");
    assertThat(Processes.run(dir, List.of("cat", "marker.txt")).output()).isEqualTo("here\n");
  }

  @Test
  void runGivesTheCommandNoInputSoACommandThatReadsItEndsAtOnce() {
    assertThat(Processes.run(dir, List.of("cat"))).isEqualTo(new Processes.Result(0, ""));
  }

  @Test
  void inheritReturnsTheExitStatusOfACommandWhoseOutputGoesToThisProcess() throws IOException {
    assertThat(Processes.inherit(dir, List.of("sh", "-c", "exit 4"))).isEqualTo(4);
    assertThat(Processes.inherit(dir, List.of("sh", "-c", "test -f marker.txt"))).isEqualTo(1);
    Files.writeString(dir.resolve("marker.txt"), "");
    assertThat(Processes.inherit(dir, List.of("sh", "-c", "test -f marker.txt"))).isZero();
  }

  @Test
  void aCommandThatCannotStartIsAnError() {
    assertThatThrownBy(() -> Processes.run(dir, List.of("no-such-command-anywhere")))
        .isInstanceOf(UncheckedIOException.class)
        .hasCauseInstanceOf(IOException.class);
    assertThatThrownBy(() -> Processes.quiet(dir, List.of("no-such-command-anywhere")))
        .isInstanceOf(UncheckedIOException.class)
        .hasCauseInstanceOf(IOException.class);
    assertThatThrownBy(() -> Processes.inherit(dir, List.of("no-such-command-anywhere")))
        .isInstanceOf(UncheckedIOException.class)
        .hasCauseInstanceOf(IOException.class);
  }

  @Test
  void anInterruptedWaitIsAnErrorAndKeepsTheInterrupt() {
    Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
    try {
      assertThatThrownBy(() -> Processes.inherit(dir, List.of("sleep", "2")))
          .isInstanceOf(UncheckedIOException.class)
          .hasMessageEndingWith("interrupted while sleep 2 ran");
      assertThat(Thread.currentThread().isInterrupted()).isTrue();
    } finally {
      Thread.interrupted();
    }
  }
}
```

`tools/src/test/java/dev/metis/tools/GitTest.java`:

```java
package dev.metis.tools;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.io.UncheckedIOException;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.function.Function;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.io.TempDir;

class GitTest {

  private static final List<String> LIST =
      List.of("ls-files", "-co", "--exclude-standard", "-z", "--", ".");
  private static final List<String> STATUS =
      List.of("--no-optional-locks", "status", "--porcelain", "--", ".");
  private static final String PINNED = "pinned/brand/tokens.css";

  @TempDir Path root;

  // A git stand-in that answers each command it knows with its result and fails the test otherwise.
  private static Function<List<String>, Processes.Result> answering(
      Map<List<String>, Processes.Result> answers) {
    return args -> {
      assertThat(answers).containsKey(args);
      return answers.get(args);
    };
  }

  private static Processes.Result ok(String output) {
    return new Processes.Result(0, output);
  }

  private static String listed(String... paths) {
    return String.join("\0", paths) + "\0";
  }

  private Git gitListing(String listing, String status) {
    return new Git(root, answering(Map.of(LIST, ok(listing), STATUS, ok(status))));
  }

  private void write(String path, String text) throws IOException {
    Files.createDirectories(root.resolve(path).getParent());
    Files.writeString(root.resolve(path), text);
  }

  @Test
  void theTreeHashesThePathAndBytesOfEachListedFileAndCountsTheChanges() throws IOException {
    write("a.txt", "a\n");
    write("src/b.txt", "b\n");
    write("notes.txt", "not listed\n");
    write(PINNED, ":root {}\n");
    String status = "?? a.txt\n M src/b.txt\n";
    String tree = gitListing(listed("src/b.txt", "a.txt", PINNED), status).tree();
    assertThat(tree).matches("[0-9a-f]{12} \\(2 uncommitted\\)");
    // Listing order, a path listed twice, a deleted file and unlisted files leave the hash alone.
    Git same = gitListing(listed("a.txt", PINNED, "src/b.txt", "a.txt", "gone.txt"), status);
    write("notes.txt", "edited\n");
    assertThat(same.tree()).isEqualTo(tree);
    for (String file : List.of("src/b.txt", PINNED)) {
      String before = Files.readString(root.resolve(file));
      write(file, "changed\n");
      assertThat(same.tree()).as(file).isNotEqualTo(tree);
      write(file, before);
    }
    assertThat(same.tree()).isEqualTo(tree);
  }

  @Test
  void aPathIsPartOfTheHashSoTheSameBytesUnderAnotherNameAreAnotherTree() throws IOException {
    write("a.txt", "x\n");
    write("b.txt", "x\n");
    assertThat(gitListing(listed("a.txt"), "").tree())
        .isNotEqualTo(gitListing(listed("b.txt"), "").tree());
  }

  @Test
  void theBytesOfOneFileCannotPassForTheNameOfTheNext() throws IOException {
    write("a.txt", "x");
    write("b.txt", "y");
    String two = gitListing(listed("a.txt", "b.txt"), "").tree();
    write("a.txt", "xb.txt\0y");
    assertThat(gitListing(listed("a.txt"), "").tree()).isNotEqualTo(two);
  }

  @Test
  void theTreeCountsEveryLineOfTheStatusAndNothingElse() throws IOException {
    write("a.txt", "a\n");
    String clean = gitListing(listed("a.txt"), "").tree();
    assertThat(clean).endsWith(" (0 uncommitted)");
    assertThat(gitListing(listed("a.txt"), " M a.txt\n").tree())
        .isEqualTo(clean.replace("(0", "(1"));
  }

  @Test
  void theFilesAreTheListedOnesThatExistInPathOrder() throws IOException {
    write("b.txt", "");
    write("a/c.txt", "");
    Files.createDirectories(root.resolve("folder"));
    Git git = gitListing(listed("b.txt", "gone.txt", "a/c.txt", "b.txt", "folder"), "");
    assertThat(git.files()).contains(List.of("a/c.txt", "b.txt"));
  }

  @Test
  void whereGitCannotListTheFilesTheTreeIsUnknownAndThereAreNoFiles() throws IOException {
    write("a.txt", "a\n");
    Processes.Result failed = new Processes.Result(128, "fatal: not a git repository");
    List<Git> lost =
        List.of(
            new Git(root, answering(Map.of(LIST, failed, STATUS, ok("")))),
            new Git(root, answering(Map.of(LIST, ok(listed("a.txt")), STATUS, failed))),
            new Git(
                root,
                args -> {
                  throw new UncheckedIOException(new IOException("git: not found"));
                }));
    for (Git git : lost) {
      assertThat(git.tree()).isEqualTo(Git.UNKNOWN);
    }
    assertThat(lost.getFirst().files()).isEmpty();
    assertThat(lost.getLast().files()).isEmpty();
  }

  @Test
  void aListedFileThatCannotBeReadMakesTheTreeUnknown() throws IOException {
    write("a.txt", "a\n");
    Git git = gitListing(listed("a.txt"), "");
    assertThat(root.resolve("a.txt").toFile().setReadable(false)).isTrue();
    try {
      assertThat(git.tree()).isEqualTo(Git.UNKNOWN);
    } finally {
      assertThat(root.resolve("a.txt").toFile().setReadable(true)).isTrue();
    }
  }

  @Test
  void theCommitIsHeadOrNoneBeforeTheFirstCommit() {
    List<String> head = List.of("rev-parse", "HEAD");
    assertThat(new Git(root, answering(Map.of(head, ok("abc123\n")))).commit()).isEqualTo("abc123");
    Processes.Result none = new Processes.Result(128, "fatal: ambiguous argument 'HEAD'");
    assertThat(new Git(root, answering(Map.of(head, none))).commit()).isEqualTo("none");
  }

  @Test
  void withTheRealGitTheTreeNamesTheFilesItWouldCommit() throws IOException {
    List<List<String>> asked = new ArrayList<>();
    Git git =
        new Git(
            root,
            args -> {
              asked.add(args);
              List<String> command = new ArrayList<>(List.of("git"));
              command.addAll(args);
              return Processes.run(root, command);
            });
    assertThat(git.tree()).isEqualTo(Git.UNKNOWN);
    assertThat(Processes.run(root, List.of("git", "init", "-q")).status()).isZero();
    write(".gitignore", "build/\n");
    write("a.txt", "a\n");
    write("build/out.txt", "ignored\n");
    assertThat(git.files()).contains(List.of(".gitignore", "a.txt"));
    assertThat(git.tree()).matches("[0-9a-f]{12} \\(2 uncommitted\\)");
    assertThat(git.commit()).isEqualTo("none");
    assertThat(asked).contains(LIST, STATUS, List.of("rev-parse", "HEAD"));
  }
}
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.io.UncheckedIOException;
import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.concurrent.CompletableFuture;
import java.util.stream.Collectors;

/** Runs a command in a folder and waits for it to end; a command that cannot run is an error. */
public final class Processes {

  private Processes() {}

  /** The exit status of a command and everything it wrote, both streams in one text. */
  public record Result(int status, String output) {}

  /** Runs the command with its output captured. */
  public static Result run(Path dir, List<String> command) {
    return capture(new ProcessBuilder(command).redirectErrorStream(true), dir, command);
  }

  /** Runs the command for a reader of what it prints: its errors are kept for a failure alone. */
  public static Result quiet(Path dir, List<String> command) {
    try {
      Process process = new ProcessBuilder(command).directory(dir.toFile()).start();
      process.getOutputStream().close();
      // Read apart, so a command that fills one stream never waits for the other to be read.
      CompletableFuture<String> errors =
          CompletableFuture.supplyAsync(
              () ->
                  process
                      .errorReader(StandardCharsets.UTF_8)
                      .lines()
                      .map(line -> line + "\n")
                      .collect(Collectors.joining()));
      String output = new String(process.getInputStream().readAllBytes(), StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
      int status = waitFor(process, command);
      return new Result(status, status == 0 ? output : output + errors.join());
    } catch (IOException failed) {
      throw new UncheckedIOException(failed);
    }
  }

  private static Result capture(ProcessBuilder builder, Path dir, List<String> command) {
    try {
      Process process = builder.directory(dir.toFile()).start();
      process.getOutputStream().close();
      String output = new String(process.getInputStream().readAllBytes(), StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
      return new Result(waitFor(process, command), output);
    } catch (IOException failed) {
      throw new UncheckedIOException(failed);
    }
  }

  /** Runs the command with its output going where the output of this process goes. */
  public static int inherit(Path dir, List<String> command) {
    try {
      return waitFor(
          new ProcessBuilder(command).directory(dir.toFile()).inheritIO().start(), command);
    } catch (IOException failed) {
      throw new UncheckedIOException(failed);
    }
  }

  private static int waitFor(Process process, List<String> command) throws IOException {
    try {
      return process.waitFor();
    } catch (InterruptedException interrupted) {
      Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
      throw new IOException("interrupted while " + String.join(" ", command) + " ran", interrupted);
    }
  }
}
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.io.UncheckedIOException;
import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.security.MessageDigest;
import java.security.NoSuchAlgorithmException;
import java.util.Arrays;
import java.util.HexFormat;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Optional;
import java.util.TreeSet;
import java.util.function.Function;

/** What git says about a repository: the files it would commit, their stamp and the commit. */
public final class Git {

  /** The tree of a row whose files git could not list, which a full run of ./verify refuses. */
  public static final String UNKNOWN = "unknown (git could not list the files)";

  private static final List<String> LIST =
      List.of("ls-files", "-co", "--exclude-standard", "-z", "--", ".");
  private static final List<String> STATUS =
      List.of("--no-optional-locks", "status", "--porcelain", "--", ".");

  private final Path root;
  private final Function<List<String>, Processes.Result> git;

  /** A view of the repository at root, where git runs a git command given its arguments. */
  public Git(Path root, Function<List<String>, Processes.Result> git) {
    this.root = root;
    this.git = git;
  }

  /** The files git would commit that exist, in path order; empty when git cannot list them. */
  public Optional<List<String>> files() {
    return quietly(LIST)
        .map(
            listed ->
                new TreeSet<>(Arrays.asList(listed.output().split("\0")))
                    .stream().filter(path -> Files.isRegularFile(root.resolve(path))).toList());
  }

  /** A hash of the paths and bytes of the files git would commit, and the count of changes. */
  public String tree() {
    Optional<List<String>> files = files();
    Optional<Processes.Result> status = quietly(STATUS);
    if (files.isEmpty() || status.isEmpty()) {
      return UNKNOWN;
    }
    try {
      MessageDigest digest = MessageDigest.getInstance("SHA-256");
      for (String file : files.get()) {
        digest.update((file + "\0").getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
        digest.update(Files.readAllBytes(root.resolve(file)));
        digest.update((byte) 0);
      }
      String hash = HexFormat.of().formatHex(digest.digest()).substring(0, 12);
      return hash + " (" + status.get().output().lines().count() + " uncommitted)";
    } catch (IOException | NoSuchAlgorithmException unreadable) {
      return UNKNOWN;
    }
  }

  /** The commit git stands on, or none before the first commit. */
  public String commit() {
    return quietly(List.of("rev-parse", "HEAD")).map(head -> head.output().strip()).orElse("none");
  }

  private Optional<Processes.Result> quietly(List<String> args) {
    try {
      return Optional.of(git.apply(args)).filter(result -> result.status() == 0);
    } catch (UncheckedIOException missing) {
      return Optional.empty();
    }
  }
}
```

The tool keeps the list of the checks of the spec, in its order, as `Checks.ORDER`, and learns from Gradle which of them the build has: the launcher of Task 6 writes the tasks named `check` and a capital that Gradle has in every project into `tools/build/launcher/checks`, however a build file declares them, and a check task the list lacks stops the run, in whatever project it is registered; the two tasks of the licence report plugin, which `checkDeps` runs, are no checks of their own. package dev.metis.tools.verify;

```java
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThatThrownBy;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.util.List;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.io.TempDir;

class ChecksTest {

  @TempDir Path root;

  @Test
  void theChecksAreTheChecksOfTheListGradleHasInTheOrderOfTheList() {
    assertThat(Checks.of(List.of("checkUnit", "checkFormat", "checkCompile")))
        .containsExactly("format", "compile", "unit");
    assertThat(Checks.of(List.of())).isEmpty();
  }

  @Test
  void aCheckTaskTheListLacksIsAnErrorWhateverWayAndInWhateverProjectItWasDeclared() {
    assertThatThrownBy(() -> Checks.of(List.of("checkFormat", "checkTyped", ":core:checkOther")))
        .isInstanceOf(IllegalArgumentException.class)
        .hasMessage(
            "Gradle has check tasks that Checks.ORDER does not list: checkTyped, :core:checkOther");
  }

  @Test
  void aTaskOfAPluginThatACheckRunsIsNoCheckOfItsOwn() {
    assertThat(
            Checks.of(List.of(":core:checkLicense", ":core:checkLicensePreparation", "checkDeps")))
        .containsExactly("deps");
  }

  @Test
  void theFastGroupIsTheFirstTenChecksOfTheSpecWhichEndAtUnit() {
    assertThat(Checks.FAST)
        .containsExactlyInAnyOrder(
            "format",
            "compile",
            "lint",
            "language",
            "architecture",
            "deadcode",
            "tooling",
            "contract",
            "trace",
            "unit");
    assertThat(Checks.ORDER).startsWith("format").contains("integration", "coverage", "image");
  }

  @Test
  void theTasksAreTheLinesTheLauncherWroteAndAMissingFileSaysWhoWritesIt() throws IOException {
    assertThatThrownBy(() -> Checks.tasks(root))
        .isInstanceOf(IOException.class)
        .hasMessage(
            "no list of the checks in tools/build/launcher/checks: run ./verify, whose launcher"
                + " writes it");
    Files.createDirectories(root.resolve("tools/build/launcher"));
    Files.writeString(root.resolve(Checks.TASKS), "checkFormat\n\ncheckUnit\n");
    assertThat(Checks.tasks(root)).containsExactly("checkFormat", "checkUnit");
  }

  @Test
  void aCheckRunsAsItsGradleTask() {
    assertThat(Checks.task("format")).isEqualTo("checkFormat");
    assertThat(Checks.task("deadcode")).isEqualTo("checkDeadcode");
  }

  @Test
  void aCheckRunsThroughTheWrapperAtLowPriorityOnPartOfTheCoresAndGoesOnAfterAFailure() {
    Path repo = Path.of("/repo");
    assertThat(Checks.command(repo, "unit", 5, List.of()))
        .containsExactly(
            "/repo/gradlew",
            "--continue",
            "--console=plain",
            "--priority=low",
            "--max-workers=5",
            "checkUnit");
    assertThat(Checks.command(repo, "mutation", 2, List.of("-Pmutate=a.B")))
        .endsWith("--max-workers=2", "checkMutation", "-Pmutate=a.B");
  }
}
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools.verify;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThatThrownBy;

import java.util.List;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

class PlanTest {

  private static final List<String> ALL =
      List.of("format", "lint", "unit", "integration", "coverage", "image");

  @Test
  void withoutOptionsEveryCheckRunsAndTheRecordStartsAgain() {
    assertThat(Plan.of(List.of(), ALL)).isEqualTo(new Plan(ALL, false, true));
  }

  @Test
  void onlyRunsTheNamedChecksInTheOrderOfTheBuildAndAppendExtendsTheRecord() {
    assertThat(Plan.of(List.of("--only", "unit,format", "--append"), ALL))
        .isEqualTo(new Plan(List.of("format", "unit"), true, false));
    assertThat(Plan.of(List.of("--only=lint"), ALL))
        .isEqualTo(new Plan(List.of("lint"), false, false));
    assertThat(Plan.of(List.of("--append"), ALL)).isEqualTo(new Plan(ALL, true, true));
  }

  @Test
  void onlyEveryCheckIsAFullRun() {
    assertThat(
            Plan.of(List.of("--only", "image,coverage,integration,unit,lint,format"), ALL).full())
        .isTrue();
  }

  @Test
  void fastRunsTheFastGroupOfTheSpecSoAContainerCheckAfterUnitIsLeftOut() {
    assertThat(Plan.of(List.of("--fast"), ALL))
        .isEqualTo(new Plan(List.of("format", "lint", "unit"), false, false));
    List<String> noCoverage = List.of("format", "lint");
    assertThat(Plan.of(List.of("--fast"), noCoverage)).isEqualTo(new Plan(noCoverage, false, true));
    List<String> coverageFirst = List.of("coverage", "image");
    assertThat(Plan.of(List.of("--fast"), coverageFirst))
        .isEqualTo(new Plan(List.of(), false, false));
  }

  @Test
  void anUnknownCheckOrOptionStopsTheRunBeforeAnyCheckRuns() {
    assertThatThrownBy(() -> Plan.of(List.of("--only", "lint,unti"), ALL))
        .isInstanceOf(IllegalArgumentException.class)
        .hasMessage("no such check: unti");
    assertThatThrownBy(() -> Plan.of(List.of("--every"), ALL))
        .isInstanceOf(IllegalArgumentException.class)
        .hasMessage("unknown option: --every");
    assertThatThrownBy(() -> Plan.of(List.of("--only"), ALL))
        .isInstanceOf(IllegalArgumentException.class)
        .hasMessage("--only needs a list of checks");
    assertThatThrownBy(() -> Plan.of(List.of("--fast", "--only", "lint"), ALL))
        .isInstanceOf(IllegalArgumentException.class)
        .hasMessage("--fast and --only exclude each other");
  }
}
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools.verify;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.NoSuchFileException;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Set;

/** The checks of the spec, of which a check runs when Gradle has its task. */
public final class Checks {

  /** Every check of the spec, in the order ./verify runs them. */
  public static final List<String> ORDER =
      List.of(
          "format",
          "compile",
          "lint",
          "language",
          "architecture",
          "deadcode",
          "tooling",
          "contract",
          "trace",
          "unit",
          "integration",
          "coverage",
          "mutation",
          "deps",
          "secrets",
          "image");

  /** The fast group of the spec, which CI runs on every push. */
  static final Set<String> FAST =
      Set.of(
          "format",
          "compile",
          "lint",
          "language",
          "architecture",
          "deadcode",
          "tooling",
          "contract",
          "trace",
          "unit");

  // The licence report plugin names its tasks so; checkDeps runs them.
  private static final Set<String> OWNED =
      Set.of(":core:checkLicense", ":core:checkLicensePreparation");

  /** Where the launcher writes the tasks named check and a capital of every project. */
  public static final String TASKS = "tools/build/launcher/checks";

  private Checks() {}

  /** The check tasks Gradle has, as the launcher wrote them before the tool started. */
  public static List<String> tasks(Path root) throws IOException {
    try {
      return Files.readAllLines(root.resolve(TASKS)).stream()
          .filter(line -> !line.isBlank())
          .toList();
    } catch (NoSuchFileException missing) {
      throw new IOException(
          "no list of the checks in " + TASKS + ": run ./verify, whose launcher writes it",
          missing);
    }
  }

  /**
   * The checks whose tasks Gradle has, in the order of the list; any other check task is an error.
   */
  public static List<String> of(List<String> tasks) {
    List<String> listed = ORDER.stream().map(Checks::task).toList();
    List<String> unknown =
        tasks.stream().filter(task -> !listed.contains(task) && !OWNED.contains(task)).toList();
    if (!unknown.isEmpty()) {
      throw new IllegalArgumentException(
          "Gradle has check tasks that Checks.ORDER does not list: " + String.join(", ", unknown));
    }
    return ORDER.stream().filter(check -> tasks.contains(task(check))).toList();
  }

  /** The Gradle task of a check. */
  public static String task(String check) {
    return "check" + Character.toUpperCase(check.charAt(0)) + check.substring(1);
  }

  /** The command that runs a check of the tree at root, which goes on after a failed task. */
  public static List<String> command(Path root, String check, int workers, List<String> args) {
    List<String> command = new ArrayList<>();
    command.add(root.resolve("gradlew").toString());
    command.add("--continue");
    command.add("--console=plain");
    // Low priority starts a daemon of its own, so no check runs in a daemon of normal priority.
    command.add("--priority=low");
    command.add("--max-workers=" + workers);
    command.add(task(check));
    command.addAll(args);
    return command;
  }
}
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools.verify;

import java.util.Arrays;
import java.util.Iterator;
import java.util.List;
import org.jspecify.annotations.Nullable;

/** Which checks a run of ./verify runs, and whether it adds its rows to the record. */
public record Plan(List<String> checks, boolean append, boolean full) {

  private static final String ONLY = "--only";

  /** The plan the command line asks for, given every check in the order of the build. */
  public static Plan of(List<String> args, List<String> all) {
    boolean append = false;
    boolean fast = false;
    @Nullable String only = null;
    for (Iterator<String> next = args.iterator(); next.hasNext(); ) {
      String arg = next.next();
      switch (arg) {
        case "--append" -> append = true;
        case "--fast" -> fast = true;
        case ONLY -> only = listAfter(next);
        default -> only = valueOf(arg);
      }
    }
    if (fast && only != null) {
      throw new IllegalArgumentException("--fast and --only exclude each other");
    }
    List<String> checks = fast ? fastOf(all) : only == null ? all : named(only, all);
    return new Plan(checks, append, checks.equals(all));
  }

  private static String listAfter(Iterator<String> next) {
    if (!next.hasNext()) {
      throw new IllegalArgumentException(ONLY + " needs a list of checks");
    }
    return next.next();
  }

  private static String valueOf(String arg) {
    if (!arg.startsWith(ONLY + "=")) {
      throw new IllegalArgumentException("unknown option: " + arg);
    }
    return arg.substring(ONLY.length() + 1);
  }

  private static List<String> fastOf(List<String> all) {
    return all.stream().filter(Checks.FAST::contains).toList();
  }

  private static List<String> named(String only, List<String> all) {
    List<String> names = Arrays.asList(only.split(","));
    List<String> unknown = names.stream().filter(name -> !all.contains(name)).toList();
    if (!unknown.isEmpty()) {
      throw new IllegalArgumentException("no such check: " + String.join(", ", unknown));
    }
    return all.stream().filter(names::contains).toList();
  }
}
```

### Task 5: The tool, part three: the record of a run

A check leaves its facts (counts, measures) in `build/facts/<check>.txt`; the record holds one row per check with its result, seconds, facts, tree and time, in `reports/verify.json`, and the page `reports/verify.md` is rendered from the JSON alone, so no hand-written passage survives a run. The record is read back only in the exact shape the tool writes, and `--append` keeps the earlier rows as reruns.

- [ ] **Step 2: Write the lock files and the checksums again**

A configuration in strict mode resolves only against its lock state, and an artifact only against its checksum, so a change of the dependencies writes both again. `--rerun-tasks` runs every task for real: a task restored from the build cache resolves nothing, and its artifacts would miss their checksums.

```sh
./gradlew --console=plain --max-workers=5 --refresh-dependencies --write-locks --write-verification-metadata sha256 --rerun-tasks help
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.io.TempDir;

class FactsTest {

  @TempDir Path root;

  @Test
  void aCheckLeavesItsFactsInTheBuildFolderAndTheyReadBackOnce() throws IOException {
    Facts.write(root, "unit", "12 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped");
    assertThat(root.resolve("build/facts/unit.txt")).hasContent("12 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped");
    assertThat(Files.readString(root.resolve("build/facts/unit.txt"))).endsWith("skipped\n");
    assertThat(Facts.read(root, "unit")).contains("12 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped");
    assertThat(Facts.read(root, "coverage")).isEmpty();
    Facts.clear(root, "unit");
    Facts.clear(root, "coverage");
    assertThat(Facts.read(root, "unit")).isEmpty();
  }

  @Test
  void factsThatCouldBreakOutOfATableCellAreNoFacts() throws IOException {
    for (String text : new String[] {"a | b", "a\nb", "a\rb"}) {
      Files.createDirectories(root.resolve("build/facts"));
      Files.writeString(root.resolve("build/facts/unit.txt"), text + "\n");
      assertThat(Facts.read(root, "unit")).as(text).isEmpty();
    }
  }

  @Test
  void safeTextHoldsNoLineBreakAndNoBar() {
    assertThat(Facts.safe("abc (1 uncommitted)")).isTrue();
    assertThat(Facts.safe("")).isTrue();
    assertThat(Facts.safe("a|b")).isFalse();
    assertThat(Facts.safe("a\nb")).isFalse();
    assertThat(Facts.safe("a\rb")).isFalse();
  }
}
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools.verify;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

import java.util.List;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

class LedgerTest {

  private static final List<String> ALL = List.of("format", "lint", "unit", "mutation");
  private static final Row GREEN =
      new Row("format", "green", 2.04, "", "abc (1 uncommitted)", "T1");
  private static final Row RED =
      new Row("unit", "RED", 0.5, "3 passed, 1 failed, 0 skipped", "abc (1 uncommitted)", "T2");
  private static final Ledger LEDGER = new Ledger("none", List.of(GREEN, RED), List.of());

  @Test
  void aLedgerReadsBackAsItWasWritten() {
    String text = Ledger.write(LEDGER);
    assertThat(text).startsWith("{\n").endsWith("}\n").contains("\"seconds\" : 2.04");
    assertThat(Ledger.read(text, ALL)).contains(LEDGER);
    Ledger reruns = new Ledger("abc123", List.of(GREEN), List.of(RED, GREEN));
    assertThat(Ledger.read(Ledger.write(reruns), ALL)).contains(reruns);
  }

  @Test
  void aLedgerIsReadBackOnlyInTheShapeThisToolWritesWithSafeTextAndKnownChecks() {
    String row =
        """
        {"check": "format", "result": "green", "seconds": 1, "facts": "", "tree": "t", "at": "T"}""";
    String good = "{\"commit\": \"none\", \"rows\": [" + row + "], \"reruns\": []}";
    assertThat(Ledger.read(good, ALL)).isPresent();
    List<String> forged =
        List.of(
            "",
            "{",
            "[]",
            good.replace("\"none\"", "1"),
            good.replace("\"none\"", "\"abc\\n## Signed off\""),
            good.replace(", \"reruns\": []", ""),
            good.replace("\"reruns\": []", "\"reruns\": {}"),
            good.replace("\"rows\": [" + row + "]", "\"rows\": []"),
            good.replace("\"rows\": [" + row + "]", "\"rows\": {}"),
            good.replace("\"rows\": [" + row + "]", "\"rows\": [1]"),
            good.replace("\"check\": \"format\"", "\"check\": \"forged\""),
            good.replace("\"check\": \"format\"", "\"check\": 1"),
            good.replace("\"result\": \"green\"", "\"result\": \"passed\""),
            good.replace("\"result\": \"green\"", "\"result\": true"),
            good.replace("\"seconds\": 1", "\"seconds\": \"1.0\""),
            good.replace("\"facts\": \"\"", "\"facts\": \"ok | x\""),
            good.replace("\"facts\": \"\"", "\"facts\": 1"),
            good.replace("\"tree\": \"t\"", "\"tree\": \"a\\nb\""),
            good.replace("\"at\": \"T\"", "\"at\": \"T\\r\""),
            good.replace(", \"at\": \"T\"", ""));
    for (String text : forged) {
      assertThat(Ledger.read(text, ALL)).as(text).isEmpty();
    }
    String rerun = good.replace("\"reruns\": []", "\"reruns\": [" + row + "]");
    assertThat(Ledger.read(rerun, ALL)).isPresent();
    assertThat(
            Ledger.read(
                rerun.replace(
                    "\"reruns\": [{\"check\": \"format\"", "\"reruns\": [{\"check\": \"x\""),
                ALL))
        .isEmpty();
  }
}
```

```java
  }
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.util.Optional;

/** The counts a check leaves for the record of ./verify, one line in the build folder. */
public final class Facts {

  private Facts() {}

  /** Text for a cell or a header line of the report: no line break and no bar. */
  public static boolean safe(String text) {
    return text.chars().noneMatch(c -> c == '|' || c == '\n' || c == '\r');
  }

  /** Leaves the facts of a check. */
  public static void write(Path root, String check, String text) throws IOException {
    Path file = fileOf(root, check);
    Files.createDirectories(file.getParent());
    Files.writeString(file, text + "\n");
  }

  /** The facts a check left, if it left any that a table cell can hold. */
  public static Optional<String> read(Path root, String check) throws IOException {
    Path file = fileOf(root, check);
    return Files.exists(file)
        ? Optional.of(Files.readString(file).strip()).filter(Facts::safe)
        : Optional.empty();
  }

  /** Removes the facts of an earlier run, so that they never speak for this one. */
  public static void clear(Path root, String check) throws IOException {
    Files.deleteIfExists(fileOf(root, check));
  }

  private static Path fileOf(Path root, String check) {
    return root.resolve("build/facts").resolve(check + ".txt");
  }
}
```

```java
/** One check of one run: its result, its seconds, its facts and the tree it ran on. */
public record Row(
    String check, String result, double seconds, String facts, String tree, String at) {

  /** The result of a check that exited 0 and left the facts it owes. */
  public static final String GREEN = "green";

  /** The result of any other check. */
  public static final String RED = "RED";
```

`tools/src/main/java/dev/metis/tools/verify/Ledger.java`:

```java
package dev.metis.tools.verify;

import dev.metis.tools.Facts;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Optional;
import tools.jackson.core.JacksonException;
import tools.jackson.databind.JsonNode;
import tools.jackson.databind.json.JsonMapper;
import tools.jackson.databind.node.ArrayNode;
import tools.jackson.databind.node.ObjectNode;

/** The record of ./verify: the commit, the rows of the last full or fresh run, and the reruns. */
public record Ledger(String commit, List<Row> rows, List<Row> reruns) {

  private static final JsonMapper JSON = JsonMapper.builder().build();

  /** The same ledger with more reruns after the ones it holds. */
  public Ledger withReruns(List<Row> more) {
    List<Row> all = new ArrayList<>(reruns);
    all.addAll(more);
    return new Ledger(commit, rows, all);
  }

  /** The ledger as reports/verify.json holds it. */
  public static String write(Ledger ledger) {
    ObjectNode root = JSON.createObjectNode().put("commit", ledger.commit());
    root.set("rows", arrayOf(ledger.rows()));
    root.set("reruns", arrayOf(ledger.reruns()));
    return JSON.writerWithDefaultPrettyPrinter().writeValueAsString(root) + "\n";
  }

  private static ArrayNode arrayOf(List<Row> rows) {
    ArrayNode array = JSON.createArrayNode();
    for (Row row : rows) {
      array
          .addObject()
          .put("check", row.check())
          .put("result", row.result())
          .put("seconds", row.seconds())
          .put("facts", row.facts())
          .put("tree", row.tree())
          .put("at", row.at());
    }
    return array;
  }

  /** The ledger in the text, if the text has exactly the shape write gives, with known checks. */
  public static Optional<Ledger> read(String text, List<String> checks) {
    try {
      JsonNode root = JSON.readTree(text);
      List<Row> rows = rowsOf(root.path("rows"), checks);
      List<Row> reruns = rowsOf(root.path("reruns"), checks);
      return rows.isEmpty()
          ? Optional.empty()
          : Optional.of(new Ledger(text(root, "commit"), rows, reruns));
    } catch (JacksonException | IllegalArgumentException forged) {
      return Optional.empty();
    }
  }

  private static List<Row> rowsOf(JsonNode list, List<String> checks) {
    if (!list.isArray()) {
      throw new IllegalArgumentException("not a list of rows");
    }
    List<Row> rows = new ArrayList<>();
    for (JsonNode row : list) {
      rows.add(rowOf(row, checks));
    }
    return rows;
  }

  private static Row rowOf(JsonNode row, List<String> checks) {
    String check = text(row, "check");
    String result = text(row, "result");
    if (!checks.contains(check) || !List.of(Row.GREEN, Row.RED).contains(result)) {
      throw new IllegalArgumentException("not a row of a known check");
    }
    // A value that is not a number throws, as a text that is not a string does below.
    double seconds = row.path("seconds").doubleValue();
    return new Row(check, result, seconds, text(row, "facts"), text(row, "tree"), text(row, "at"));
  }

  private static String text(JsonNode node, String field) {
    String text = node.path(field).stringValue();
    if (!Facts.safe(text)) {
      throw new IllegalArgumentException(field + " is not safe text");
    }
    return text;
  }
}
```

`tools/src/main/java/dev/metis/tools/verify/Report.java`:

```java
package dev.metis.tools.verify;

import dev.metis.tools.Git;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Locale;
import java.util.Set;
import java.util.stream.Collectors;
import java.util.stream.Stream;

/** The report reports/verify.md, drawn from the ledger on every run, so no edit of it survives. */
public final class Report {

  /** Why a row on an unknown tree proves nothing about the code. */
  public static final String UNBOUND =
      "git could not list the files of some rows, so they name no tree: run ./verify in a git"
          + " work tree (a copy needs git init -q at its root)";

  private static final String HEAD =
      "| Check | Result | Seconds | Facts | Tree |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n";

  private Report() {}

  /** The report of the ledger, given every check of the build in its order. */
  public static String of(Ledger ledger, List<String> checks) {
    List<Row> every = Stream.concat(ledger.rows().stream(), ledger.reruns().stream()).toList();
    Set<String> trees = every.stream().map(Row::tree).collect(Collectors.toSet());
    // A row on an unknown tree may stand on any tree, so whether the rows share one is unknown.
    boolean unknown = trees.contains(Git.UNKNOWN);
    String one = unknown ? "unknown" : trees.size() == 1 ? "yes" : "no";
    List<String> left = new ArrayList<>(checks);
    every.forEach(row -> left.remove(row.check()));
    StringBuilder text = new StringBuilder("# ./verify\n\n");
    text.append("Commit: ").append(ledger.commit()).append('\n');
    text.append("Tree: ").append(ledger.rows().getFirst().tree()).append('\n');
    text.append("All rows on one tree: ").append(one).append('\n');
    text.append("Not run: ").append(left.isEmpty() ? "none" : String.join(", ", left));
    text.append("\n\n").append(unknown ? "Warning: " + UNBOUND + "\n\n" : "");
    text.append(tableOf(ledger.rows()));
    if (!ledger.reruns().isEmpty()) {
      text.append("\n## Reruns\n\n").append(tableOf(ledger.reruns()));
    }
    return text.toString();
  }

  private static String tableOf(List<Row> rows) {
    StringBuilder table = new StringBuilder(HEAD);
    for (Row row : rows) {
      String seconds = String.format(Locale.ROOT, "%.1f", row.seconds());
      String facts = row.facts().isEmpty() ? "-" : row.facts();
      table.append(
          "| %s | %s | %s | %s | %s |\n"
              .formatted(row.check(), row.result(), seconds, facts, row.tree()));
    }
    return table.toString();
  }
}
```

Add the files the list above names, the generated ones included, to the ledger of the run. Never run git add, git commit or git push: the owner commits.

### Task 6: The tool, part four: the verify command and its launcher

The command `verify` runs each check of the plan through the wrapper with `--continue`, at low priority and with half the cores as workers, goes on after a red check, and writes the record. A full run on a tree git cannot list exits 1. The edges to the machine (processes, the clock, the output) reach the commands through one `Context` record of JDK functional types, so a test gives each edge or fails on it. `./verify` runs the Gradle task `launcher`, which writes the Java, the classpath and the check tasks Gradle has, and starts the tool at nice 19, which every child inherits. Git is read from its standard output alone, through `Processes.quiet`, so a warning never reads as a file or a change, while a failure keeps the reason git gives on its standard error.

- Produces: `Context`: `public record Context(Path root, PrintStream out, BiFunction<Path, List<String>, Processes.Result> run, BiFunction<Path, List<String>, Processes.Result> quiet, ToIntBiFunction<Path, List<String>> inherit, LongSupplier nanos, Supplier<Instant> now, int workers)`; `public Git git()`. `Command`: `int run(Context context, List<String> args) throws IOException`. `Cli`: `public final class Cli`; `public static int run(Context context, List<String> args) throws IOException`. `Main`: `public final class Main`; `public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException`. `Verify`: `public final class Verify`; `public static int command(Context context, List<String> args) throws IOException`.
```java
package dev.metis.tools;

import java.io.ByteArrayOutputStream;
import java.io.PrintStream;
import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.time.Instant;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.function.BiFunction;
import java.util.function.ToIntBiFunction;

/** A context for the tests of a command: its output is kept, and an edge not given fails. */
public final class TestContext {

  /** The time of the first stamp; each stamp is a second later than the one before. */
  public static final Instant START = Instant.parse("2026-10-14T00:00:00Z");

  private final ByteArrayOutputStream printed = new ByteArrayOutputStream();
  private final Path root;
  private BiFunction<Path, List<String>, Processes.Result> run = TestContext::unexpected;
  private ToIntBiFunction<Path, List<String>> inherit =
      (dir, command) -> unexpected(dir, command).status();
  private long nanos;
  private long stamps;

  public TestContext(Path root) {
    this.root = root;
  }

  private static Processes.Result unexpected(Path dir, List<String> command) {
    throw new AssertionError("unexpected command in " + dir + ": " + command);
  }

  public TestContext run(BiFunction<Path, List<String>, Processes.Result> run) {
    this.run = run;
    return this;
  }

  public TestContext inherit(ToIntBiFunction<Path, List<String>> inherit) {
    this.inherit = inherit;
    return this;
  }

  /** The context, whose clock moves 1.5 seconds on each read. */
  public Context context() {
    return new Context(
        root,
        new PrintStream(printed, true, StandardCharsets.UTF_8),
        run,
        run,
        inherit,
        () -> nanos += 1_500_000_000L,
        () -> START.plusSeconds(stamps++),
        3);
  }

  /** What the command printed. */
  public String printed() {
    return printed.toString(StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
  }
}
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

import dev.metis.tools.verify.Report;
import java.io.IOException;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.nio.file.attribute.PosixFilePermissions;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.io.TempDir;

// The process entry point sits outside coverage, so it runs here for real, in a JVM of its own.
class MainTest {

  // A wrapper stand-in that logs its arguments and fails the format check.
  private static final String GRADLEW =
      """
      #!/bin/sh
      echo "$@" >> gradlew.log
      case "$*" in *checkFormat*) exit 1 ;; esac
      exit 0
      """;

  @TempDir Path root;

  private Processes.Result tool(String... args) {
    List<String> command = new ArrayList<>();
    command.add(ProcessHandle.current().info().command().orElseThrow());
    command.add("-cp");
    command.add(System.getProperty("java.class.path"));
    command.add(Main.class.getName());
    command.addAll(List.of(args));
    return Processes.run(root, command);
  }

  private void repository(boolean git) throws IOException {
    Files.createDirectories(root.resolve("tools/build/launcher"));
    Files.writeString(root.resolve("tools/build/launcher/checks"), "checkFormat\ncheckUnit\n");
    Files.writeString(root.resolve(".gitignore"), "reports/\nbuild/\ngradlew.log\n");
    Files.writeString(root.resolve("gradlew"), GRADLEW);
    Files.setPosixFilePermissions(
        root.resolve("gradlew"), PosixFilePermissions.fromString("rwxr-xr-x"));
    if (git) {
      assertThat(Processes.run(root, List.of("git", "init", "-q")).status()).isZero();
    }
  }

  @Test
  void verifyRunsEachCheckThroughTheWrapperOfTheFolderItStartsInAndExitsAsTheChecksDo()
      throws IOException {
    repository(true);
    Processes.Result full = tool("verify");
    assertThat(full.status()).isEqualTo(1);
    String report = Files.readString(root.resolve("reports/verify.md"));
    assertThat(report)
        .contains("| format | RED |", "| unit | green |", "\nAll rows on one tree: yes\n");
    assertThat(full.output()).contains(report);
    int workers = Math.max(1, Runtime.getRuntime().availableProcessors() / 2);
    assertThat(Files.readAllLines(root.resolve("gradlew.log")))
        .containsExactly(
            "--continue --console=plain --priority=low --max-workers=" + workers + " checkFormat",
            "--continue --console=plain --priority=low --max-workers=" + workers + " checkUnit");
    assertThat(tool("verify", "--only", "unit", "--append").status()).isZero();
    assertThat(Files.readString(root.resolve("reports/verify.md"))).contains("## Reruns");
  }

  @Test
  void aFullRunOutsideAGitWorkTreeExitsOneAndAnUnknownCommandExitsTwo() throws IOException {
    repository(false);
    Processes.Result lost = tool("verify", "--only", "format,unit");
    assertThat(lost.status()).isEqualTo(1);
    assertThat(lost.output()).endsWith("verify: " + Report.UNBOUND + "\n");
    assertThat(tool("nope").status()).isEqualTo(2);
  }
}
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools.verify;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import static org.assertj.core.groups.Tuple.tuple;

import dev.metis.tools.Facts;

import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.io.TempDir;

class VerifyTest {

  private static final String TREE = "[0-9a-f]{12} \\(0 uncommitted\\)";

  @TempDir Path root;

  private final List<String> ran = new ArrayList<>();

  // A git that lists one file and no change, and a wrapper whose checks exit as the map says.
  private TestContext gitAndChecks(Map<String, Integer> exits) throws IOException {
    Files.writeString(root.resolve("a.txt"), "a\n");
    return new TestContext(root)
        .run(
            (dir, command) ->
                switch (command.get(1)) {
                  case "ls-files" -> new Processes.Result(0, "a.txt\0");
                  case "rev-parse" -> new Processes.Result(0, "abc123\n");
                  default -> new Processes.Result(0, "");
                })
        .inherit(
            (dir, command) -> {
              assertThat(dir).isEqualTo(root);
              String task = command.get(5);
              ran.add(task);
              return exits.getOrDefault(task, 99);
            });
  }

  @Test
  void runsEveryCheckInOrderEvenAfterARedOneAndEachRowNamesTheTreeAndTheTimeItStartedAt()
      throws IOException {
    TestContext test = gitAndChecks(Map.of("checkFormat", 0, "checkLint", 1, "checkLanguage", 0));
    List<Row> rows = Verify.run(test.context(), List.of("format", "lint", "language"));
    assertThat(ran).containsExactly("checkFormat", "checkLint", "checkLanguage");
    assertThat(rows)
        .extracting(Row::check, Row::result, Row::seconds, Row::facts, Row::at)
        .containsExactly(
            tuple("format", Row.GREEN, 1.5, "", "2026-10-14T00:00:00Z"),
            tuple("lint", Row.RED, 1.5, "", "2026-10-14T00:00:01Z"),
            tuple("language", Row.GREEN, 1.5, "", "2026-10-14T00:00:02Z"));
    assertThat(rows).allSatisfy(row -> assertThat(row.tree()).matches(TREE));
  }

  @Test
  void aRowShowsTheFactsItsCheckLeftAndAFileAnEarlierRunLeftIsGoneBeforeTheCheckRuns()
      throws IOException {
    Facts.write(root, "unit", "stale");
    Facts.write(root, "tooling", "stale");
    TestContext test =
        gitAndChecks(Map.of())
            .inherit(
                (dir, command) -> {
                  ran.add(command.get(5));
                  if (command.get(5).equals("checkUnit")) {
                    writeFacts("unit", "12 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped");
                  }
                  return 0;
                });
    List<Row> rows = Verify.run(test.context(), List.of("unit", "tooling"));
    assertThat(rows)
        .extracting(Row::check, Row::result, Row::facts)
        .containsExactly(
            tuple("unit", Row.GREEN, "12 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped"),
            tuple("tooling", Row.GREEN, ""));
  }

  private void writeFacts(String check, String text) {
    try {
      Facts.write(root, check, text);
    } catch (IOException failed) {
      throw new AssertionError(failed);
    }
  }
}
```

```java
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

import dev.metis.tools.Git;
import dev.metis.tools.Processes;
import dev.metis.tools.TestContext;
import java.io.IOException;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.util.List;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.BeforeEach;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.io.TempDir;

class VerifyCommandTest {

  @TempDir Path root;

  @BeforeEach
  void build() throws IOException {
    tasks("checkFormat", "checkUnit");
    Files.writeString(root.resolve("a.txt"), "a\n");
  }

  // The list of the check tasks of the build, as the launcher writes it.
  private void tasks(String... names) throws IOException {
    Files.createDirectories(root.resolve(Checks.TASKS).getParent());
    Files.writeString(root.resolve(Checks.TASKS), String.join("\n", names) + "\n");
  }

  // A repository whose git lists one file, unless git is lost, and whose format check is red.
  private TestContext repository(boolean lost) {
    return new TestContext(root)
        .run(
            (dir, command) ->
                lost
                    ? new Processes.Result(128, "fatal: not a git repository")
                    : new Processes.Result(0, command.get(1).equals("ls-files") ? "a.txt\0" : ""))
        .inherit((dir, command) -> command.get(5).equals("checkFormat") ? 1 : 0);
  }

  private String report() throws IOException {
    return Files.readString(root.resolve("reports/verify.md"));
  }

  @Test
  void aRedCheckExitsOneWithARedRowAndOnlyWithAppendAddsARerun() throws IOException {
    TestContext full = repository(false);
    assertThat(Verify.command(full.context(), List.of())).isEqualTo(1);
    String written = report();
    assertThat(written)
        .contains("| format | RED |", "| unit | green |", "\nNot run: none\n", "\nCommit: ")
        .doesNotContain("Warning: ");
    assertThat(full.printed()).isEqualTo("\n" + written);
    TestContext rerun = repository(false);
    assertThat(Verify.command(rerun.context(), List.of("--only", "unit", "--append"))).isZero();
    assertThat(rerun.printed()).startsWith("\n# ./verify\n");
    String extended = report();
    assertThat(extended).startsWith(written).contains("\n## Reruns\n").endsWith(" |\n");
    assertThat(extended.substring(written.length())).contains("| unit | green |");
    assertThat(
            Ledger.read(
                Files.readString(root.resolve("reports/verify.json")), List.of("format", "unit")))
        .hasValueSatisfying(ledger -> assertThat(ledger.reruns()).hasSize(1));
  }

  @Test
  void aRunWithoutAppendStartsANewRecordOverAnEarlierOne() throws IOException {
    Verify.command(repository(false).context(), List.of());
    assertThat(Verify.command(repository(false).context(), List.of("--only", "unit"))).isZero();
    assertThat(report()).contains("\nNot run: format\n").doesNotContain("## Reruns");
  }

  @Test
  void handEditsToTheReportDoNotSurviveAnAppendWhichReadsOnlyTheLedger() throws IOException {
    Verify.command(repository(false).context(), List.of());
    String forged = report().replace("| format | RED |", "| format | green |") + "\nAll green.\n";
    Files.writeString(root.resolve("reports/verify.md"), forged);
    Verify.command(repository(false).context(), List.of("--only", "unit", "--append"));
    assertThat(report()).contains("| format | RED |").doesNotContain("All green.");
  }

  @Test
  void anAppendOverAMissingOrUnreadableLedgerStartsANewRecordAndSaysSo() throws IOException {
    for (String corrupt : new String[] {null, "{ \"commit\": \"none\", \"rows\": ["}) {
      Files.deleteIfExists(root.resolve("reports/verify.json"));
      if (corrupt != null) {
        Files.createDirectories(root.resolve("reports"));
        Files.writeString(root.resolve("reports/verify.json"), corrupt);
      }
      TestContext test = repository(false);
      assertThat(Verify.command(test.context(), List.of("--only", "unit", "--append"))).isZero();
      assertThat(test.printed())
          .startsWith(
              "verify: reports/verify.json is missing or unreadable, so a new record starts\n");
      assertThat(report()).contains("\nNot run: format\n").doesNotContain("## Reruns");
    }
  }

  @Test
  void aFullRunThatGitCannotListForExitsOneAndSaysWhyAndARunOfSomeChecksDoesNot()
      throws IOException {
    tasks("checkUnit");
    TestContext full = repository(true);
    assertThat(Verify.command(full.context(), List.of())).isEqualTo(1);
    assertThat(full.printed()).endsWith("verify: " + Report.UNBOUND + "\n");
    assertThat(report()).contains("\nAll rows on one tree: unknown\n", "| " + Git.UNKNOWN + " |");
    TestContext some = repository(true);
    tasks("checkFormat", "checkUnit");
    assertThat(Verify.command(some.context(), List.of("--only", "unit"))).isZero();
    assertThat(some.printed()).doesNotContain("verify: " + Report.UNBOUND);
  }

  @Test
  void anUnknownNameAMissingListAnUnlistedTaskOrNoCheckStopsTheRunBeforeAnythingRuns()
      throws IOException {
    TestContext unknown = new TestContext(root);
    assertThat(Verify.command(unknown.context(), List.of("--only", "gamma"))).isEqualTo(1);
    assertThat(unknown.printed()).isEqualTo("verify: no such check: gamma\n");
    tasks("checkFormat", "checkTyped");
    TestContext unlisted = new TestContext(root);
    assertThat(Verify.command(unlisted.context(), List.of())).isEqualTo(1);
    assertThat(unlisted.printed())
        .isEqualTo("verify: Gradle has check tasks that Checks.ORDER does not list: checkTyped\n");
    Files.writeString(root.resolve(Checks.TASKS), "");
    TestContext empty = new TestContext(root);
    assertThat(Verify.command(empty.context(), List.of())).isEqualTo(1);
    assertThat(empty.printed()).isEqualTo("verify: the build has no check task\n");
    Files.delete(root.resolve(Checks.TASKS));
    TestContext missing = new TestContext(root);
    assertThat(Verify.command(missing.context(), List.of())).isEqualTo(1);
    assertThat(missing.printed()).startsWith("verify: no list of the checks in ");
    assertThat(root.resolve("reports")).doesNotExist();
  }
}
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.util.List;

/** A command of the tool, run with the arguments after its name; it returns the exit code. */
@FunctionalInterface
interface Command {

  int run(Context context, List<String> args) throws IOException;
}
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools;

import java.io.PrintStream;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.time.Instant;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.function.BiFunction;
import java.util.function.LongSupplier;
import java.util.function.Supplier;
import java.util.function.ToIntBiFunction;

/** The edges of a command: the root, the output, processes, clocks and the workers of a build. */
public record Context(
    Path root,
    PrintStream out,
    BiFunction<Path, List<String>, Processes.Result> run,
    BiFunction<Path, List<String>, Processes.Result> quiet,
    ToIntBiFunction<Path, List<String>> inherit,
    LongSupplier nanos,
    Supplier<Instant> now,
    int workers) {

  /**
   * Git in the repository root; a warning never reads as output, and a failure keeps its reason.
   */
  public Git git() {
    return new Git(
        root,
        args -> {
          List<String> command = new ArrayList<>(List.of("git"));
          command.addAll(args);
          return quiet().apply(root, command);
        });
  }
}
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools;

import dev.metis.tools.verify.Verify;
import java.io.IOException;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import org.jspecify.annotations.Nullable;

/** The commands of the tool of the checks. */
public final class Cli {

  private static final Map<String, Command> COMMANDS = Map.of("verify", Verify::command);

  private static final String USAGE =
      """
      usage: verify [--only <check>[,<check>]] [--fast] [--append]""";

  private Cli() {}

  /** Runs the command the arguments name and returns its exit code. */
  public static int run(Context context, List<String> args) throws IOException {
    @Nullable Command command = args.isEmpty() ? null : COMMANDS.get(args.getFirst());
    if (command == null) {
      context.out().println(USAGE);
      return 2;
    }
    return command.run(context, args.subList(1, args.size()));
  }
}
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.time.Instant;
import java.util.List;

/** The process of the tool, which ./verify and ./canary start from the repository root. */
public final class Main {

  private Main() {}

  public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException {
    // Half the cores, as for the tests and the mutation testing of a build.
    int workers = Math.max(1, Runtime.getRuntime().availableProcessors() / 2);
    Context context =
        new Context(
            Path.of("").toAbsolutePath(),
            System.out,
            Processes::run,
            Processes::quiet,
            Processes::inherit,
            System::nanoTime,
            Instant::now,
            workers);
    System.exit(Cli.run(context, List.of(args)));
  }
}
```
