```java
package dev.metis.tools.verify;

import dev.metis.tools.Context;
import dev.metis.tools.Facts;
import dev.metis.tools.Git;
import java.io.IOException;
import java.io.PrintStream;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Optional;

/** ./verify: runs the checks, one after the other, and keeps the record of the run. */
public final class Verify {

  private Verify() {}

  /** Runs the checks the arguments ask for, writes the record and returns the exit code. */
  public static int command(Context context, List<String> args) throws IOException {
    Path root = context.root();
    PrintStream out = context.out();
    Optional<List<String>> found = checksOf(root, out);
    if (found.isEmpty()) {
      return 1;
    }
    List<String> all = found.get();
    Plan plan;
    try {
      plan = Plan.of(args, all);
    } catch (IllegalArgumentException wrong) {
      out.println("verify: " + wrong.getMessage());
      return 1;
    }
    Optional<Ledger> previous = plan.append() ? previous(root, all) : Optional.empty();
    if (plan.append() && previous.isEmpty()) {
      out.println("verify: reports/verify.json is missing or unreadable, so a new record starts");
    }
    List<Row> rows = run(context, plan.checks());
    Ledger ledger =
        previous
            .map(earlier -> earlier.withReruns(rows))
            .orElseGet(() -> new Ledger(context.git().commit(), rows, List.of()));
    Files.createDirectories(root.resolve("reports"));
    Files.writeString(root.resolve("reports/verify.json"), Ledger.write(ledger));
    String report = Report.of(ledger, all);
    Files.writeString(root.resolve("reports/verify.md"), report);
    out.print("\n" + report);
    // A full run is the record others cite, so one that cannot name its tree fails.
    boolean unbound = plan.full() && rows.stream().anyMatch(row -> row.tree().equals(Git.UNKNOWN));
    if (unbound) {
      out.println("verify: " + Report.UNBOUND);
    }
    return unbound || rows.stream().anyMatch(row -> row.result().equals(Row.RED)) ? 1 : 0;
  }

  // The checks Gradle has, or none when the list is missing, holds a task the tool lacks, or is
  // empty.
  private static Optional<List<String>> checksOf(Path root, PrintStream out) {
    try {
      List<String> all = Checks.of(Checks.tasks(root));
      if (all.isEmpty()) {
        out.println("verify: the build has no check task");
      }
      return Optional.of(all).filter(checks -> !checks.isEmpty());
    } catch (IOException | IllegalArgumentException unusable) {
      out.println("verify: " + unusable.getMessage());
      return Optional.empty();
    }
  }

  private static Optional<Ledger> previous(Path root, List<String> all) throws IOException {
    Path json = root.resolve("reports/verify.json");
    return Files.exists(json) ? Ledger.read(Files.readString(json), all) : Optional.empty();
  }

  /** Runs each check, even after a red one, and gives its row. */
  static List<Row> run(Context context, List<String> checks) throws IOException {
    Path root = context.root();
    Git git = context.git();
    List<Row> rows = new ArrayList<>();
    for (String check : checks) {
      Facts.clear(root, check);
      String tree = git.tree();
      String at = context.now().get().toString();
      long start = context.nanos().getAsLong();
      List<String> command = Checks.command(root, check, context.workers(), List.of());
      int status = context.inherit().applyAsInt(root, command);
      double seconds = (context.nanos().getAsLong() - start) / 1e9;
      String result = status == 0 ? Row.GREEN : Row.RED;
      rows.add(new Row(check, result, seconds, Facts.read(root, check).orElse(""), tree, at));
    }
    return rows;
  }
}
```

```kotlin
plugins {
    id("metis.java-conventions")
    application

application {
    mainClass = "dev.metis.tools.Main"
}

dependencies {
    implementation("tools.jackson.core:jackson-core")
    implementation("tools.jackson.core:jackson-databind")
}

// ./verify and ./canary start the tool with the Java and the classpath this task writes, and the tool
// learns from it the check tasks Gradle has in every project, however a build file declares them.
val launcher = tasks.register("launcher") {
    val executable = javaToolchains.launcherFor(java.toolchain).map { it.executablePath.asFile.path }
    val classpath = sourceSets.main.map { it.runtimeClasspath }
    val checks = rootProject.allprojects.flatMap { project ->
        val prefix = if (project == rootProject) "" else project.path + ":"
        project.tasks.names.filter { it.matches(Regex("check[A-Z]\\w*")) }.map { prefix + it }
    }
    val folder = layout.buildDirectory.dir("launcher")
    inputs.files(classpath)
    inputs.property("java", executable)
    inputs.property("checks", checks)
    outputs.dir(folder)
    doLast {
        folder.get().file("java").asFile.writeText(executable.get() + "\n")
        folder.get().file("args").asFile.writeText("-cp\n\"" + classpath.get().asPath + "\"\n")
        folder.get().file("checks").asFile.writeText(checks.joinToString("") { "$it\n" })
    }
}
```

```sh
#!/bin/sh
# Runs every check of the repository and writes reports/verify.json and reports/verify.md.
# The lowest priority, which every child inherits, keeps the machine usable during a long run.
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
nice -n 19 ./gradlew --quiet --priority=low :tools:launcher
exec nice -n 19 "$(cat tools/build/launcher/java)" @tools/build/launcher/args dev.metis.tools.Main verify "$@"
```

- [ ] **Step 7: Add the files of this task to the ledger**

Add the files the list above names, the generated ones included, to the ledger of the run. Never run git add, git commit or git push: the owner commits.

### Task 7: The counter-tests, the format check and the compile check

A counter-test (a canary) copies the files git lists into `build/canary/<name>/`, requires its check green on the copy, plants one defect (a file written, a text appended, a file deleted), and requires the check red with the text that names that very defect, so a check red for another reason proves nothing. `./canary <name>` runs one, `./canary all` runs them all and exits 1 if one was blind. The first two checks: `checkFormat` (Spotless with google-java-format, unused imports removed, trailing whitespace and a final newline in the other text files) and `checkCompile`. Every check owes the facts of its judge, or fails, unless the root build names it in `factFree`, so a test check wired without its judge is red; the runs of `./verify` and `./canary` clear the facts before each check.

```java
package dev.metis.tools.canary;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThatThrownBy;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.NoSuchFileException;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.io.TempDir;

class CanaryTest {

  @TempDir Path root;

  @Test
  void aCanaryCollectsWhatItPlantsWithoutChangingTheOneItWasMadeFrom() {
    Canary bare = Canary.of("lint-length", "lint", "[FileLength]");
    Canary planted =
        bare.writing("a/B.java", "class B {}\n")
            .writing("a/C.java", "class C {}\n")
            .appending("build.gradle.kts", "tasks.register(\"checkCanary\")\n")
            .replacing("build.gradle.kts", "dependsOn(a, b)", "dependsOn(a)")
            .deleting("test-floor.json");
    assertThat(bare)
        .isEqualTo(
            new Canary(
                "lint-length",
                "lint",
                "[FileLength]",
                List.of(),
                Map.of(),
                Map.of(),
                List.of(),
                List.of()));
    assertThat(planted.writes())
        .containsExactly(
            Map.entry("a/B.java", "class B {}\n"), Map.entry("a/C.java", "class C {}\n"));
    assertThat(planted.appends())
        .containsExactly(Map.entry("build.gradle.kts", "tasks.register(\"checkCanary\")\n"));
    assertThat(planted.replacements())
        .containsExactly(
            new Canary.Replacement("build.gradle.kts", "dependsOn(a, b)", "dependsOn(a)"));
    assertThat(planted.deletes()).containsExactly("test-floor.json");
  }

  @Test
  void plantingWritesFilesInNewFoldersAppendsToFilesReplacesATextAndDeletesFiles()
      throws IOException {
    Files.writeString(root.resolve("build.gradle.kts"), "plugins {}\n");
    Files.writeString(root.resolve("a.kts"), "dependsOn(a, b)\ndependsOn(a, b)\n");
    Files.writeString(root.resolve("test-floor.json"), "{}\n");
    Files.writeString(root.resolve("Old.java"), "class Old {}\n");
    Canary.of("all-kinds", "lint", "x")
        .writing("a/b/New.java", "class New {}\n")
        .writing("Old.java", "class Replaced {}\n")
        .appending("build.gradle.kts", "tasks.register(\"checkCanary\")\n")
        .replacing("a.kts", "dependsOn(a, b)", "dependsOn(a)")
        .deleting("test-floor.json")
        .plant(root);
    assertThat(root.resolve("a.kts")).hasContent("dependsOn(a)\ndependsOn(a, b)");
    assertThat(root.resolve("a/b/New.java")).hasContent("class New {}");
    assertThat(root.resolve("Old.java")).hasContent("class Replaced {}");
    assertThat(root.resolve("build.gradle.kts"))
        .hasContent("plugins {}\ntasks.register(\"checkCanary\")");
    assertThat(root.resolve("test-floor.json")).doesNotExist();
  }

  @Test
  void appendingToOrDeletingAFileTheTreeLacksIsAnError() {
    assertThatThrownBy(() -> Canary.of("a", "lint", "x").appending("gone.txt", "x").plant(root))
        .isInstanceOf(NoSuchFileException.class);
    assertThatThrownBy(() -> Canary.of("d", "lint", "x").deleting("gone.txt").plant(root))
        .isInstanceOf(NoSuchFileException.class);
  }

  @Test
  void replacingATextTheFileLacksIsAnErrorSoACounterTestNeverPlantsNothing() throws IOException {
    Files.writeString(root.resolve("a.kts"), "dependsOn(a)\n");
    assertThatThrownBy(
            () -> Canary.of("r", "unit", "x").replacing("a.kts", "dependsOn(b)", "").plant(root))
        .isInstanceOf(IOException.class)
        .hasMessage("a.kts holds no dependsOn(b)");
  }
}
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools.canary;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

import dev.metis.tools.Processes;
import dev.metis.tools.TestContext;
import java.io.IOException;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.nio.file.attribute.PosixFilePermissions;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.BeforeEach;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.io.TempDir;

class CanaryRunTest {

  private static final Canary LENGTH =
      Canary.of("lint-length", "lint", "[FileLength]").writing("core/Long.java", "class Long {}\n");
  private static final Processes.Result GREEN = new Processes.Result(0, "BUILD SUCCESSFUL\n");

  @TempDir Path root;

  private final List<List<String>> commands = new ArrayList<>();

  @BeforeEach
  void tree() throws IOException {
    Files.writeString(root.resolve("gradlew"), "#!/bin/sh\n");
    Files.setPosixFilePermissions(
        root.resolve("gradlew"), PosixFilePermissions.fromString("rwxr-xr-x"));
    Files.createDirectories(root.resolve("core"));
    Files.writeString(root.resolve("core/A.java"), "class A {}\n");
    Files.writeString(root.resolve("notes.txt"), "not listed\n");
  }

  private Path scratch() {
    return root.resolve("build/canary/lint-length");
  }

  // A check that answers the first run and the second one with the given results.
  private TestContext checks(Processes.Result before, Processes.Result after) {
    return new TestContext(root)
        .run(
            (dir, command) -> {
              assertThat(dir).isEqualTo(scratch());
              commands.add(command);
              boolean planted = Files.exists(dir.resolve("core/Long.java"));
              assertThat(planted).isEqualTo(commands.size() == 2);
              return planted ? after : before;
            });
  }

  private boolean run(TestContext test) throws IOException {
    return CanaryRun.run(test.context(), LENGTH, List.of("core/A.java", "gradlew"));
  }

  @Test
  void theFactsOfTheGreenRunAreGoneBeforeTheRunOnThePlantedDefect() throws IOException {
    TestContext test =
        new TestContext(root)
            .run(
                (dir, command) -> {
                  Path facts = dir.resolve("build/facts/lint.txt");
                  assertThat(facts).doesNotExist();
                  write(facts);
                  commands.add(command);
                  return commands.size() == 1 ? GREEN : new Processes.Result(1, "[FileLength]");
                });
    assertThat(run(test)).isTrue();
  }

  private static void write(Path facts) {
    try {
      Files.createDirectories(facts.getParent());
      Files.writeString(facts, "12 passed");
    } catch (IOException failed) {
      throw new AssertionError(failed);
    }
  }

  @Test
  void aCheckGreenOnTheCopyAndRedForThePlantedDefectCatchesItAndTheCopyIsRemoved()
      throws IOException {
    TestContext test = checks(GREEN, new Processes.Result(1, "Long.java:1: [FileLength]\n"));
    assertThat(run(test)).isTrue();
    assertThat(test.printed())
        .isEqualTo(
            """
            canary lint-length: running checkLint ...
            canary lint-length: checkLint went red because of the planted defect
            """);
    assertThat(commands)
        .allSatisfy(
            command ->
                assertThat(command)
                    .startsWith(scratch().resolve("gradlew").toString())
                    .endsWith("checkLint"));
    assertThat(scratch()).doesNotExist();
    assertThat(root.resolve("build/canary/lint-length.log"))
        .hasContent("Long.java:1: [FileLength]");
    assertThat(root.resolve("core/Long.java")).doesNotExist();
  }

  @Test
  void theCopyHoldsTheListedFilesWithTheirModesAndNothingAnEarlierRunLeft() throws IOException {
    Files.createDirectories(scratch());
    Files.writeString(scratch().resolve("leftover.txt"), "from an earlier run\n");
    TestContext test =
        new TestContext(root)
            .run(
                (dir, command) -> {
                  assertThat(dir.resolve("core/A.java")).hasContent("class A {}");
                  assertThat(dir.resolve("gradlew")).isExecutable();
                  assertThat(dir.resolve("notes.txt")).doesNotExist();
                  assertThat(dir.resolve("leftover.txt")).doesNotExist();
                  return GREEN;
                });
    assertThat(run(test)).isFalse();
    assertThat(scratch()).isDirectory();
  }

  @Test
  void aCheckThatStaysGreenWithTheDefectIsBlindAndKeepsItsCopy() throws IOException {
    TestContext test = checks(GREEN, GREEN);
    assertThat(run(test)).isFalse();
    assertThat(test.printed())
        .endsWith(
            "canary lint-length: checkLint did NOT catch the planted defect (exit 0),"
                + " see build/canary/lint-length.log\n");
    assertThat(scratch().resolve("core/Long.java")).exists();
  }

  @Test
  void aCheckRedForAnotherReasonOrGreenWhilePrintingTheTextDoesNotCatchTheDefect()
      throws IOException {
    assertThat(run(checks(GREEN, new Processes.Result(1, "ENOENT\n")))).isFalse();
    commands.clear();
    TestContext loud = checks(GREEN, new Processes.Result(0, "[FileLength]\n"));
    assertThat(run(loud)).isFalse();
    assertThat(loud.printed()).contains("did NOT catch the planted defect (exit 0)");
  }

  @Test
  void aCheckAlreadyRedBeforePlantingFailsAtOnceAndPlantsNothing() throws IOException {
    Processes.Result red = new Processes.Result(3, "[FileLength] in another file\n");
    TestContext test = checks(red, GREEN);
    assertThat(run(test)).isFalse();
    assertThat(commands).hasSize(1);
    assertThat(test.printed())
        .endsWith(
            "canary lint-length: checkLint was already red before planting (exit 3),"
                + " see build/canary/lint-length.log\n");
    assertThat(scratch().resolve("core/Long.java")).doesNotExist();
    assertThat(root.resolve("build/canary/lint-length.log"))
        .hasContent("[FileLength] in another file");
  }
}
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools.canary;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

import dev.metis.tools.Processes;
import dev.metis.tools.TestContext;
import java.io.IOException;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.HashMap;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.TreeMap;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.io.TempDir;

class CanaryCommandTest {

  @TempDir Path root;

  private final Map<String, Integer> runs = new HashMap<>();

  // The files a canary appends to, replaces a text of or deletes, which the copy needs, each
  // holding the texts the canaries replace.
  private List<String> tree() throws IOException {
    Map<String, String> files = new TreeMap<>(Map.of("gradlew", ""));
    for (Canary canary : Canaries.ALL) {
      canary.appends().keySet().forEach(file -> files.putIfAbsent(file, ""));
      canary.deletes().forEach(file -> files.putIfAbsent(file, ""));
      canary.replacements().forEach(swap -> files.merge(swap.path(), swap.text(), String::concat));
    }
    for (Map.Entry<String, String> file : files.entrySet()) {
      Files.createDirectories(root.resolve(file.getKey()).getParent());
      Files.writeString(root.resolve(file.getKey()), file.getValue());
    }
    return new ArrayList<>(files.keySet());
  }

  // Git lists the tree; each check is green on its copy, then red with the text its canary expects.
  private TestContext checks(List<String> files, boolean blindLast) {
    return new TestContext(root)
        .run(
            (dir, command) -> {
              if (command.getFirst().equals("git")) {
                return new Processes.Result(0, String.join("\0", files) + "\0");
              }
              Canary canary = canaryOf(dir);
              int run = runs.merge(canary.name(), 1, Integer::sum);
              if (run == 1) {
                return new Processes.Result(0, "BUILD SUCCESSFUL\n");
              }
              planted(dir, canary);
              boolean blind = blindLast && canary.equals(Canaries.ALL.getLast());
              return blind
                  ? new Processes.Result(0, "BUILD SUCCESSFUL\n")
                  : new Processes.Result(1, "... " + canary.expect() + " ...\n");
            });
  }

  private static Canary canaryOf(Path dir) {
    String name = dir.getFileName().toString();
    return Canaries.ALL.stream()
        .filter(canary -> canary.name().equals(name))
        .findFirst()
        .orElseThrow();
  }

  private static void planted(Path dir, Canary canary) {
    canary.writes().forEach((file, text) -> assertThat(read(dir.resolve(file))).isEqualTo(text));
    canary.appends().forEach((file, text) -> assertThat(read(dir.resolve(file))).endsWith(text));
    canary
        .replacements()
        .forEach(swap -> assertThat(read(dir.resolve(swap.path()))).contains(swap.with()));
    canary.deletes().forEach(file -> assertThat(dir.resolve(file)).doesNotExist());
  }

  private static String read(Path file) {
    try {
      return Files.readString(file);
    } catch (IOException failed) {
      throw new AssertionError(failed);
    }
  }

  @Test
  void allRunsEveryCanaryOnItsOwnCopyAndExitsZeroWhenEachOneCaught() throws IOException {
    TestContext test = checks(tree(), false);
    assertThat(CanaryRun.command(test.context(), List.of("all"))).isZero();
    assertThat(runs)
        .hasSize(Canaries.ALL.size())
        .allSatisfy((name, count) -> assertThat(count).isEqualTo(2));
    assertThat(
            test.printed().lines().filter(line -> line.endsWith("because of the planted defect")))
        .hasSize(Canaries.ALL.size());
  }

  @Test
  void oneBlindCanaryAmongAllMakesTheRunExitOneAfterEveryCanaryRan() throws IOException {
    TestContext test = checks(tree(), true);
    assertThat(CanaryRun.command(test.context(), List.of("all"))).isEqualTo(1);
    assertThat(runs).hasSize(Canaries.ALL.size());
  }

  @Test
  void aNameRunsThatCanaryAlone() throws IOException {
    TestContext test = checks(tree(), false);
    String name = Canaries.ALL.getFirst().name();
    assertThat(CanaryRun.command(test.context(), List.of(name))).isZero();
    assertThat(runs).containsOnlyKeys(name);
  }

  @Test
  void anUnknownNameNoNameOrATreeGitCannotListStopsTheRun() throws IOException {
    TestContext unknown = new TestContext(root);
    assertThat(CanaryRun.command(unknown.context(), List.of("nope"))).isEqualTo(1);
    assertThat(unknown.printed()).isEqualTo("canary: no such canary: nope\n");
    TestContext none = new TestContext(root);
    assertThat(CanaryRun.command(none.context(), List.of())).isEqualTo(2);
    assertThat(CanaryRun.command(none.context(), List.of("a", "b"))).isEqualTo(2);
    assertThat(none.printed()).isEqualTo("usage: canary <name>|all\nusage: canary <name>|all\n");
    TestContext lost =
        new TestContext(root)
            .run((dir, command) -> new Processes.Result(128, "fatal: not a git repository"));
    assertThat(CanaryRun.command(lost.context(), List.of("all"))).isEqualTo(1);
    assertThat(lost.printed()).isEqualTo("canary: git cannot list the files of the tree\n");
  }
}
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools.canary;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.nio.file.StandardOpenOption;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.Collections;
import java.util.LinkedHashMap;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;

/** A counter-test: a defect for a copy of the tree, and the text its check must go red with. */
public record Canary(
    String name,
    String check,
    String expect,
    List<String> args,
    Map<String, String> writes,
    Map<String, String> appends,
    List<Canary.Replacement> replacements,
    List<String> deletes) {

  /** A text of a file of the tree that the canary replaces with another. */
  public record Replacement(String path, String text, String with) {}

  /** A canary that plants nothing yet. */
  public static Canary of(String name, String check, String expect) {
    return new Canary(name, check, expect, List.of(), Map.of(), Map.of(), List.of(), List.of());
  }

  /** The same canary, which also writes the file, in place of the one the tree holds. */
  public Canary writing(String path, String text) {
    return new Canary(
        name, check, expect, args, with(writes, path, text), appends, replacements, deletes);
  }

  /** The same canary, which also adds the text to the end of a file of the tree. */
  public Canary appending(String path, String text) {
    return new Canary(
        name, check, expect, args, writes, with(appends, path, text), replacements, deletes);
  }

  /** The same canary, which also replaces the first place of a text in a file of the tree. */
  public Canary replacing(String path, String text, String with) {
    List<Replacement> more = new ArrayList<>(replacements);
    more.add(new Replacement(path, text, with));
    return new Canary(name, check, expect, args, writes, appends, List.copyOf(more), deletes);
  }

  /** The same canary, which also deletes a file of the tree. */
  public Canary deleting(String path) {
    return new Canary(
        name, check, expect, args, writes, appends, replacements, with(deletes, path));
  }

  /** Plants the defect in the copy of the tree at root. */
  void plant(Path root) throws IOException {
    for (Map.Entry<String, String> file : writes().entrySet()) {
      Path path = root.resolve(file.getKey());
      Files.createDirectories(path.getParent());
      Files.writeString(path, file.getValue());
    }
    for (Map.Entry<String, String> file : appends().entrySet()) {
      Files.writeString(root.resolve(file.getKey()), file.getValue(), StandardOpenOption.APPEND);
    }
    for (Replacement swap : replacements()) {
      Path path = root.resolve(swap.path());
      String text = Files.readString(path);
      int at = text.indexOf(swap.text());
      if (at < 0) {
        throw new IOException(swap.path() + " holds no " + swap.text());
      }
      Files.writeString(
          path, text.substring(0, at) + swap.with() + text.substring(at + swap.text().length()));
    }
    for (String path : deletes()) {
      Files.delete(root.resolve(path));
    }
  }

  private static Map<String, String> with(Map<String, String> map, String key, String value) {
    Map<String, String> copy = new LinkedHashMap<>(map);
    copy.put(key, value);
    return Collections.unmodifiableMap(copy);
  }

  private static List<String> with(List<String> list, String more) {
    List<String> copy = new ArrayList<>(list);
    copy.add(more);
    return List.copyOf(copy);
  }
}
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools.canary;

import dev.metis.tools.Context;
import dev.metis.tools.Facts;
import dev.metis.tools.Processes;
import dev.metis.tools.verify.Checks;
import java.io.IOException;
import java.io.PrintStream;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.nio.file.StandardCopyOption;
import java.util.Comparator;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Optional;
import java.util.stream.Stream;

/** ./canary: runs counter-tests, each on a copy of the tree under build/canary. */
public final class CanaryRun {

  private CanaryRun() {}

  /** Runs the canary the arguments name, or all of them, and exits 0 when each one caught. */
  public static int command(Context context, List<String> args) throws IOException {
    PrintStream out = context.out();
    if (args.size() != 1) {
      out.println("usage: canary <name>|all");
      return 2;
    }
    String name = args.getFirst();
    List<Canary> chosen =
        Canaries.ALL.stream()
            .filter(canary -> name.equals("all") || canary.name().equals(name))
            .toList();
    if (chosen.isEmpty()) {
      out.println("canary: no such canary: " + name);
      return 1;
    }
    Optional<List<String>> files = context.git().files();
    if (files.isEmpty()) {
      out.println("canary: git cannot list the files of the tree");
      return 1;
    }
    boolean caught = true;
    for (Canary canary : chosen) {
      caught &= run(context, canary, files.get());
    }
    return caught ? 0 : 1;
  }

  /** Runs one counter-test, on a fresh copy of the listed files, and says whether it caught. */
  static boolean run(Context context, Canary canary, List<String> files) throws IOException {
    Path folder = context.root().resolve("build/canary");
    Path copy = folder.resolve(canary.name());
    String log = "build/canary/" + canary.name() + ".log";
    String task = Checks.task(canary.check());
    String named = "canary " + canary.name() + ": " + task;
    PrintStream out = context.out();
    copyInto(copy, context.root(), files);
    out.println("canary " + canary.name() + ": running " + task + " ...");
    // A check red before the defect is planted proves nothing about the defect.
    Processes.Result before = check(context, copy, canary);
    if (before.status() != 0) {
      Files.writeString(context.root().resolve(log), before.output());
      out.printf(
          "%s was already red before planting (exit %d), see %s%n", named, before.status(), log);
      return false;
    }
    canary.plant(copy);
    Processes.Result after = check(context, copy, canary);
    Files.writeString(context.root().resolve(log), after.output());
    boolean caught = after.status() != 0 && after.output().contains(canary.expect());
    if (caught) {
      out.println(named + " went red because of the planted defect");
      delete(copy);
    } else {
      out.printf(
          "%s did NOT catch the planted defect (exit %d), see %s%n", named, after.status(), log);
    }
    return caught;
  }

  // The facts of an earlier run in the copy must not stand in for a judge that did not run.
  private static Processes.Result check(Context context, Path copy, Canary canary)
      throws IOException {
    Facts.clear(copy, canary.check());
    List<String> command = Checks.command(copy, canary.check(), context.workers(), canary.args());
    return context.run().apply(copy, command);
  }

  private static void copyInto(Path copy, Path root, List<String> files) throws IOException {
    delete(copy);
    for (String file : files) {
      Path target = copy.resolve(file);
      Files.createDirectories(target.getParent());
      Files.copy(root.resolve(file), target, StandardCopyOption.COPY_ATTRIBUTES);
    }
  }

  private static void delete(Path folder) throws IOException {
    if (Files.exists(folder)) {
      try (Stream<Path> paths = Files.walk(folder)) {
        for (Path path : paths.sorted(Comparator.reverseOrder()).toList()) {
          Files.delete(path);
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

```java
  /** Every counter-test, one list per check. */
```

```java
/** The counter-test of the format check. */
final class FormatCanaries {

  static final List<Canary> ALL =
      List.of(
          // A line indented by three spaces, which the formatter would move.
          Canary.of("format-indent", "format", "CanaryFormat.java")
              .writing(
                  Canaries.CORE + "CanaryFormat.java",
                  """
                  package dev.metis.core;

                  final class CanaryFormat {
                     private CanaryFormat() {}
                  }
                  """),
          // Spaces at the end of a line of a file that is no Java, which the plain step trims.
          Canary.of("format-misc", "format", "CANARY.md")
              .writing("CANARY.md", "A line that ends in spaces.   \n"));
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools.canary;

import java.util.List;

/** The counter-tests of the compile check. */
final class CompileCanaries {

  static final List<Canary> ALL =
      List.of(
          // Error Prone names an unused local after the unnamed variable that would replace it.
          Canary.of("compile-unused-local", "compile", "[UnnamedVariable]")
              .writing(
                  Canaries.CORE + "CanaryUnused.java",
                  """
                  package dev.metis.core;

                  final class CanaryUnused {
                    private CanaryUnused() {}

                    static int two() {
                      int unused = 1;
                      return 2;
                    }
                  }
                  """),
          Canary.of("compile-null", "compile", "[NullAway]")
              .writing(
                  Canaries.CORE + "CanaryNull.java",
                  """
                  package dev.metis.core;

                  final class CanaryNull {
                    private CanaryNull() {}

                    static String name() {
                      return null;
                    }
                  }
                  """),
          Canary.of("compile-raw-type", "compile", "[rawtypes]")
              .writing(
                  Canaries.CORE + "CanaryRaw.java",
                  """
                  package dev.metis.core;

                  import java.util.ArrayList;
                  import java.util.List;

                  final class CanaryRaw {
                    private CanaryRaw() {}

                    static List<?> names() {
                      return new ArrayList();
                    }
                  }
                  """));

  private CompileCanaries() {}
}
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools;

import dev.metis.tools.canary.CanaryRun;
import dev.metis.tools.verify.Verify;
import java.io.IOException;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import org.jspecify.annotations.Nullable;

/** The commands of the tool of the checks. */
public final class Cli {

  private static final Map<String, Command> COMMANDS =
      Map.of(
          "verify", Verify::command,
          "canary", CanaryRun::command);

  private static final String USAGE =
      """
      usage: verify [--only <check>[,<check>]] [--fast] [--append]
             canary <name>|all""";

  private Cli() {}

  /** Runs the command the arguments name and returns its exit code. */
  public static int run(Context context, List<String> args) throws IOException {
    @Nullable Command command = args.isEmpty() ? null : COMMANDS.get(args.getFirst());
    if (command == null) {
      context.out().println(USAGE);
      return 2;
    }
    return command.run(context, args.subList(1, args.size()));
  }
}
```

`./canary`:

```sh
#!/bin/sh
# Runs one counter-test, or all of them, each on a copy of the tree under build/canary.
# The lowest priority, which every child inherits, keeps the machine usable during a long run.
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
nice -n 19 ./gradlew --quiet --priority=low :tools:launcher
exec nice -n 19 "$(cat tools/build/launcher/java)" @tools/build/launcher/args dev.metis.tools.Main canary "$@"
```

`build.gradle.kts`:

```kotlin
plugins {
    alias(libs.plugins.spotless)
}

dependencyLocking {
    lockAllConfigurations()
}

spotless {
    java {
        target("core/src/**/*.java", "tools/src/**/*.java")
        googleJavaFormat(libs.versions.google.java.format.get())
        removeUnusedImports()
    }
    format("misc") {
        target(
            "**/*.kts", "**/*.md", "**/*.yml", "**/*.yaml", "**/*.toml", "**/*.properties",
            "**/*.json", "**/*.xml", "**/*.txt", "**/Dockerfile", "**/.gitignore", ".dockerignore",
            "verify", "canary",
        )
        targetExclude("**/build/**", "**/.gradle/**", "**/.kotlin/**", "gradle/verification-metadata.xml")
        trimTrailingWhitespace()
        endWithNewline()
    }
}

// The checks of ./verify, which runs them in the order of the list of the tool, Checks.ORDER.

tasks.register("checkFormat") {
    description = "Every source file is formatted."
    dependsOn("spotlessCheck")
}

tasks.register("checkCompile") {
    description = "The code compiles with every warning an error, no bug pattern and no null where none is allowed."
    dependsOn(":core:compileJava", ":core:compileTestJava", ":tools:compileJava", ":tools:compileTestJava")
}

// A check whose judge did not run would pass on the exit of its tasks alone, so a check that owes
// facts fails without them; ./verify and ./canary clear the facts before each run of a check.
val factFree = setOf("checkFormat", "checkCompile", "checkDeps", "checkSecrets")
tasks.matching { it.name.matches(Regex("check[A-Z]\\w*")) && it.name !in factFree }.configureEach {
    val check = name.removePrefix("check").replaceFirstChar(Char::lowercase)
    val facts = layout.buildDirectory.file("facts/$check.txt")
    doLast {
        if (!facts.get().asFile.exists()) {
            throw GradleException("$name: its judge left no facts in build/facts/$check.txt")
        }
    }
}
```

### Task 8: The language check

The port of the app's `check-language.mjs`. The command `language` reads every text file under the paths given, or under the whole repository, skipping binary files and, by their exact place, git's folder and the record `reports/` at the root and the folders `build`, `.gradle` and `.kotlin` that Gradle writes beside a build script, so a package named `reports` or `build` is read. A letter outside ASCII is a problem anywhere; in a comment, so is a citation of a plan or a ruling, a section of a spec, a line of a file or a date. Comments are found by tokens: `//` and `/* */` in Java and Kotlin scripts (strings and text blocks stepped over), `<!-- -->` in XML, `#` in the other kinds, `--` and `/* */` in SQL (strings stepped over), and every line of Markdown, which is prose. `lang-exception: <reason>` excuses the next line. A file that is not UTF-8 is a problem of its own, never skipped; only a NUL byte makes a file binary, unless the file opens with the mark of UTF-16, a text in another encoding. `TextFiles` lists the files, for this check and the next one, and `Comments.javaCode` gives the code of a Java line without its comments and strings, for the next one.

`tools/src/test/java/dev/metis/tools/TestContext.java`:

```java
package dev.metis.tools;

import java.io.ByteArrayOutputStream;
import java.io.PrintStream;
import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.time.Instant;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.function.BiFunction;
import java.util.function.ToIntBiFunction;

/** A context for the tests of a command: its output is kept, and an edge not given fails. */
public final class TestContext {

  /** The time of the first stamp; each stamp is a second later than the one before. */
  public static final Instant START = Instant.parse("2026-10-14T00:00:00Z");

  /** The exit code a test keeps beside the context, for a helper that runs the command. */
  public int exit;

  private final ByteArrayOutputStream printed = new ByteArrayOutputStream();
  private final Path root;
  private BiFunction<Path, List<String>, Processes.Result> run = TestContext::unexpected;
  private ToIntBiFunction<Path, List<String>> inherit =
      (dir, command) -> unexpected(dir, command).status();
  private long nanos;
  private long stamps;

  public TestContext(Path root) {
    this.root = root;
  }

  private static Processes.Result unexpected(Path dir, List<String> command) {
    throw new AssertionError("unexpected command in " + dir + ": " + command);
  }

  public TestContext run(BiFunction<Path, List<String>, Processes.Result> run) {
    this.run = run;
    return this;
  }

  public TestContext inherit(ToIntBiFunction<Path, List<String>> inherit) {
    this.inherit = inherit;
    return this;
  }

  /** The context, whose clock moves 1.5 seconds on each read. */
  public Context context() {
    return new Context(
        root,
        new PrintStream(printed, true, StandardCharsets.UTF_8),
        run,
        run,
        inherit,
        () -> nanos += 1_500_000_000L,
        () -> START.plusSeconds(stamps++),
        3);
  }

  /** What the command printed. */
  public String printed() {
    return printed.toString(StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
  }
}
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThatThrownBy;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.io.UncheckedIOException;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.NoSuchFileException;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.util.List;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.io.TempDir;

class TextFilesTest {

  @TempDir Path root;

  private void write(String path, String text) throws IOException {
    Files.createDirectories(root.resolve(path).getParent());
    Files.writeString(root.resolve(path), text);
  }

  @Test
  void theTextFilesUnderAFolderAreInPathOrderWithoutTheFoldersABuildOrAnyRunWrites()
      throws IOException {
    write("settings.gradle.kts", "rootProject.name = \"x\"\n");
    write("core/build.gradle.kts", "plugins {}\n");
    write("a/c.java", "int c;\n");
    for (String folder :
        List.of(".git", ".gradle", ".kotlin", "build", "reports", "core/build", "core/.gradle")) {
      write(folder + "/x.java", "int x;\n");
    }
    write("buildx/y.java", "int y;\n");
    // A link to a folder is no file, and the walk does not follow it.
    Files.createSymbolicLink(root.resolve("linked"), root.resolve("a"));
    assertThat(TextFiles.under(root, root))
        .containsExactly(
            root.resolve("a/c.java"),
            root.resolve("buildx/y.java"),
            root.resolve("core/build.gradle.kts"),
            root.resolve("settings.gradle.kts"));
  }

  @Test
  void aFolderNamedLikeOneABuildWritesIsReadWhereNoGradleScriptStandsBesideIt() throws IOException {
    write("settings.gradle.kts", "rootProject.name = \"x\"\n");
    write("core/src/main/java/dev/reports/A.java", "int a;\n");
    write("core/src/main/java/dev/build/B.java", "int b;\n");
    write("core/reports/C.java", "int c;\n");
    assertThat(TextFiles.under(root, root))
        .containsExactly(
            root.resolve("core/reports/C.java"),
            root.resolve("core/src/main/java/dev/build/B.java"),
            root.resolve("core/src/main/java/dev/reports/A.java"),
            root.resolve("settings.gradle.kts"));
  }

  @Test
  void aBinaryFileIsNoTextWhereverItsNulByteIsButAFileInAnotherEncodingIsText() throws IOException {
    Files.write(root.resolve("wrapper.jar"), new byte[] {80, 75, 3, 4, 0, 1});
    Files.write(root.resolve("leading.bin"), new byte[] {0, 'a'});
    Files.write(root.resolve("latin1.txt"), new byte[] {'c', 'a', 'f', (byte) 0xe9});
    Files.write(root.resolve("utf16le.txt"), new byte[] {(byte) 0xff, (byte) 0xfe, 'a', 0});
    Files.write(root.resolve("utf16be.txt"), new byte[] {(byte) 0xfe, (byte) 0xff, 0, 'a'});
    Files.write(root.resolve("unmarked.bin"), new byte[] {(byte) 0xfe, 0, (byte) 0xff});
    write("ok.txt", "ok\n");
    assertThat(TextFiles.under(root, root))
        .containsExactly(
            root.resolve("latin1.txt"),
            root.resolve("ok.txt"),
            root.resolve("utf16be.txt"),
            root.resolve("utf16le.txt"));
  }

  @Test
  void aFolderOrAFileGivenInsideASkippedFolderIsReadAsGiven() throws IOException {
    write("settings.gradle.kts", "rootProject.name = \"x\"\n");
    write("build/C.java", "int c;\n");
    write("build/d/E.java", "int e;\n");
    assertThat(TextFiles.under(root, root.resolve("build")))
        .containsExactly(root.resolve("build/C.java"), root.resolve("build/d/E.java"));
    assertThat(TextFiles.under(root, root.resolve("build/C.java")))
        .containsExactly(root.resolve("build/C.java"));
    assertThat(TextFiles.under(root, root.resolve("build/d")))
        .containsExactly(root.resolve("build/d/E.java"));
  }

  @Test
  void aStartThatDoesNotExistOrAFileThatCannotBeReadIsAnError() throws IOException {
    assertThatThrownBy(() -> TextFiles.under(root, root.resolve("missing")))
        .isInstanceOf(NoSuchFileException.class);
    write("A.java", "int a;\n");
    assertThat(root.resolve("A.java").toFile().setReadable(false)).isTrue();
    try {
      assertThatThrownBy(() -> TextFiles.under(root, root))
          .isInstanceOf(UncheckedIOException.class);
    } finally {
      assertThat(root.resolve("A.java").toFile().setReadable(true)).isTrue();
    }
  }
}
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools.language;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

import java.util.List;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

class CommentsTest {

  private static List<List<String>> read(String path, String text) {
    return Comments.of(path, text.lines().toList());
  }

  @Test
  void eachFileKindHasItsCommentSyntax() {
    assertThat(Comments.kindOf("core/src/main/java/A.java")).isEqualTo(Comments.Kind.SLASH);
    assertThat(Comments.kindOf("build.gradle.kts")).isEqualTo(Comments.Kind.SLASH);
    assertThat(Comments.kindOf("config/checkstyle/checkstyle.xml")).isEqualTo(Comments.Kind.XML);
    assertThat(Comments.kindOf("README.md")).isEqualTo(Comments.Kind.MARKDOWN);
    assertThat(Comments.kindOf("core/src/main/resources/db/V1__init.sql"))
        .isEqualTo(Comments.Kind.SQL);
    for (String path :
        List.of(
            "a.yml",
            "a.yaml",
            "a.properties",
            "a.toml",
            "core/Dockerfile",
            ".gitignore",
            "verify")) {
      assertThat(Comments.kindOf(path)).as(path).isEqualTo(Comments.Kind.HASH);
    }
  }

  @Test
  void aJavaOrKotlinCommentIsALineCommentOrABlockCommentOverItsLines() {
    assertThat(read("A.java", "int a = 1; // why\n/* one\n   two */ int b;\nint c; /** three */\n"))
        .containsExactly(List.of(" why"), List.of(" one"), List.of("   two "), List.of("* three "));
    assertThat(read("A.kts", "/*\n * inner\n */\nval a = 1\n"))
        .containsExactly(List.of(""), List.of(" * inner"), List.of(" "), List.of());
  }

  @Test
  void stringsCharactersAndTextBlocksOpenNoComment() {
    String code =
        """
        String url = "https://x.test/a"; // after a string
        char slash = '/'; String glob = "src/**/*.java";
        String quoted = "a \\" // b";
        String block = \"""
            // not a comment
            \""";
        int after = 1; // after a text block
        val raw = \"""/* raw */\"""
        """;
    assertThat(read("A.java", code))
        .containsExactly(
            List.of(" after a string"),
            List.of(),
            List.of(),
            List.of(),
            List.of(),
            List.of(),
            List.of(" after a text block"),
            List.of());
  }

  @Test
  void anXmlCommentRunsToItsCloserOverLines() {
    assertThat(read("a.xml", "<a/> <!-- one -->\n<!--\n two\n-->\n<b/>\n"))
        .containsExactly(List.of(" one "), List.of(""), List.of(" two"), List.of(""), List.of());
  }

  @Test
  void everyLineOfMarkdownIsProseAndAHashStartsACommentAtTheStartOrAfterASpace() {
    assertThat(read("A.md", "# Title\ntext\n"))
        .containsExactly(List.of("# Title"), List.of("text"));
    assertThat(read("a.yml", "# top\nkey: value # why\nurl: a#b\n"))
        .containsExactly(List.of("# top"), List.of(" # why"), List.of());
  }

  @Test
  void anSqlCommentIsADoubleDashToTheEndOfTheLineOrABlockAndAStringHidesBoth() {
    assertThat(
            read(
                "V1.sql",
                "select 1; -- why\nselect '--', \"a--b\" /* one\ntwo */ from t; -- it's\n"))
        .containsExactly(List.of(" why"), List.of(" one"), List.of("two ", " it's"));
  }

  @Test
  void theCodeOfAJavaLineLeavesOutItsCommentsStringsAndTextBlocks() {
    assertThat(
            Comments.javaCode(
                List.of(
                    "int a = 1; // @Gone",
                    "String s = \"@Gone\" + 'x'; /* @Gone",
                    "still a comment */ int b; @Kept",
                    "String t = \"\"\"",
                    "  @Gone",
                    "  \"\"\"; @Kept")))
        .containsExactly(
            "int a = 1; ", "String s =  + ; ", " int b; @Kept", "String t = ", "", "; @Kept");
  }
}
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools.language;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

import java.util.List;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

class LanguageTest {

  // Banned samples are built from pieces and escapes, so this file passes the check it tests.
  private static final String VI = "Ti\u1ebfng Vi\u1ec7t";
  private static final List<String> RULINGS =
      List.of("R-" + "B15", "D-" + "B23", "FE-" + "23", "BK-" + "02", "RD-" + "13", "BE-" + "01");
  private static final List<String> TASKS =
      List.of("Task" + " 13", "Task" + " 6b", "Tasks" + " 3 and 4", "plan" + " two", "Plan" + " B");
  private static final String SPEC = "spec" + " 4.4";
  private static final String LETTER = "non-ascii-letter";
  private static final String MARK = "lang-" + "exception:";

  private static List<String> rules(String path, String text) {
    return Language.scan(path, text).stream()
        .map(problem -> problem.line() + ":" + problem.rule())
        .toList();
  }

  private static List<String> found(String sample) {
    return rules("A.java", "// " + sample + "\n");
  }

  private static void flagged(String rule, List<String> samples) {
    for (String sample : samples) {
      assertThat(found(sample)).as(sample).containsExactly("1:" + rule);
    }
  }

  private static void clean(List<String> samples) {
    for (String sample : samples) {
      assertThat(found(sample)).as(sample).isEmpty();
    }
  }

  @Test
  void flagsEveryLetterOutsideAsciiInAnyCaseOrScriptComposedOrDecomposed() {
    assertThat(rules("A.java", "// " + VI + "\nint a = 1;\n")).containsExactly("1:" + LETTER);
    assertThat(rules("A.java", "String a = \"" + VI + "\";\n")).containsExactly("1:" + LETTER);
    String decomposed = java.text.Normalizer.normalize(VI, java.text.Normalizer.Form.NFD);
    assertThat(decomposed).isNotEqualTo(VI);
    flagged(
        LETTER,
        List.of("Jos\u00e9 M\u00fcller", "\u0110\u00c0 N\u1eb4NG", "\u65e5\u672c", decomposed));
    assertThat(rules("a.yml", "# " + VI + "\n")).containsExactly("1:" + LETTER);
  }

  @Test
  void ignoresPunctuationAndSymbolsThatAreNotLetters() {
    assertThat(rules("A.java", "String a = \"+ 2 \u00b7 seen \u2318 \u00a9\";\n")).isEmpty();
  }

  @Test
  void aLangExceptionWithAReasonExcusesTheNextLineAndOnlyTheLetterRule() {
    String text =
        "// " + MARK + " a native name\nString a = \"" + VI + "\";\nString b = \"" + VI + "\";\n";
    assertThat(rules("A.java", text)).containsExactly("3:" + LETTER);
    assertThat(rules("A.java", "// " + MARK + " sample\n// " + RULINGS.getFirst() + "\n"))
        .containsExactly("2:plan-reference");
    assertThat(rules("A.java", "// lang-exception without the colon\nString a = \"" + VI + "\";\n"))
        .containsExactly("2:" + LETTER);
  }

  @Test
  void flagsRulingIdsTaskNumbersAndPlanNamesButKeepsBrdIds() {
    flagged("plan-reference", RULINGS);
    flagged("plan-reference", TASKS);
    flagged("plan-reference", List.of("ruling" + " 14", "Rulings" + " 3"));
    clean(
        List.of(
            "OVW-01 BR-24 D-19",
            "PR-B15 SFE-23 FE-23x Task 5th R-12",
            "a task queue, a plan of the trip"));
  }

  @Test
  void flagsSpecSectionNumbersInEveryForm() {
    flagged(
        "spec-reference",
        List.of(
            SPEC,
            "Spec" + " 3.2",
            "specs" + " 3.2",
            "spec" + " line 71",
            "spec" + " section 4.4",
            "spec" + " \u00a74.4",
            "see \u00a7" + "4.4",
            "per section" + " 4.4",
            "Section" + " 7"));
    clean(List.of("the spec says so", "the section on tiers"));
  }

  @Test
  void flagsALineOfAnotherFileButNotAPortOrAVersion() {
    flagged(
        "file-line",
        List.of(
            "Verify" + ".java:42",
            "see verify" + ".mjs:12",
            "application" + ".yml:3",
            "README" + ".md line 3",
            "a" + ".java lines 3"));
    clean(
        List.of(
            "http://127.0.0.1:8080", "version 1.2.3", "line 4 of the table", "core/Dockerfile"));
  }

  @Test
  void flagsDatesInComments() {
    flagged(
        "date", List.of("measured on 9" + " Oct 2026", "10" + " October 2026", "2026" + "-10-09"));
    clean(List.of("in Oct 2026, 2026-10 and version 2026.10.9"));
  }

  @Test
  void theReferenceRulesReadCommentsOnlySoProductTextInCodeAndDataPasses() {
    String date = "2026" + "-10-09";
    assertThat(rules("A.java", "String a = \"" + TASKS.getFirst() + " " + date + "\";\n"))
        .isEmpty();
    assertThat(rules("a.yml", "name: " + TASKS.getFirst() + "\n")).isEmpty();
    assertThat(rules("a.yml", "name: x # " + TASKS.getFirst() + "\n"))
        .containsExactly("1:plan-reference");
    assertThat(rules("A.md", TASKS.getFirst() + " added this\n"))
        .containsExactly("1:plan-reference");
    assertThat(rules("a.xml", "<a>" + TASKS.getFirst() + "</a> <!-- " + date + " -->\n"))
        .containsExactly("1:date");
  }

  @Test
  void reportsEachBrokenRuleOnceALineWithTheLineTrimmedAndCutAtAHundredCharacters() {
    List<Language.Problem> problems =
        Language.scan(
            "A.java", "   // " + SPEC + " " + RULINGS.getFirst() + " " + "x".repeat(200) + "\n");
    assertThat(problems)
        .extracting(Language.Problem::rule)
        .containsExactly("plan-reference", "spec-reference");
    assertThat(problems.getFirst().excerpt()).hasSize(100).startsWith("// spec");
    assertThat(problems.getFirst().line()).isEqualTo(1);
  }
}
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools.language;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThatThrownBy;

import dev.metis.tools.Facts;
import dev.metis.tools.TestContext;
import java.io.IOException;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.NoSuchFileException;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.io.TempDir;

class LanguageCommandTest {

  private static final String VI = "Ti\u1ebfng Vi\u1ec7t";
  private static final String RULING = "R-" + "B15";

  @TempDir Path root;

  private void tree(Map<String, String> files) throws IOException {
    for (Map.Entry<String, String> file : files.entrySet()) {
      Files.createDirectories(root.resolve(file.getKey()).getParent());
      Files.writeString(root.resolve(file.getKey()), file.getValue());
    }
  }

  private TestContext run(String... paths) throws IOException {
    TestContext test = new TestContext(root);
    test.exit = Language.command(test.context(), List.of(paths));
    return test;
  }

  @Test
  void theRepositoryIsCheckedWholeWhenNoPathIsGivenAndEachProblemNamesItsPlace()
      throws IOException {
    tree(
        Map.of(
            "core/src/A.java", "int a = 1;\n// " + VI + "\n",
            ".github/workflows/check.yml", "# " + RULING + "\n",
            "README.md", "Clean text.\n",
            "verify", "#!/bin/sh\n# " + VI + "\n"));
    TestContext test = run();
    assertThat(test.exit).isEqualTo(1);
    assertThat(test.printed().lines())
        .containsExactly(
            ".github/workflows/check.yml:1: plan-reference: # " + RULING,
            "core/src/A.java:2: non-ascii-letter: // " + VI,
            "verify:2: non-ascii-letter: # " + VI,
            "language: 3 problems in 3 files");
  }

  @Test
  void onlyThePathsGivenAreCheckedAndAPathInsideASkippedFolderStillCounts() throws IOException {
    tree(
        Map.of(
            "a/One.java", "// " + VI + "\n", "b/Two.java", "int b;\n", "build/C.java", "int c;\n"));
    TestContext some = run("b", "build/C.java");
    assertThat(some.exit).isZero();
    assertThat(some.printed()).isEqualTo("language: clean (2 files)\n");
  }

  @Test
  void pathsThatHoldNoFileToScanFailAndAPathThatDoesNotExistIsAnError() throws IOException {
    tree(Map.of("only/wrapper.jar", "PK\u0003\u0004\u0000"));
    Files.createDirectories(root.resolve("empty"));
    TestContext test = run("empty", "only");
    assertThat(test.exit).isEqualTo(1);
    assertThat(test.printed()).isEqualTo("language: error: no file to scan in empty only\n");
    assertThatThrownBy(() -> run("missing")).isInstanceOf(NoSuchFileException.class);
  }

  @Test
  void theTestsOfThisCheckHoldNothingItBansSoTheyNeedNoExemption() throws IOException {
    for (String test : List.of("LanguageTest", "LanguageCommandTest", "CommentsTest")) {
      Path source = Path.of("src/test/java/dev/metis/tools/language/" + test + ".java");
      assertThat(Language.scan("Other.java", Files.readString(source))).as(test).isEmpty();
    }
  }

  @Test
  void aFileThatIsNotUtf8IsAProblemAndTheFactsCountTheFiles() throws IOException {
    tree(Map.of("ok.yml", "a: 1\n"));
    TestContext clean = run();
    assertThat(clean.exit).isZero();
    assertThat(Facts.read(root, "language")).hasValue("1 files");
    Files.write(
        root.resolve("latin1.properties"), new byte[] {'#', ' ', 'c', 'a', 'f', (byte) 0xe9});
    Files.write(root.resolve("utf16.properties"), new byte[] {(byte) 0xff, (byte) 0xfe, '#', 0});
    TestContext test = run();
    assertThat(test.exit).isEqualTo(1);
    assertThat(test.printed().lines())
        .containsExactly(
            "latin1.properties:1: not-utf8: the file is not UTF-8",
            "utf16.properties:1: not-utf8: the file is not UTF-8",
            "language: 2 problems in 2 files");
  }
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools;

import static java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets.ISO_8859_1;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.io.UncheckedIOException;
import java.nio.file.FileVisitResult;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.nio.file.SimpleFileVisitor;
import java.nio.file.attribute.BasicFileAttributes;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Set;

/** The text files of a part of the repository, which the language and lint checks read. */
public final class TextFiles {

  // What Gradle writes beside a build script; a folder of the same name elsewhere is read.
  private static final Set<String> BUILT = Set.of(".gradle", ".kotlin", "build");

  private TextFiles() {}

  /**
   * The text files under the start, or the start itself, in path order; a binary file is none, nor
   * is git's folder, the record of ./verify at the root of the repository or what Gradle writes.
   */
  public static List<Path> under(Path root, Path start) throws IOException {
    List<Path> files = new ArrayList<>();
    Files.walkFileTree(
        start,
        new SimpleFileVisitor<>() {
          @Override
          public FileVisitResult preVisitDirectory(Path folder, BasicFileAttributes attributes) {
            return folder.equals(start) || !skipped(root, folder)
                ? FileVisitResult.CONTINUE
                : FileVisitResult.SKIP_SUBTREE;
          }

          @Override
          public FileVisitResult visitFile(Path file, BasicFileAttributes attributes) {
            if (Files.isRegularFile(file) && isText(file)) {
              files.add(file);
            }
            return FileVisitResult.CONTINUE;
          }
        });
    files.sort(null);
    return files;
  }

  private static boolean skipped(Path root, Path folder) {
    if (folder.equals(root.resolve(".git")) || folder.equals(root.resolve("reports"))) {
      return true;
    }
    return BUILT.contains(folder.getFileName().toString())
        && (Files.exists(folder.resolveSibling("build.gradle.kts"))
            || Files.exists(folder.resolveSibling("settings.gradle.kts")));
  }

  // A file is text unless it holds a NUL byte, or opens with the mark of UTF-16, which holds them;
  // the checks report a text in another encoding.
  private static boolean isText(Path file) {
    try {
      byte[] bytes = Files.readAllBytes(file);
      String opening = new String(bytes, ISO_8859_1);
      if (opening.startsWith("\u00fe\u00ff") || opening.startsWith("\u00ff\u00fe")) {
        return true;
      }
      for (byte b : bytes) {
        if (b == 0) {
          return false;
        }
      }
      return true;
    } catch (IOException unreadable) {
      throw new UncheckedIOException(unreadable);
    }
  }
}
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools.language;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.regex.Matcher;
import java.util.regex.Pattern;

// ponytail: it reads tokens, so a Kotlin template holding a quote misleads it; a parser lifts it.
/** The comments of a file, line by line, and the code of a Java file without them. */
public final class Comments {

  /** How a kind of file writes a comment. */
  enum Kind {
    SLASH,
    SQL,
    XML,
    MARKDOWN,
    HASH
  }

  // In a Java or Kotlin file a string or a text block may hold what opens a comment elsewhere.
  private static final Pattern SLASH_TOKEN =
      Pattern.compile("//|/\\*|\"\"\"|\"(?:\\\\.|[^\\\\\"])*\"|'(?:\\\\.|[^\\\\'])*'");
  // In SQL a string doubles its quote to hold one, and a quoted name may hold what opens a comment.
  private static final Pattern SQL_TOKEN =
      Pattern.compile("--|/\\*|'(?:[^']|'')*'|\"(?:[^\"]|\"\")*\"");
  private static final Pattern XML_TOKEN = Pattern.compile("<!--");
  private static final Pattern HASH = Pattern.compile("(^|\\s)#");

  private Comments() {}

  /** The kind of a file, by its name. */
  static Kind kindOf(String path) {
    if (path.endsWith(".java") || path.endsWith(".kts")) {
      return Kind.SLASH;
    }
    if (path.endsWith(".sql")) {
      return Kind.SQL;
    }
    if (path.endsWith(".xml")) {
      return Kind.XML;
    }
    return path.endsWith(".md") ? Kind.MARKDOWN : Kind.HASH;
  }

  /** The texts of the comments of each line; Markdown is prose, so a whole line counts. */
  static List<List<String>> of(String path, List<String> lines) {
    Kind kind = kindOf(path);
    Reader reader =
        new Reader(
            switch (kind) {
              case XML -> XML_TOKEN;
              case SQL -> SQL_TOKEN;
              default -> SLASH_TOKEN;
            });
    List<List<String>> comments = new ArrayList<>();
    for (String line : lines) {
      comments.add(
          switch (kind) {
            case MARKDOWN -> List.of(line);
            case HASH -> hashed(line);
            case SLASH, SQL, XML -> reader.read(line).comments();
          });
    }
    return comments;
  }

  /** The code of each line of a Java file: what is left without its comments and strings. */
  public static List<String> javaCode(List<String> lines) {
    Reader reader = new Reader(SLASH_TOKEN);
    List<String> code = new ArrayList<>();
    for (String line : lines) {
      code.add(reader.read(line).code());
    }
    return code;
  }

  private static List<String> hashed(String line) {
    Matcher hash = HASH.matcher(line);
    return hash.find() ? List.of(line.substring(hash.start())) : List.of();
  }

  /** The comments of one line, and the code around them, its strings left out. */
  private record Line(List<String> comments, String code) {}

  /** Reads a file one line at a time, carrying a block comment or a text block it left open. */
  private static final class Reader {

    private final Pattern tokens;
    private String closer = "";

    private Reader(Pattern tokens) {
      this.tokens = tokens;
    }

    private Line read(String line) {
      List<String> texts = new ArrayList<>();
      StringBuilder code = new StringBuilder();
      int at = 0;
      while (at >= 0) {
        at = closer.isEmpty() ? token(line, at, texts, code) : span(line, at, texts);
      }
      return new Line(texts, code.toString());
    }

    // From at to the closer of the open span, or to the end of the line; only a comment is kept.
    private int span(String line, int at, List<String> texts) {
      int end = line.indexOf(closer, at);
      if (!closer.equals("\"\"\"")) {
        texts.add(line.substring(at, end < 0 ? line.length() : end));
      }
      if (end < 0) {
        return -1;
      }
      int next = end + closer.length();
      closer = "";
      return next;
    }

    // The next token from at: a line comment ends the line, a block or a text block opens a span.
    private int token(String line, int at, List<String> texts, StringBuilder code) {
      Matcher token = tokens.matcher(line);
      if (!token.find(at)) {
        code.append(line, at, line.length());
        return -1;
      }
      code.append(line, at, token.start());
      switch (token.group()) {
        case "//", "--" -> {
          texts.add(line.substring(token.end()));
          return -1;
        }
        case "/*" -> closer = "*/";
        case "<!--" -> closer = "-->";
        case "\"\"\"" -> closer = "\"\"\"";
        default -> {
          // A string or a character, stepped over.
        }
      }
      return token.end();
    }
  }
}
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools.language;

import static java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets.UTF_8;

import dev.metis.tools.Context;
import dev.metis.tools.Facts;
import dev.metis.tools.TextFiles;
import java.io.IOException;
import java.io.PrintStream;
import java.nio.ByteBuffer;
import java.nio.charset.CharacterCodingException;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.text.Normalizer;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.LinkedHashMap;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.regex.Pattern;

/** English only, and no comment that cites what a maintainer cannot open, such as a ruling. */
public final class Language {

  /** One problem: the line, the rule it breaks and the start of the line. */
  record Problem(int line, String rule, String excerpt) {}

  static final String LETTER_RULE = "non-ascii-letter";
  // Built from pieces, so that this file holds no mark of its own.
  private static final String MARK = "lang-" + "exception:";
  private static final Pattern LETTER = Pattern.compile("(?![\\x00-\\x7F])\\p{L}");
  private static final String MONTH = "(?:Jan|Feb|Mar|Apr|May|Jun|Jul|Aug|Sep|Oct|Nov|Dec)[a-z]*";
  private static final String FILE = "(?:java|kts|kt|md|ya?ml|json|xml|toml|properties|m?js|ts|sh)";
  private static final Map<String, Pattern> REFERENCES = new LinkedHashMap<>();

  static {
    REFERENCES.put(
        "plan-reference",
        Pattern.compile(
            "\\b(?:R-[A-Z]\\d+|D-B\\d+|(?:FE|BK|RD|BE)-\\d+|Tasks? \\d+[A-Za-z]?"
                + "|[Pp]lan (?:[A-Z]|one|two|three|four)|[Rr]ulings? \\d+)\\b"));
    REFERENCES.put(
        "spec-reference",
        Pattern.compile(
            "\\bspecs?\\s+(?:(?:section|line)s?\\s+|\u00a7\\s*)?\\d+(?:\\.\\d+)*\\b"
                + "|\u00a7\\s*\\d|\\bsection \\d+(?:\\.\\d+)*",
            Pattern.CASE_INSENSITIVE));
    REFERENCES.put(
        "file-line", Pattern.compile("[\\w./-]+\\." + FILE + ":\\d+|\\." + FILE + " lines? \\d+"));
    REFERENCES.put(
        "date", Pattern.compile("\\b\\d{1,2} " + MONTH + " \\d{4}\\b|\\b\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}\\b"));
  }

  private Language() {}

  /** Checks the paths given, or the whole repository, and prints one line per problem. */
  public static int command(Context context, List<String> args) throws IOException {
    Path root = context.root();
    PrintStream out = context.out();
    List<Path> starts = args.isEmpty() ? List.of(root) : args.stream().map(root::resolve).toList();
    int files = 0;
    List<String> problems = new ArrayList<>();
    for (Path start : starts) {
      for (Path file : TextFiles.under(root, start)) {
        files++;
        String shown = root.relativize(file).toString();
        for (Problem problem : problemsOf(shown, Files.readAllBytes(file))) {
          problems.add(
              shown + ":" + problem.line() + ": " + problem.rule() + ": " + problem.excerpt());
        }
      }
    }
    problems.forEach(out::println);
    if (files == 0) {
      out.println("language: error: no file to scan in " + String.join(" ", args));
      return 1;
    }
    long touched =
        problems.stream().map(line -> line.substring(0, line.indexOf(':'))).distinct().count();
    String facts =
        problems.isEmpty()
            ? files + " files"
            : problems.size() + " problems in " + touched + " files";
    Facts.write(root, "language", facts);
    out.println(problems.isEmpty() ? "language: clean (" + facts + ")" : "language: " + facts);
    return problems.isEmpty() ? 0 : 1;
  }

  // A file in another encoding cannot be read for its letters, so it is a problem of its own.
  private static List<Problem> problemsOf(String path, byte[] bytes) {
    try {
      return scan(path, UTF_8.newDecoder().decode(ByteBuffer.wrap(bytes)).toString());
    } catch (CharacterCodingException notUtf8) {
      return List.of(new Problem(1, "not-utf8", "the file is not UTF-8"));
    }
  }

  /** The problems of a file's text; its path picks how its comments are read. */
  static List<Problem> scan(String path, String text) {
    List<String> lines = Normalizer.normalize(text, Normalizer.Form.NFC).lines().toList();
    List<List<String>> comments = Comments.of(path, lines);
    List<Problem> problems = new ArrayList<>();
    for (int at = 0; at < lines.size(); at++) {
      String line = lines.get(at);
      String excerpt = line.strip().substring(0, Math.min(100, line.strip().length()));
      boolean excused = at > 0 && lines.get(at - 1).contains(MARK);
      if (!excused && LETTER.matcher(line).find()) {
        problems.add(new Problem(at + 1, LETTER_RULE, excerpt));
      }
      for (Map.Entry<String, Pattern> rule : REFERENCES.entrySet()) {
        if (comments.get(at).stream().anyMatch(part -> rule.getValue().matcher(part).find())) {
          problems.add(new Problem(at + 1, rule.getKey(), excerpt));
        }
      }
    }
    return problems;
  }
}
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools.canary;

import java.util.List;

/** The counter-tests of the language check. */
final class LanguageCanaries {

  static final List<Canary> ALL =
      List.of(
          // The letters as escapes, so that this file stays English.
          Canary.of("language-vietnamese", "language", "non-ascii-letter")
              .writing(Canaries.CORE + "CanaryVietnamese.java", comment("Ti\u1ebfng Vi\u1ec7t")),
          Canary.of("language-ruling", "language", "plan-reference")
              .writing(
                  Canaries.CORE + "CanaryRuling.java",
                  comment("closes on select, as R-" + "B15 says")),
          Canary.of("language-date", "language", ": date: ")
              .writing(Canaries.CORE + "CanaryDate.java", comment("measured on 9 Oct" + " 2026")),
          // A migration, whose comments open with two dashes.
          Canary.of("language-sql-date", "language", "V0__canary.sql:1: date")
              .writing(
                  "core/src/main/resources/db/migration/V0__canary.sql",
                  "-- measured on 9 Oct" + " 2026\nselect 1;\n"));

  private LanguageCanaries() {}

  // A class of the core whose only comment is the text.
  private static String comment(String text) {
    return """
        package dev.metis.core;

        // %s
        final class Canary {}
        """
        .formatted(text);
  }
}
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools;

import dev.metis.tools.canary.CanaryRun;
import dev.metis.tools.language.Language;
import dev.metis.tools.verify.Verify;
import java.io.IOException;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import org.jspecify.annotations.Nullable;

/** The commands of the tool of the checks. */
public final class Cli {

  private static final Map<String, Command> COMMANDS =
      Map.of(
          "verify", Verify::command,
          "canary", CanaryRun::command,
          "language", Language::command);

  private static final String USAGE =
      """
      usage: verify [--only <check>[,<check>]] [--fast] [--append]
             canary <name>|all
             language [<path> ...]""";

  private Cli() {}

  /** Runs the command the arguments name and returns its exit code. */
  public static int run(Context context, List<String> args) throws IOException {
    @Nullable Command command = args.isEmpty() ? null : COMMANDS.get(args.getFirst());
    if (command == null) {
      context.out().println(USAGE);
      return 2;
    }
    return command.run(context, args.subList(1, args.size()));
  }
}
```

`tools/build.gradle.kts`:

```kotlin
plugins {
    id("metis.java-conventions")
    application
}

application {
    mainClass = "dev.metis.tools.Main"
}

dependencies {
    implementation("tools.jackson.core:jackson-core")
    implementation("tools.jackson.core:jackson-databind")
}

// A command of the tool, run from the repository root, for a check of the root build to depend on.
fun tool(name: String, vararg arguments: String) =
    tasks.register<JavaExec>(name) {
        classpath = sourceSets.main.get().runtimeClasspath
        mainClass = application.mainClass
        workingDir = rootDir
        args(*arguments)
    }

tool("language", "language")

// ./verify and ./canary start the tool with the Java and the classpath this task writes, and the tool
// learns from it the check tasks Gradle has in every project, however a build file declares them.
val launcher = tasks.register("launcher") {
    val executable = javaToolchains.launcherFor(java.toolchain).map { it.executablePath.asFile.path }
    val classpath = sourceSets.main.map { it.runtimeClasspath }
    val checks = rootProject.allprojects.flatMap { project ->
        val prefix = if (project == rootProject) "" else project.path + ":"
        project.tasks.names.filter { it.matches(Regex("check[A-Z]\\w*")) }.map { prefix + it }
    }
    val folder = layout.buildDirectory.dir("launcher")
    inputs.files(classpath)
    inputs.property("java", executable)
    inputs.property("checks", checks)
    outputs.dir(folder)
    doLast {
        folder.get().file("java").asFile.writeText(executable.get() + "\n")
        folder.get().file("args").asFile.writeText("-cp\n\"" + classpath.get().asPath + "\"\n")
        folder.get().file("checks").asFile.writeText(checks.joinToString("") { "$it\n" })
    }
}
```

`build.gradle.kts`:

```kotlin
plugins {
    alias(libs.plugins.spotless)
}

dependencyLocking {
    lockAllConfigurations()
}

spotless {
    java {
        target("core/src/**/*.java", "tools/src/**/*.java")
        googleJavaFormat(libs.versions.google.java.format.get())
        removeUnusedImports()
    }
    format("misc") {
        target(
            "**/*.kts", "**/*.md", "**/*.yml", "**/*.yaml", "**/*.toml", "**/*.properties",
            "**/*.json", "**/*.xml", "**/*.txt", "**/Dockerfile", "**/.gitignore", ".dockerignore",
            "verify", "canary",
        )
        targetExclude("**/build/**", "**/.gradle/**", "**/.kotlin/**", "gradle/verification-metadata.xml")
        trimTrailingWhitespace()
        endWithNewline()
    }
}

// The checks of ./verify, which runs them in the order of the list of the tool, Checks.ORDER.

tasks.register("checkFormat") {
    description = "Every source file is formatted."
    dependsOn("spotlessCheck")
}

tasks.register("checkCompile") {
    description = "The code compiles with every warning an error, no bug pattern and no null where none is allowed."
    dependsOn(":core:compileJava", ":core:compileTestJava", ":tools:compileJava", ":tools:compileTestJava")
}

tasks.register("checkLanguage") {
    description = "English only, and no comment that cites a plan, a ruling, a task, a date or a line of a file."
    dependsOn(":tools:language")
}

// A check whose judge did not run would pass on the exit of its tasks alone, so a check that owes
// facts fails without them; ./verify and ./canary clear the facts before each run of a check.
val factFree = setOf("checkFormat", "checkCompile", "checkDeps", "checkSecrets")
tasks.matching { it.name.matches(Regex("check[A-Z]\\w*")) && it.name !in factFree }.configureEach {
    val check = name.removePrefix("check").replaceFirstChar(Char::lowercase)
    val facts = layout.buildDirectory.file("facts/$check.txt")
    doLast {
        if (!facts.get().asFile.exists()) {
            throw GradleException("$name: its judge left no facts in build/facts/$check.txt")
        }
    }
}
```

### Task 9: The lint check

Checkstyle 14.3.0 with two modules only: a cyclomatic complexity of at most 10 per method and at most 300 lines per file. The command `marks` checks every escape hatch of the repository: each `@SuppressWarnings`, each annotation whose name ends in `DoNotMutate`, each annotation whose name holds `Generated` or is `CoverageIgnore` (JaCoCo and PIT leave out what they mark), anywhere in the code of a Java line, a parameter included, and each `lang-exception:` and each line of `config/coverage-exclusions.txt`, carries a reason, and their counts equal `config/debt.json`, so a new one shows in the change that adds it and a removed one must lower the file. The exclusion list keeps one class of every project at least, since coverage and mutation testing would measure nothing of a project it emptied. The one debt of the plan: `dev.metis.tools.Main` is left out of coverage, since it exits the JVM and `MainTest` runs it as a process (Task 13 and Task 14 apply the list).

```kotlin
import net.ltgt.gradle.errorprone.errorprone
import org.gradle.api.tasks.testing.logging.TestExceptionFormat

plugins {
    java
    checkstyle
    id("net.ltgt.errorprone")
    id("info.solidsoft.pitest")
}

val catalog = the<VersionCatalogsExtension>().named("libs")

// Half the cores, so that tests and mutation testing never take the whole machine.
val half = (Runtime.getRuntime().availableProcessors() / 2).coerceAtLeast(1)

java {
    toolchain {
        languageVersion = JavaLanguageVersion.of(25)
        vendor = JvmVendorSpec.AMAZON
    }
}

dependencyLocking {
    lockAllConfigurations()
    lockMode = LockMode.STRICT
}

dependencies {
    implementation(platform(catalog.findLibrary("spring-boot-bom").get()))
    implementation(platform(catalog.findLibrary("jackson-bom").get()))
    constraints {
        for (tomcat in listOf("tomcat-embed-core", "tomcat-embed-el", "tomcat-embed-websocket")) {
            implementation(catalog.findLibrary(tomcat).get())
        }
    }
    compileOnly("org.jspecify:jspecify")
    testCompileOnly("org.jspecify:jspecify")
    errorprone(catalog.findLibrary("errorprone-core").get())
    errorprone(catalog.findLibrary("nullaway").get())
    testImplementation(platform(catalog.findLibrary("junit-bom").get()))
    testImplementation("org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter-api")
    testImplementation("org.assertj:assertj-core")
    testRuntimeOnly("org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter-engine")
    testRuntimeOnly("org.junit.platform:junit-platform-launcher")
}

tasks.withType<JavaCompile>().configureEach {
    options.compilerArgs.addAll(listOf("-Xlint:all", "-Werror"))
    options.errorprone {
        error("UnusedVariable", "UnusedMethod", "UnusedNestedClass", "NullAway")
        option("NullAway:OnlyNullMarked", "true")
    }
}

// A new seed on every run, printed, so that a test that depends on another one shows, and the run can be repeated.
val testSeed = providers.gradleProperty("testSeed").getOrElse(System.nanoTime().toString())

tasks.withType<Test>().configureEach {
    useJUnitPlatform()
    maxParallelForks = half
    // Every check runs its tests anew and no old report stays; coverage pays by running them again.
    dependsOn("clean${name.replaceFirstChar(Char::uppercase)}")
    systemProperty("junit.jupiter.testclass.order.default", "org.junit.jupiter.api.ClassOrderer\$Random")
    systemProperty("junit.jupiter.testmethod.order.default", "org.junit.jupiter.api.MethodOrderer\$Random")
    systemProperty("junit.jupiter.execution.order.random.seed", testSeed)
    testLogging {
        exceptionFormat = TestExceptionFormat.FULL
    }
    doFirst {
        logger.lifecycle("Test order seed $testSeed: repeat it with -PtestSeed=$testSeed")
    }
}

checkstyle {
    toolVersion = catalog.findVersion("checkstyle").get().requiredVersion
    configDirectory = rootProject.layout.projectDirectory.dir("config/checkstyle")
}

pitest {
    pitestVersion = catalog.findVersion("pitest").get().requiredVersion
    junit5PluginVersion = catalog.findVersion("pitest-junit5").get().requiredVersion
    targetClasses = setOf("dev.metis.${project.name}.*")
    targetTests = setOf("dev.metis.${project.name}.*")
    mutators = setOf("STRONGER")
    threads = half
    outputFormats = setOf("XML", "HTML")
    timestampedReports = false
}
```
