```java
package dev.metis.tools.lint;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

import dev.metis.tools.Facts;
import dev.metis.tools.TestContext;
import java.io.IOException;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.util.List;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.BeforeEach;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.io.TempDir;

class MarksTest {

  // The marks are built from pieces, so that this file holds none of its own.
  private static final String SUPPRESS = "@Suppress" + "Warnings";
  private static final String MUTATE = "@Do" + "NotMutate";
  private static final String GENERATED = "@Gene" + "rated";
  private static final String LANG = "lang-" + "exception:";

  @TempDir Path root;

  @BeforeEach
  void config() throws IOException {
    write("config/coverage-exclusions.txt", "# A class no test can run in process.\n");
    debt(0, 0, 0, 0, 0);
  }

  private void write(String path, String text) throws IOException {
    Files.createDirectories(root.resolve(path).getParent());
    Files.writeString(root.resolve(path), text);
  }

  private void debt(int suppressions, int mutations, int generated, int languages, int exclusions)
      throws IOException {
    write(
        "config/debt.json",
        """
        {"SuppressWarnings": %d, "DoNotMutate": %d, "Generated": %d, "lang-exception": %d,
         "coverage-exclusion": %d}
        """
            .formatted(suppressions, mutations, generated, languages, exclusions));
  }

  private TestContext lint() throws IOException {
    TestContext test = new TestContext(root);
    test.exit = Marks.command(test.context(), List.of());
    return test;
  }

  @Test
  void everyMarkWithItsReasonAndADebtThatHoldsItsCountIsClean() throws IOException {
    write(
        "core/A.java",
        "class A {\n  " + SUPPRESS + "(\"unused\") // read by reflection\n  int a;\n}\n");
    write(
        "core/B.java",
        "class B {\n  " + MUTATE + "(reason = \"no behaviour to observe\")\n  void b() {}\n}\n");
    write(
        "core/C.java",
        GENERATED
            + " // written by a generator\nclass C {\n  int c("
            + SUPPRESS
            + "(\"x\") int x) {"
            + " // read by reflection\n    return x;\n  }\n}\n");
    write("README.md", "<!-- " + LANG + " a native name -->\n");
    write(
        "config/coverage-exclusions.txt", "# Classes.\n\ndev.metis.tools.Main: the process edge\n");
    debt(2, 1, 1, 1, 1);
    TestContext test = lint();
    assertThat(test.exit).isZero();
    assertThat(test.printed()).isEqualTo("lint: clean (6 marks)\n");
    assertThat(Facts.read(root, "lint")).hasValue("6 marks");
  }

  @Test
  void aMarkWithoutItsReasonIsAProblemOfItsLine() throws IOException {
    write(
        "core/A.java",
        "class A {\n  " + SUPPRESS + "(\"unused\")\n  int a;\n  " + SUPPRESS + "(\"x\") //  \n}\n");
    write("core/B.java", "class B {\n  " + MUTATE + "(reason = \" \")\n  void b() {}\n}\n");
    write("core/C.java", "class C {\n  int c(" + SUPPRESS + "(\"x\") int x) { return x; }\n}\n");
    write(
        "core/D.java",
        "@org.springframework.aot.generate" + GENERATED.substring(1) + "\nclass D {}\n");
    write("a.yml", "# " + LANG + "\n");
    write("config/coverage-exclusions.txt", "dev.metis.tools.Main\ndev.metis.tools.Other:\n");
    debt(3, 1, 1, 1, 2);
    TestContext test = lint();
    assertThat(test.exit).isEqualTo(1);
    assertThat(test.printed().lines())
        .containsExactly(
            "a.yml:1: no-reason: # " + LANG,
            "config/coverage-exclusions.txt:1: no-reason: dev.metis.tools.Main",
            "config/coverage-exclusions.txt:2: no-reason: dev.metis.tools.Other:",
            "core/A.java:2: no-reason: " + SUPPRESS + "(\"unused\")",
            "core/A.java:4: no-reason: " + SUPPRESS + "(\"x\") //",
            "core/B.java:2: no-reason: " + MUTATE + "(reason = \" \")",
            "core/C.java:2: no-reason: int c(" + SUPPRESS + "(\"x\") int x) { return x; }",
            "core/D.java:1: no-reason: @org.springframework.aot.generate" + GENERATED.substring(1),
            "lint: 8 problems");
  }

  @Test
  void aCountAboveOrBelowItsDebtIsAProblemSoTheDebtFileChangesInTheSameChange() throws IOException {
    write(
        "core/A.java",
        "class A {\n  " + SUPPRESS + "(\"unused\") // read by reflection\n  int a;\n}\n");
    debt(0, 1, 0, 0, 0);
    TestContext test = lint();
    assertThat(test.exit).isEqualTo(1);
    assertThat(test.printed().lines())
        .containsExactly(
            "config/debt.json: debt-grew: 1 SuppressWarnings, the debt file holds 0",
            "config/debt.json: debt-shrank: 0 DoNotMutate, the debt file holds 1: lower it",
            "lint: 2 problems");
  }

  @Test
  void aMarkInAStringOrACommentIsNoMarkButAMentionOfTheLanguageMarkIsOne() throws IOException {
    write(
        "core/A.java",
        "class A {\n  String s = \""
            + SUPPRESS
            + "\"; // "
            + GENERATED
            + "\n  /* "
            + MUTATE
            + " */\n  String t = \"\"\"\n    "
            + SUPPRESS
            + "(\"x\")\n    \"\"\";\n}\n");
    write("settings.gradle.kts", "rootProject.name = \"x\"\n");
    write("build/C.java", SUPPRESS + "(\"x\")\n");
    write("Notes.kts", SUPPRESS + "(\"x\")\n" + MUTATE + "(reason = \" \")\n");
    write("notes.md", "Write a " + LANG + " reason on the line above.\n");
    Files.write(root.resolve("latin1.properties"), new byte[] {'#', ' ', (byte) 0xe9});
    debt(0, 0, 0, 1, 0);
    assertThat(lint().printed()).isEqualTo("lint: clean (1 marks)\n");
  }

  @Test
  void anExclusionListThatLeavesOutEveryProductionClassOfAProjectIsAProblem() throws IOException {
    write("core/src/main/java/dev/metis/core/A.java", "class A {}\n");
    write("core/src/main/java/dev/metis/core/B.java", "class B {}\n");
    write("core/src/main/java/dev/metis/core/package-info.java", "package dev.metis.core;\n");
    write("core/src/test/java/dev/metis/core/ATest.java", "class ATest {}\n");
    write("tools/src/main/java/dev/metis/tools/Main.java", "class Main {}\n");
    write("tools/src/main/java/dev/metis/tools/Cli.java", "class Cli {}\n");
    String some = "dev.metis.core.A: a reason\ndev.metis.tools.Main: a reason\n";
    write("config/coverage-exclusions.txt", some);
    debt(0, 0, 0, 0, 2);
    assertThat(lint().printed()).isEqualTo("lint: clean (2 marks)\n");
    write("config/coverage-exclusions.txt", some + "dev.metis.core.B: a reason\n");
    debt(0, 0, 0, 0, 3);
    TestContext test = lint();
    assertThat(test.exit).isEqualTo(1);
    assertThat(test.printed().lines())
        .containsExactly(
            "config/coverage-exclusions.txt: whole-project: every class of core is left out",
            "lint: 1 problems");
  }

  @Test
  void aDebtFileWithoutACountOfAKindIsAProblem() throws IOException {
    write("config/debt.json", "{\"SuppressWarnings\": 0}\n");
    TestContext test = lint();
    assertThat(test.exit).isEqualTo(1);
    assertThat(test.printed().lines())
        .containsExactly(
            "config/debt.json: no-count: DoNotMutate",
            "config/debt.json: no-count: Generated",
            "config/debt.json: no-count: lang-exception",
            "config/debt.json: no-count: coverage-exclusion",
            "lint: 4 problems");
  }
}
```

`tools/src/main/java/dev/metis/tools/lint/Marks.java`:

```java
package dev.metis.tools.lint;

import static java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets.UTF_8;

import dev.metis.tools.Context;
import dev.metis.tools.Facts;
import dev.metis.tools.TextFiles;
import dev.metis.tools.language.Comments;
import java.io.IOException;
import java.io.PrintStream;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.HashSet;
import java.util.LinkedHashMap;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.Set;
import java.util.TreeMap;
import java.util.regex.Matcher;
import java.util.regex.Pattern;
import tools.jackson.databind.JsonNode;
import tools.jackson.databind.json.JsonMapper;

/** Every escape hatch gives its reason, and their counts equal the debt file, so none slips in. */
public final class Marks {

  static final List<String> KINDS =
      List.of(
          "SuppressWarnings", "DoNotMutate", "Generated", "lang-exception", "coverage-exclusion");

  private static final String DEBT = "config/debt.json";
  private static final String EXCLUSIONS = "config/coverage-exclusions.txt";
  // Found anywhere in the code of a line, so a mark on a parameter or after a modifier counts too.
  private static final Pattern SUPPRESSED =
      Pattern.compile("@(?:java\\.lang\\.)?SuppressWarnings\\b");
  private static final Pattern UNMUTATED = Pattern.compile("@(?:[\\w$]+\\.)*\\w*DoNotMutate\\b");
  // JaCoCo leaves out what an annotation whose name holds Generated marks, and PIT CoverageIgnore.
  private static final Pattern GENERATED =
      Pattern.compile("@(?:[\\w$]+\\.)*(?:\\w*Generated\\w*|CoverageIgnore)\\b");
  // Built from pieces, so that this file holds no mark of its own.
  private static final String EXCUSED = "lang-" + "exception:";
  private static final Pattern COMMENT_REASON = Pattern.compile("//\\s*\\S");
  private static final Pattern MUTATION_REASON = Pattern.compile("reason\\s*=\\s*\"\\s*[^\\s\"]");
  private static final Pattern LANGUAGE_REASON = Pattern.compile(EXCUSED + "\\s*\\S");
  private static final Pattern EXCLUSION = Pattern.compile("^[\\w.$]+:\\s*\\S");
  // A class of a project: the folder of the project, then the path of the class in it.
  private static final Pattern PRODUCTION = Pattern.compile("(.+)/src/main/java/(.+)\\.java");

  private Marks() {}

  /** Checks every mark of the repository against its reason and its debt. */
  public static int command(Context context, List<String> args) throws IOException {
    Path root = context.root();
    PrintStream out = context.out();
    Map<String, Integer> counts = new LinkedHashMap<>();
    KINDS.forEach(kind -> counts.put(kind, 0));
    List<String> problems = new ArrayList<>();
    List<Path> files = TextFiles.under(root, root);
    for (Path file : files) {
      String shown = root.relativize(file).toString();
      // Marks are plain ASCII, so a file in another encoding is read for them all the same; the
      // language check reports every file that is not UTF-8.
      List<String> lines = new String(Files.readAllBytes(file), UTF_8).lines().toList();
      List<String> code = Comments.javaCode(lines);
      for (int at = 0; at < lines.size(); at++) {
        String line = lines.get(at);
        for (Mark mark : marksOf(shown, line, code.get(at))) {
          counts.merge(mark.kind(), 1, Integer::sum);
          if (!mark.reasoned()) {
            problems.add(shown + ":" + (at + 1) + ": no-reason: " + line.strip());
          }
        }
      }
    }
    problems.addAll(wholeProjects(root, files));
    problems.addAll(debtProblems(root, counts));
    problems.forEach(out::println);
    int marks = counts.values().stream().mapToInt(Integer::intValue).sum();
    Facts.write(root, "lint", marks + " marks");
    out.println(
        problems.isEmpty()
            ? "lint: clean (" + marks + " marks)"
            : "lint: " + problems.size() + " problems");
    return problems.isEmpty() ? 0 : 1;
  }

  private record Mark(String kind, boolean reasoned) {}

  private static List<Mark> marksOf(String path, String line, String code) {
    List<Mark> marks = new ArrayList<>();
    if (path.endsWith(".java")) {
      boolean commented = COMMENT_REASON.matcher(line).find();
      boolean reasoned = MUTATION_REASON.matcher(line).find();
      SUPPRESSED
          .matcher(code)
          .results()
          .forEach(on -> marks.add(new Mark(KINDS.get(0), commented)));
      UNMUTATED.matcher(code).results().forEach(on -> marks.add(new Mark(KINDS.get(1), reasoned)));
      GENERATED.matcher(code).results().forEach(on -> marks.add(new Mark(KINDS.get(2), commented)));
    }
    if (line.contains(EXCUSED)) {
      marks.add(new Mark(KINDS.get(3), LANGUAGE_REASON.matcher(line).find()));
    }
    if (path.equals(EXCLUSIONS) && !line.isBlank() && !line.startsWith("#")) {
      marks.add(new Mark(KINDS.get(4), EXCLUSION.matcher(line).find()));
    }
    return marks;
  }

  // Coverage and mutation testing measure nothing of a project whose every class the list leaves
  // out, so the list keeps one class of each project at least.
  private static List<String> wholeProjects(Path root, List<Path> files) throws IOException {
    Set<String> excluded = new HashSet<>();
    for (String line : Files.readAllLines(root.resolve(EXCLUSIONS))) {
      excluded.add(line.replaceFirst(":.*", "").strip());
    }
    Map<String, Set<String>> classes = new TreeMap<>();
    for (Path file : files) {
      Matcher production = PRODUCTION.matcher(root.relativize(file).toString());
      if (production.matches() && !production.group(2).endsWith("-info")) {
        classes
            .computeIfAbsent(production.group(1), project -> new HashSet<>())
            .add(production.group(2).replace('/', '.'));
      }
    }
    List<String> problems = new ArrayList<>();
    classes.forEach(
        (project, names) -> {
          if (excluded.containsAll(names)) {
            problems.add(
                EXCLUSIONS + ": whole-project: every class of " + project + " is left out");
          }
        });
    return problems;
  }

  private static List<String> debtProblems(Path root, Map<String, Integer> counts)
      throws IOException {
    JsonNode debt = JsonMapper.builder().build().readTree(Files.readString(root.resolve(DEBT)));
    List<String> problems = new ArrayList<>();
    counts.forEach(
        (kind, count) -> {
          JsonNode held = debt.path(kind);
          if (!held.isIntegralNumber()) {
            problems.add(DEBT + ": no-count: " + kind);
          } else if (count > held.intValue()) {
            problems.add(
                "%s: debt-grew: %d %s, the debt file holds %d"
                    .formatted(DEBT, count, kind, held.intValue()));
          } else if (count < held.intValue()) {
            problems.add(
                "%s: debt-shrank: %d %s, the debt file holds %d: lower it"
                    .formatted(DEBT, count, kind, held.intValue()));
          }
        });
    return problems;
  }
}
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools.canary;

import java.util.List;
import java.util.stream.Collectors;
import java.util.stream.IntStream;

/** The counter-tests of the lint check. */
final class LintCanaries {

  // Built from pieces, so that this file holds no mark of its own.
  private static final String SUPPRESS = "@Suppress" + "Warnings(\"unused\")";

  static final List<Canary> ALL =
      List.of(
          // Ten branches over the one path of a method pass the ceiling of 10.
          Canary.of("lint-complexity", "lint", "[CyclomaticComplexity]")
              .writing(
                  Canaries.CORE + "CanaryComplex.java",
                  classOf(
                      "CanaryComplex",
                      "  static int grade(int n) {\n"
                          + IntStream.range(0, 10)
                              .mapToObj(
                                  i ->
                                      "    if (n > %d) {\n      return %d;\n    }\n"
                                          .formatted(i, i))
                              .collect(Collectors.joining())
                          + "    return -1;\n  }\n")),
          // A file of 301 lines passes the ceiling of 300.
          Canary.of("lint-file-length", "lint", "[FileLength]")
              .writing(
                  Canaries.CORE + "CanaryLong.java",
                  classOf(
                      "CanaryLong",
                      IntStream.range(0, 295)
                          .mapToObj(i -> "  static final int N%d = %d;\n".formatted(i, i))
                          .collect(Collectors.joining()))),
          Canary.of("lint-no-reason", "lint", "no-reason")
              .writing(
                  Canaries.CORE + "CanarySuppressed.java",
                  classOf("CanarySuppressed", "  " + SUPPRESS + "\n  private int idle;\n")),
          // A mark with its reason still has to be counted in the debt file.
          Canary.of("lint-debt", "lint", "debt-grew")
              .writing(
                  Canaries.CORE + "CanaryCounted.java",
                  classOf(
                      "CanaryCounted",
                      "  " + SUPPRESS + " // read by reflection\n  private int idle;\n")),
          // A mark on a parameter, which no line starts with.
          Canary.of("lint-parameter-suppression", "lint", "no-reason: static int twice(")
              .writing(
                  Canaries.CORE + "CanaryParameter.java",
                  classOf(
                      "CanaryParameter",
                      "  static int twice("
                          + SUPPRESS
                          + " int number) {\n    return number * 2;\n  }\n")),
          // JaCoCo and PIT leave out a class so marked, so the mark is counted like the others.
          Canary.of("lint-generated", "lint", "debt-grew: 1 Generated")
              .writing(
                  Canaries.CORE + "CanaryGenerated.java",
                  """
                  package dev.metis.core;

                  @org.springframework.aot.generate.Generated
                  final class CanaryGenerated {
                    private CanaryGenerated() {}
                  }
                  """),
          // A mark in a package named like the record of ./verify, which only the root holds.
          Canary.of("lint-nested-reports", "lint", "reports/CanaryReports.java:6: no-reason")
              .writing(
                  Canaries.CORE + "reports/CanaryReports.java",
                  classOf("CanaryReports", "  " + SUPPRESS + "\n  private int idle;\n")
                      .replace("package dev.metis.core;", "package dev.metis.core.reports;")),
          // An exclusion of the one class of the core, which would leave the core unmeasured.
          Canary.of("lint-whole-project-excluded", "lint", "every class of core is left out")
              .appending(
                  "config/coverage-exclusions.txt", "dev.metis.core.CoreApplication: a canary\n"));

  private LintCanaries() {}

  // A class of the core with the body given, and a private constructor before it.
  private static String classOf(String name, String body) {
    return """
        package dev.metis.core;

        final class %s {
          private %s() {}

        %s}
        """
        .formatted(name, name, body);
  }
}
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools.canary;

import java.util.List;
import java.util.stream.Stream;

/** Every counter-test, in the order ./canary all runs them. */
public final class Canaries {

  /** The folder of the core's own classes, where most canaries plant a class. */
  static final String CORE = "core/src/main/java/dev/metis/core/";

  /** Every counter-test, one list per check. */
  public static final List<Canary> ALL =
      Stream.of(FormatCanaries.ALL, CompileCanaries.ALL, LintCanaries.ALL, LanguageCanaries.ALL)
          .flatMap(List::stream)
          .toList();

  private Canaries() {}
}
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools;

import dev.metis.tools.canary.CanaryRun;
import dev.metis.tools.language.Language;
import dev.metis.tools.lint.Marks;
import dev.metis.tools.verify.Verify;
import java.io.IOException;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import org.jspecify.annotations.Nullable;

/** The commands of the tool of the checks. */
public final class Cli {

  private static final Map<String, Command> COMMANDS =
      Map.of(
          "verify", Verify::command,
          "canary", CanaryRun::command,
          "language", Language::command,
          "marks", Marks::command);

  private static final String USAGE =
      """
      usage: verify [--only <check>[,<check>]] [--fast] [--append]
             canary <name>|all
             language [<path> ...]
             marks""";

  private Cli() {}

  /** Runs the command the arguments name and returns its exit code. */
  public static int run(Context context, List<String> args) throws IOException {
    @Nullable Command command = args.isEmpty() ? null : COMMANDS.get(args.getFirst());
    if (command == null) {
      context.out().println(USAGE);
      return 2;
    }
    return command.run(context, args.subList(1, args.size()));
  }
}
```

`tools/build.gradle.kts`:

```kotlin
plugins {
    id("metis.java-conventions")
    application
}

application {
    mainClass = "dev.metis.tools.Main"
}

dependencies {
    implementation("tools.jackson.core:jackson-core")
    implementation("tools.jackson.core:jackson-databind")
}

// A command of the tool, run from the repository root, for a check of the root build to depend on.
fun tool(name: String, vararg arguments: String) =
    tasks.register<JavaExec>(name) {
        classpath = sourceSets.main.get().runtimeClasspath
        mainClass = application.mainClass
        workingDir = rootDir
        args(*arguments)
    }

tool("language", "language")
tool("marks", "marks")

// ./verify and ./canary start the tool with the Java and the classpath this task writes, and the tool
// learns from it the check tasks Gradle has in every project, however a build file declares them.
val launcher = tasks.register("launcher") {
    val executable = javaToolchains.launcherFor(java.toolchain).map { it.executablePath.asFile.path }
    val classpath = sourceSets.main.map { it.runtimeClasspath }
    val checks = rootProject.allprojects.flatMap { project ->
        val prefix = if (project == rootProject) "" else project.path + ":"
        project.tasks.names.filter { it.matches(Regex("check[A-Z]\\w*")) }.map { prefix + it }
    }
    val folder = layout.buildDirectory.dir("launcher")
    inputs.files(classpath)
    inputs.property("java", executable)
    inputs.property("checks", checks)
    outputs.dir(folder)
    doLast {
        folder.get().file("java").asFile.writeText(executable.get() + "\n")
        folder.get().file("args").asFile.writeText("-cp\n\"" + classpath.get().asPath + "\"\n")
        folder.get().file("checks").asFile.writeText(checks.joinToString("") { "$it\n" })
    }
}
```

`build.gradle.kts`:

```kotlin
plugins {
    alias(libs.plugins.spotless)
}

dependencyLocking {
    lockAllConfigurations()
}

spotless {
    java {
        target("core/src/**/*.java", "tools/src/**/*.java")
        googleJavaFormat(libs.versions.google.java.format.get())
        removeUnusedImports()
    }
    format("misc") {
        target(
            "**/*.kts", "**/*.md", "**/*.yml", "**/*.yaml", "**/*.toml", "**/*.properties",
            "**/*.json", "**/*.xml", "**/*.txt", "**/Dockerfile", "**/.gitignore", ".dockerignore",
            "verify", "canary",
        )
        targetExclude("**/build/**", "**/.gradle/**", "**/.kotlin/**", "gradle/verification-metadata.xml")
        trimTrailingWhitespace()
        endWithNewline()
    }
}

// The checks of ./verify, which runs them in the order of the list of the tool, Checks.ORDER.

tasks.register("checkFormat") {
    description = "Every source file is formatted."
    dependsOn("spotlessCheck")
}

tasks.register("checkCompile") {
    description = "The code compiles with every warning an error, no bug pattern and no null where none is allowed."
    dependsOn(":core:compileJava", ":core:compileTestJava", ":tools:compileJava", ":tools:compileTestJava")
}

tasks.register("checkLint") {
    description = "No method above a complexity of 10, no file above 300 lines, a reason on every mark."
    dependsOn(
        ":core:checkstyleMain", ":core:checkstyleTest", ":tools:checkstyleMain", ":tools:checkstyleTest",
        ":tools:marks",
    )
}

tasks.register("checkLanguage") {
    description = "English only, and no comment that cites a plan, a ruling, a task, a date or a line of a file."
    dependsOn(":tools:language")
}

// A check whose judge did not run would pass on the exit of its tasks alone, so a check that owes
// facts fails without them; ./verify and ./canary clear the facts before each run of a check.
val factFree = setOf("checkFormat", "checkCompile", "checkDeps", "checkSecrets")
tasks.matching { it.name.matches(Regex("check[A-Z]\\w*")) && it.name !in factFree }.configureEach {
    val check = name.removePrefix("check").replaceFirstChar(Char::lowercase)
    val facts = layout.buildDirectory.file("facts/$check.txt")
    doLast {
        if (!facts.get().asFile.exists()) {
            throw GradleException("$name: its judge left no facts in build/facts/$check.txt")
        }
    }
}
```

### Task 10: The test judge, the network guard, the tooling check and the unit check

Neither Gradle nor JUnit fails on a skipped test, so the command `tests` reads the XML reports of a test task: every test passed, none skipped, failed or in error, and the number that passed equals the floor of the check in `test-floor.json` exactly, in both directions. `Xml` reads a report with DTDs and external entities refused. The network guard: a `java.net.spi.InetAddressResolverProvider` in `test-support/`, which both test source sets include, resolves only the local host and the name of the machine, so a unit test cannot reach the network by name or look an address up off the machine. `TestOrderTest`, run by both test tasks, proves that JUnit receives the random order and its seed. `CanariesTest`, one of the tool's tests, reads the check tasks Gradle has from the launcher's list and fails a check that the tool's list lacks, or that has neither a counter-test nor a reason in `NoCanary.REASONS` (empty today). The checks: `checkTooling` (the tool's tests and their floor) and `checkUnit` (the core's tests and their floor).

**Files:**

`build-logic/src/main/kotlin/metis.java-conventions.gradle.kts`:

```kotlin
import net.ltgt.gradle.errorprone.errorprone
import org.gradle.api.tasks.testing.logging.TestExceptionFormat

plugins {
    java
    checkstyle
    id("net.ltgt.errorprone")
    id("info.solidsoft.pitest")
}

val catalog = the<VersionCatalogsExtension>().named("libs")

// Half the cores, so that tests and mutation testing never take the whole machine.
val half = (Runtime.getRuntime().availableProcessors() / 2).coerceAtLeast(1)

java {
    toolchain {
        languageVersion = JavaLanguageVersion.of(25)
        vendor = JvmVendorSpec.AMAZON
    }
}

dependencyLocking {
    lockAllConfigurations()
    lockMode = LockMode.STRICT
}

// The tests of both projects share one guard against calls that leave the machine.
sourceSets.named("test") {
    java.srcDir(rootProject.layout.projectDirectory.dir("test-support/java"))
    resources.srcDir(rootProject.layout.projectDirectory.dir("test-support/resources"))
}

dependencies {
    implementation(platform(catalog.findLibrary("spring-boot-bom").get()))
    implementation(platform(catalog.findLibrary("jackson-bom").get()))
    constraints {
        for (tomcat in listOf("tomcat-embed-core", "tomcat-embed-el", "tomcat-embed-websocket")) {
            implementation(catalog.findLibrary(tomcat).get())
        }
    }
    compileOnly("org.jspecify:jspecify")
    testCompileOnly("org.jspecify:jspecify")
    errorprone(catalog.findLibrary("errorprone-core").get())
    errorprone(catalog.findLibrary("nullaway").get())
    testImplementation(platform(catalog.findLibrary("junit-bom").get()))
    testImplementation("org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter-api")
    testImplementation("org.assertj:assertj-core")
    testRuntimeOnly("org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter-engine")
    testRuntimeOnly("org.junit.platform:junit-platform-launcher")
}

tasks.withType<JavaCompile>().configureEach {
    options.compilerArgs.addAll(listOf("-Xlint:all", "-Werror"))
    options.errorprone {
        error("UnusedVariable", "UnusedMethod", "UnusedNestedClass", "NullAway")
        option("NullAway:OnlyNullMarked", "true")
    }
}

// A new seed on every run, printed, so that a test that depends on another one shows, and the run can be repeated.
val testSeed = providers.gradleProperty("testSeed").getOrElse(System.nanoTime().toString())

tasks.withType<Test>().configureEach {
    useJUnitPlatform()
    maxParallelForks = half
    // Every check runs its tests anew and no old report stays; coverage pays by running them again.
    dependsOn("clean${name.replaceFirstChar(Char::uppercase)}")
    systemProperty("junit.jupiter.testclass.order.default", "org.junit.jupiter.api.ClassOrderer\$Random")
    systemProperty("junit.jupiter.testmethod.order.default", "org.junit.jupiter.api.MethodOrderer\$Random")
    systemProperty("junit.jupiter.execution.order.random.seed", testSeed)
    testLogging {
        exceptionFormat = TestExceptionFormat.FULL
    }
    doFirst {
        logger.lifecycle("Test order seed $testSeed: repeat it with -PtestSeed=$testSeed")
    }
}

checkstyle {
    toolVersion = catalog.findVersion("checkstyle").get().requiredVersion
    configDirectory = rootProject.layout.projectDirectory.dir("config/checkstyle")
}

pitest {
    pitestVersion = catalog.findVersion("pitest").get().requiredVersion
    junit5PluginVersion = catalog.findVersion("pitest-junit5").get().requiredVersion
    targetClasses = setOf("dev.metis.${project.name}.*")
    targetTests = setOf("dev.metis.${project.name}.*")
    mutators = setOf("STRONGER")
    threads = half
    outputFormats = setOf("XML", "HTML")
    timestampedReports = false
}
```

`test-support/java/dev/metis/testsupport/LocalHostOnlyTest.java`:

```java
package dev.metis.testsupport;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThatThrownBy;

import java.net.InetAddress;
import java.net.UnknownHostException;
import java.net.spi.InetAddressResolver;
import java.net.spi.InetAddressResolver.LookupPolicy;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.stream.Stream;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

class LocalHostOnlyTest {

  @Test
  void aTestCannotResolveAHostOnTheNetwork() {
    assertThatThrownBy(() -> InetAddress.getAllByName("example.com"))
        .isInstanceOf(UnknownHostException.class)
        .hasMessage("example.com: a test resolves the local host only");
  }

  @Test
  void theLocalHostResolvesByItsNameAndByTheNameOfThisMachine() throws UnknownHostException {
    assertThat(InetAddress.getAllByName("localhost"))
        .allSatisfy(address -> assertThat(address.isLoopbackAddress()).isTrue());
    String machine = InetAddress.getLocalHost().getHostName();
    assertThat(InetAddress.getAllByName(machine)).isNotEmpty();
  }

  @Test
  void aReverseLookupOffThisMachineFailsBeforeTheBuiltinResolverIsAsked()
      throws UnknownHostException {
    List<String> asked = new ArrayList<>();
    InetAddressResolver builtin =
        new InetAddressResolver() {
          @Override
          public Stream<InetAddress> lookupByName(String host, LookupPolicy policy) {
            asked.add(host);
            return Stream.empty();
          }

          @Override
          public String lookupByAddress(byte[] address) {
            asked.add("by address");
            return "localhost";
          }
        };
    LocalResolver resolver = new LocalResolver(builtin, "machine");
    assertThatThrownBy(() -> resolver.lookupByAddress(new byte[] {(byte) 192, 0, 2, 1}))
        .isInstanceOf(UnknownHostException.class)
        .hasMessage("a test looks up the local host only");
    assertThat(asked).isEmpty();
    assertThat(resolver.lookupByAddress(new byte[] {127, 0, 0, 1})).isEqualTo("localhost");
    assertThat(resolver.lookupByName("machine", LookupPolicy.of(LookupPolicy.IPV4))).isEmpty();
    assertThat(asked).containsExactly("by address", "machine");
  }
}
```

```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

// The conventions hand JUnit a random order and its seed; a lost key would run tests in one order.
class TestOrderTest {

  @Test
  void theTestsRunInARandomOrderOfClassesAndMethodsFromThePrintedSeed() {
    assertThat(System.getProperty("junit.jupiter.testclass.order.default"))
        .isEqualTo("org.junit.jupiter.api.ClassOrderer$Random");
    assertThat(System.getProperty("junit.jupiter.testmethod.order.default"))
        .isEqualTo("org.junit.jupiter.api.MethodOrderer$Random");
    assertThat(System.getProperty("junit.jupiter.execution.order.random.seed")).matches("-?\\d+");
  }
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThatThrownBy;

import java.io.ByteArrayOutputStream;
import java.io.IOException;
import java.io.PrintStream;
import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.io.TempDir;

class XmlTest {

  @TempDir Path dir;

  @Test
  void aReportIsReadWithItsDoctypeButWithoutLoadingAnything() throws IOException {
    Path report = dir.resolve("report.xml");
    Files.writeString(
        report,
        """
        <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
        <!DOCTYPE report PUBLIC "-//JACOCO//DTD Report 1.1//EN" "http://nowhere.test/report.dtd">
        <report name="core"><counter type="LINE" missed="0" covered="3"/></report>
        """);
    assertThat(Xml.read(report).getDocumentElement().getAttribute("name")).isEqualTo("core");
  }

  @Test
  void anEntityIsNeverExpandedAndAMalformedFileIsAnError() throws IOException {
    Path entity = dir.resolve("entity.xml");
    Files.writeString(
        entity,
        """
        <?xml version="1.0"?>
        <!DOCTYPE a [<!ENTITY secret SYSTEM "file:///etc/passwd">]>
        <a>&secret;</a>
        """);
    assertThatThrownBy(() -> Xml.read(entity)).isInstanceOf(IOException.class);
    Path broken = dir.resolve("broken.xml");
    Files.writeString(broken, "<a>");
    assertThatThrownBy(() -> Xml.read(broken))
        .isInstanceOf(IOException.class)
        .hasMessageStartingWith("broken.xml is no XML: ");
  }

  @Test
  void aMalformedFilePrintsNothingOfItsOwnSinceTheErrorCarriesTheMessage() throws IOException {
    Path broken = dir.resolve("broken.xml");
    Files.writeString(broken, "<a>");
    PrintStream before = System.err;
    ByteArrayOutputStream printed = new ByteArrayOutputStream();
    System.setErr(new PrintStream(printed, true, StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
    try {
      assertThatThrownBy(() -> Xml.read(broken)).isInstanceOf(IOException.class);
    } finally {
      System.setErr(before);
    }
    assertThat(printed.toString(StandardCharsets.UTF_8)).isEmpty();
  }
}
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools.tests;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

import dev.metis.tools.Facts;
import dev.metis.tools.TestContext;
import java.io.IOException;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.util.List;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.BeforeEach;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.io.TempDir;

class TestReportsTest {

  private static final String RESULTS = "core/build/test-results/test";

  @TempDir Path root;

  @BeforeEach
  void floor() throws IOException {
    Files.writeString(root.resolve("test-floor.json"), "{\"unit\": 5, \"tooling\": 2}\n");
  }

  private void report(String dir, String name, int tests, int skipped, int failures, int errors)
      throws IOException {
    Files.createDirectories(root.resolve(dir));
    Files.writeString(
        root.resolve(dir).resolve("TEST-" + name + ".xml"),
        """
        <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
        <testsuite name="%s" tests="%d" skipped="%d" failures="%d" errors="%d">
          <properties/>
        </testsuite>
        """
            .formatted(name, tests, skipped, failures, errors));
  }

  private TestContext judge(String check, String... dirs) throws IOException {
    TestContext test = new TestContext(root);
    List<String> args = new java.util.ArrayList<>(List.of(check));
    args.addAll(List.of(dirs));
    test.exit = TestReports.command(test.context(), args);
    return test;
  }

  @Test
  void theCountsOfEveryReportOfEveryFolderAddUpAndPassedEqualsTheFloor() throws IOException {
    report(RESULTS, "a.ATest", 3, 0, 0, 0);
    report(RESULTS, "a.BTest", 1, 0, 0, 0);
    report("tools/build/test-results/test", "c.CTest", 1, 0, 0, 0);
    Files.writeString(root.resolve(RESULTS).resolve("output.bin"), "not a report");
    TestContext test = judge("unit", RESULTS, "tools/build/test-results/test");
    assertThat(test.exit).isZero();
    assertThat(test.printed()).isEqualTo("tests: 5 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped\n");
    assertThat(Facts.read(root, "unit")).contains("5 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped");
  }

  @Test
  void aSkippedTestAFailedOneOrAPassCountOtherThanTheFloorIsRedAndTheFactsSayWhy()
      throws IOException {
    report(RESULTS, "a.ATest", 6, 1, 1, 1);
    TestContext test = judge("unit", RESULTS);
    assertThat(test.exit).isEqualTo(1);
    String facts =
        "3 passed, 2 failed, 1 skipped: failed tests, skipped tests,"
            + " passed 3, floor 5: update test-floor.json";
    assertThat(test.printed()).isEqualTo("tests: " + facts + "\n");
    assertThat(Facts.read(root, "unit")).contains(facts);
  }

  @Test
  void theFloorIsExactSoOneTestMoreThanItIsRedToo() throws IOException {
    report(RESULTS, "a.ATest", 6, 0, 0, 0);
    TestContext test = judge("unit", RESULTS);
    assertThat(test.exit).isEqualTo(1);
    assertThat(test.printed())
        .isEqualTo(
            "tests: 6 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped: passed 6, floor 5: update test-floor.json\n");
  }

  @Test
  void aCheckWithoutAFloorIsRed() throws IOException {
    report(RESULTS, "a.ATest", 5, 0, 0, 0);
    TestContext test = judge("architecture", RESULTS);
    assertThat(test.exit).isEqualTo(1);
    assertThat(test.printed())
        .isEqualTo("tests: 5 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped: no floor in test-floor.json\n");
  }

  @Test
  void noReportAMissingFolderOrAMalformedReportIsRedAndLeavesNoFacts() throws IOException {
    Files.createDirectories(root.resolve(RESULTS));
    TestContext none = judge("unit", RESULTS, "missing/folder");
    assertThat(none.exit).isEqualTo(1);
    assertThat(none.printed())
        .isEqualTo("tests: no test report in " + RESULTS + " missing/folder\n");
    Files.writeString(root.resolve(RESULTS).resolve("TEST-broken.xml"), "<testsuite");
    TestContext broken = judge("unit", RESULTS);
    assertThat(broken.exit).isEqualTo(1);
    assertThat(broken.printed()).startsWith("tests: TEST-broken.xml is no XML: ");
    assertThat(Facts.read(root, "unit")).isEmpty();
  }

  @Test
  void withoutACheckAndAFolderItPrintsItsUsage() throws IOException {
    TestContext test = judge("unit");
    assertThat(test.exit).isEqualTo(2);
    assertThat(test.printed()).isEqualTo("usage: tests <check> <folder of test reports> ...\n");
  }
}
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools.canary;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

import dev.metis.tools.verify.Checks;
import java.io.IOException;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.util.HashSet;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Set;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

// The rules of the counter-tests, read on the check tasks Gradle has, so a check cannot go blind.
class CanariesTest {

  private static final Path ROOT = Path.of("..");

  // The checks of the root build as Gradle names them, whether the tool's list holds them or not.
  private static List<String> checks() throws IOException {
    return Checks.tasks(ROOT).stream()
        .filter(task -> !task.startsWith(":"))
        .map(task -> Character.toLowerCase(task.charAt(5)) + task.substring(6))
        .toList();
  }

  @Test
  void everyCheckGradleHasIsOneOfTheToolsList() throws IOException {
    assertThat(Checks.of(Checks.tasks(ROOT))).hasSameSizeAs(checks());
  }

  @Test
  void everyCheckHasACounterTestOrAReasonInNoCanaryAndNoneHasBoth() throws IOException {
    Set<String> proven = new HashSet<>();
    Canaries.ALL.forEach(canary -> proven.add(canary.check()));
    List<String> problems =
        checks().stream()
            .filter(check -> proven.contains(check) == NoCanary.REASONS.containsKey(check))
            .map(check -> check + " has neither a counter-test nor a reason in NoCanary, or both")
            .toList();
    assertThat(problems).isEmpty();
  }

  @Test
  void everyCounterTestAndEveryReasonNamesACheckOfTheBuild() throws IOException {
    List<String> checks = checks();
    assertThat(Canaries.ALL).allSatisfy(canary -> assertThat(checks).contains(canary.check()));
    assertThat(NoCanary.REASONS.keySet()).allSatisfy(check -> assertThat(checks).contains(check));
  }

  @Test
  void everyCounterTestHasANameOfItsOwn() {
    assertThat(Canaries.ALL.stream().map(Canary::name)).doesNotHaveDuplicates();
  }

  @Test
  void everyFileACounterTestChangesIsAFileOfTheRepositoryAndHoldsTheTextItReplaces()
      throws IOException {
    for (Canary canary : Canaries.ALL) {
      for (String file : canary.appends().keySet()) {
        assertThat(ROOT.resolve(file)).as(canary.name()).isRegularFile();
      }
      for (String file : canary.deletes()) {
        assertThat(ROOT.resolve(file)).as(canary.name()).isRegularFile();
      }
      for (Canary.Replacement swap : canary.replacements()) {
        assertThat(Files.readString(ROOT.resolve(swap.path())))
            .as(canary.name())
            .contains(swap.text());
      }
    }
  }
}
```

```java
package dev.metis.testsupport;

import java.net.InetAddress;
import java.net.UnknownHostException;
import java.net.spi.InetAddressResolver;
import java.util.stream.Stream;

/** The resolver of the tests: the local host by its names, and a loopback address back to one. */
final class LocalResolver implements InetAddressResolver {

  private final InetAddressResolver builtin;
  private final String machine;

  LocalResolver(InetAddressResolver builtin, String machine) {
    this.builtin = builtin;
    this.machine = machine;
  }

  @Override
  public Stream<InetAddress> lookupByName(String host, LookupPolicy policy)
      throws UnknownHostException {
    if (host.equals("localhost") || host.equals(machine)) {
      return builtin.lookupByName(host, policy);
    }
    throw new UnknownHostException(host + ": a test resolves the local host only");
  }

  @Override
  public String lookupByAddress(byte[] address) throws UnknownHostException {
    if (!InetAddress.getByAddress(address).isLoopbackAddress()) {
      throw new UnknownHostException("a test looks up the local host only");
    }
    return builtin.lookupByAddress(address);
  }
}
```

```java
package dev.metis.testsupport;

import java.net.spi.InetAddressResolver;
import java.net.spi.InetAddressResolverProvider;

// ponytail: a written-out address needs no resolver; a test network without a route lifts it.
/** Resolves the local host only, so that no test reaches the network by a name. */
public final class LocalHostOnly extends InetAddressResolverProvider {

  @Override
  public InetAddressResolver get(Configuration configuration) {
    return new LocalResolver(configuration.builtinResolver(), configuration.lookupLocalHostName());
  }

  @Override
  public String name() {
    return "local host only";
  }
}
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import javax.xml.XMLConstants;
import javax.xml.parsers.DocumentBuilder;
import javax.xml.parsers.DocumentBuilderFactory;
import javax.xml.parsers.ParserConfigurationException;
import org.w3c.dom.Document;
import org.xml.sax.SAXException;
import org.xml.sax.helpers.DefaultHandler;

/** Reads the XML reports of the build: test results, coverage and mutation testing. */
public final class Xml {

  private Xml() {}

  /** The document of a report; it never loads a DTD or anything else a report names. */
  public static Document read(Path file) throws IOException {
    try {
      DocumentBuilderFactory factory = DocumentBuilderFactory.newInstance();
      // A report names its DTD, which it does not need, and an entity of a file must stay unread.
      factory.setFeature("http://apache.org/xml/features/nonvalidating/load-external-dtd", false);
      factory.setAttribute(XMLConstants.ACCESS_EXTERNAL_DTD, "");
      DocumentBuilder builder = factory.newDocumentBuilder();
      // The default handler would print every error before the parser throws it.
      builder.setErrorHandler(new DefaultHandler());
      return builder.parse(file.toFile());
    } catch (SAXException | ParserConfigurationException malformed) {
      throw new IOException(
          file.getFileName() + " is no XML: " + malformed.getMessage(), malformed);
    }
  }
}
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools.tests;

import dev.metis.tools.Context;
import dev.metis.tools.Facts;
import dev.metis.tools.Xml;
import java.io.IOException;
import java.io.PrintStream;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.stream.Stream;
import org.w3c.dom.Element;
import tools.jackson.databind.JsonNode;
import tools.jackson.databind.json.JsonMapper;

/** Gradle and JUnit pass a skipped test, so this judge reads the reports against an exact floor. */
public final class TestReports {

  private static final String USAGE = "usage: tests <check> <folder of test reports> ...";

  private TestReports() {}

  /** Judges the reports in the folders for the check, and leaves its facts. */
  public static int command(Context context, List<String> args) throws IOException {
    PrintStream out = context.out();
    if (args.size() < 2) {
      out.println(USAGE);
      return 2;
    }
    Path root = context.root();
    String check = args.getFirst();
    List<String> folders = args.subList(1, args.size());
    List<Path> reports = reportsIn(root, folders);
    if (reports.isEmpty()) {
      out.println("tests: no test report in " + String.join(" ", folders));
      return 1;
    }
    int[] counts = new int[3];
    try {
      for (Path report : reports) {
        Element suite = Xml.read(report).getDocumentElement();
        int skipped = count(suite, "skipped");
        int failed = count(suite, "failures") + count(suite, "errors");
        counts[0] += count(suite, "tests") - skipped - failed;
        counts[1] += failed;
        counts[2] += skipped;
      }
    } catch (IOException | NumberFormatException malformed) {
      out.println("tests: " + malformed.getMessage());
      return 1;
    }
    List<String> reasons = reasonsOf(root, check, counts);
    String facts = "%d passed, %d failed, %d skipped".formatted(counts[0], counts[1], counts[2]);
    String judged = reasons.isEmpty() ? facts : facts + ": " + String.join(", ", reasons);
    Facts.write(root, check, judged);
    out.println("tests: " + judged);
    return reasons.isEmpty() ? 0 : 1;
  }

  private static List<Path> reportsIn(Path root, List<String> folders) throws IOException {
    List<Path> reports = new ArrayList<>();
    for (String folder : folders) {
      Path dir = root.resolve(folder);
      if (Files.isDirectory(dir)) {
        try (Stream<Path> files = Files.list(dir)) {
          files
              .filter(file -> file.getFileName().toString().matches("TEST-.*\\.xml"))
              .sorted()
              .forEach(reports::add);
        }
      }
    }
    return reports;
  }

  private static int count(Element suite, String attribute) {
    return Integer.parseInt(suite.getAttribute(attribute));
  }

  // Exact, so the change that adds or removes tests updates the floor in the same diff.
  private static List<String> reasonsOf(Path root, String check, int[] counts) throws IOException {
    JsonNode floor =
        JsonMapper.builder().build().readTree(Files.readString(root.resolve("test-floor.json")));
    JsonNode held = floor.path(check);
    List<String> reasons = new ArrayList<>();
    if (counts[1] > 0) {
      reasons.add("failed tests");
    }
    if (counts[2] > 0) {
      reasons.add("skipped tests");
    }
    if (!held.isIntegralNumber()) {
      reasons.add("no floor in test-floor.json");
    } else if (counts[0] != held.intValue()) {
      reasons.add(
          "passed %d, floor %d: update test-floor.json".formatted(counts[0], held.intValue()));
    }
    return reasons;
  }
}
```

```java
              .appending("build.gradle.kts", "\ntasks.register(\"checkCanary\")\n"),
          // A check registered in a project other than the root, which ./verify must see too.
          Canary.of("tooling-subproject-check", "tooling", ":core:checkIntegration")
              .appending("core/build.gradle.kts", "\ntasks.register(\"checkIntegration\")\n"),
          // A check registered with a type, which a reader of the text of the build would miss.
          Canary.of("tooling-typed-check", "tooling", "typed has neither a counter-test")
              .appending(
                  "build.gradle.kts",
                  "\ntasks.register<Exec>(\"checkTyped\") { commandLine(\"true\") }\n"));

  private ToolingCanaries() {}
}
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools.canary;

import java.util.List;

/** The counter-tests of the unit check. */
final class UnitCanaries {

  private static final String TESTS = "core/src/test/java/dev/metis/core/";

  static final List<Canary> ALL =
      List.of(
          Canary.of("unit-failing", "unit", "CanaryFailingTest > one() FAILED")
              .writing(TESTS + "CanaryFailingTest.java", test("CanaryFailingTest", "", "2")),
          Canary.of("unit-disabled", "unit", "skipped tests")
              .writing(
                  TESTS + "CanaryDisabledTest.java",
                  test("CanaryDisabledTest", "  @org.junit.jupiter.api.Disabled\n", "1")),
          // A test deleted without lowering the floor, which only the exact floor notices.
          Canary.of("unit-floor", "unit", "update test-floor.json")
              .deleting(TESTS + "ShutdownTest.java"),
          // A test check without its judge, which would pass skipped tests on the exit of Gradle.
          Canary.of("unit-no-judge", "unit", "checkUnit: its judge left no facts")
              .replacing(
                  "build.gradle.kts",
                  "dependsOn(\":core:test\", \":tools:judgeUnit\")",
                  "dependsOn(\":core:test\")"),
          // A setting of the order lost, so the methods would run in one order.
          Canary.of("unit-fixed-order", "unit", "TestOrderTest >")
              .replacing(
                  "build-logic/src/main/kotlin/metis.java-conventions.gradle.kts",
                  "    systemProperty(\"junit.jupiter.testmethod.order.default\","
                      + " \"org.junit.jupiter.api.MethodOrderer\\$Random\")\n",
                  ""),
          // An endpoint of the actuator more than health, which the API must not answer.
          Canary.of("unit-exposed-endpoint", "unit", "ProbesTest > theDiscoveryPage")
              .appending(
                  "core/src/main/resources/application.yml",
                  "management:\n  endpoints:\n    web:\n      exposure:\n        include: health,env\n"));

  private UnitCanaries() {}

  // A test class of the core with one test, which asserts that one parses to the number given.
  private static String test(String name, String annotation, String expected) {
    return """
        package dev.metis.core;

        import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

        import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

        class %s {

          @Test
        %s  void one() {
            assertThat(Integer.parseInt("1")).isEqualTo(%s);
          }
        }
        """
        .formatted(name, annotation, expected);
  }
}
```

```java
import dev.metis.tools.tests.TestReports;
import dev.metis.tools.verify.Verify;
import java.io.IOException;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import org.jspecify.annotations.Nullable;

/** The commands of the tool of the checks. */
public final class Cli {

  private static final Map<String, Command> COMMANDS =
      Map.of(
          "verify", Verify::command,
          "canary", CanaryRun::command,
          "language", Language::command,
          "marks", Marks::command,
          "tests", TestReports::command);

  private static final String USAGE =
      """
      usage: verify [--only <check>[,<check>]] [--fast] [--append]
             canary <name>|all
             language [<path> ...]
             marks
             tests <check> <folder of test reports> ...""";

  private Cli() {}

  /** Runs the command the arguments name and returns its exit code. */
  public static int run(Context context, List<String> args) throws IOException {
    @Nullable Command command = args.isEmpty() ? null : COMMANDS.get(args.getFirst());
    if (command == null) {
      context.out().println(USAGE);
      return 2;
    }
    return command.run(context, args.subList(1, args.size()));
  }
}
```

```kotlin
plugins {
    id("metis.java-conventions")
    application
}

application {
    mainClass = "dev.metis.tools.Main"
}

dependencies {
    implementation("tools.jackson.core:jackson-core")
    implementation("tools.jackson.core:jackson-databind")
}

// A command of the tool, run from the repository root, for a check of the root build to depend on.
fun tool(name: String, vararg arguments: String) =
    tasks.register<JavaExec>(name) {
        classpath = sourceSets.main.get().runtimeClasspath
        mainClass = application.mainClass
        workingDir = rootDir
        args(*arguments)
    }

tool("language", "language")
tool("marks", "marks")
// The judges of the test tasks, which run after the tests even when a test failed.
tool("judgeTooling", "tests", "tooling", "tools/build/test-results/test").configure { mustRunAfter(tasks.test) }
tool("judgeUnit", "tests", "unit", "core/build/test-results/test").configure { mustRunAfter(":core:test") }

// ./verify and ./canary start the tool with the Java and the classpath this task writes, and the tool
// learns from it the check tasks Gradle has in every project, however a build file declares them.
val launcher = tasks.register("launcher") {
    val executable = javaToolchains.launcherFor(java.toolchain).map { it.executablePath.asFile.path }
    val classpath = sourceSets.main.map { it.runtimeClasspath }
    val checks = rootProject.allprojects.flatMap { project ->
        val prefix = if (project == rootProject) "" else project.path + ":"
        project.tasks.names.filter { it.matches(Regex("check[A-Z]\\w*")) }.map { prefix + it }
    }
    val folder = layout.buildDirectory.dir("launcher")
    inputs.files(classpath)
    inputs.property("java", executable)
    inputs.property("checks", checks)
    outputs.dir(folder)
    doLast {
        folder.get().file("java").asFile.writeText(executable.get() + "\n")
        folder.get().file("args").asFile.writeText("-cp\n\"" + classpath.get().asPath + "\"\n")
        folder.get().file("checks").asFile.writeText(checks.joinToString("") { "$it\n" })
    }
}

// The tests of the counter-tests read the list of checks the launcher writes.
tasks.named("testClasses") { dependsOn(launcher) }
```

```kotlin
// The checks of ./verify, which runs them in the order of the list of the tool, Checks.ORDER.

    description = "Every source file is formatted."
    dependsOn("spotlessCheck")
}

tasks.register("checkCompile") {
    description = "The code compiles with every warning an error, no bug pattern and no null where none is allowed."
    dependsOn(":core:compileJava", ":core:compileTestJava", ":tools:compileJava", ":tools:compileTestJava")
}

tasks.register("checkLint") {
    description = "No method above a complexity of 10, no file above 300 lines, a reason on every mark."
    dependsOn(
        ":core:checkstyleMain", ":core:checkstyleTest", ":tools:checkstyleMain", ":tools:checkstyleTest",
        ":tools:marks",
    )
}

tasks.register("checkLanguage") {
    description = "English only, and no comment that cites a plan, a ruling, a task, a date or a line of a file."
    dependsOn(":tools:language")
}

tasks.register("checkTooling") {
    description = "The tests of the tool pass, and every check has a counter-test."
    dependsOn(":tools:test", ":tools:judgeTooling")
}

tasks.register("checkUnit") {
    description = "The tests of the core that need no container pass, none skipped, as many as the floor."
    dependsOn(":core:test", ":tools:judgeUnit")
}

// A check whose judge did not run would pass on the exit of its tasks alone, so a check that owes
// facts fails without them; ./verify and ./canary clear the facts before each run of a check.
val factFree = setOf("checkFormat", "checkCompile", "checkDeps", "checkSecrets")
tasks.matching { it.name.matches(Regex("check[A-Z]\\w*")) && it.name !in factFree }.configureEach {
    val check = name.removePrefix("check").replaceFirstChar(Char::lowercase)
    val facts = layout.buildDirectory.file("facts/$check.txt")
    doLast {
        if (!facts.get().asFile.exists()) {
            throw GradleException("$name: its judge left no facts in build/facts/$check.txt")
        }
    }
}
```

### Task 11: The architecture check

ArchUnit 1.5.1 on JUnit 6 (`archunit-junit6`), with the rules that already have something to check. In `core`: no field injection, no read of the system clock or the system time zone (no clock bean exists yet, so the rule forbids them all), no standard output or error, every package `@NullMarked`, no legacy date types. In `tools`: every package `@NullMarked` and no legacy date types; the tool reads the clock and prints through its context. The rules are tests tagged `architecture`, which the test task leaves to the task `architectureTest`; the judge reads its reports against the floor `architecture`.

**Files:**

- Test: `core/src/test/java/dev/metis/core/ArchitectureTest.java`
- Test: `tools/src/test/java/dev/metis/tools/ArchitectureTest.java`
- Create: `test-support/java/dev/metis/testsupport/ArchitectureRules.java`

**Interfaces:**

- Consumes: `TestReports` and the floor file (Task 10); the counter-tests of Task 7.
- Produces: `ArchitectureRules` (in `test-support`): `public static final ArchRule NULL_MARKED`; `public static final ArchRule LEGACY_DATES`. import net.ltgt.gradle.errorprone.errorprone
```kotlin
import org.gradle.api.tasks.testing.logging.TestExceptionFormat

plugins {
    java
    checkstyle
    id("net.ltgt.errorprone")
    id("info.solidsoft.pitest")
}

val catalog = the<VersionCatalogsExtension>().named("libs")

// Half the cores, so that tests and mutation testing never take the whole machine.
val half = (Runtime.getRuntime().availableProcessors() / 2).coerceAtLeast(1)

java {
    toolchain {
        languageVersion = JavaLanguageVersion.of(25)
        vendor = JvmVendorSpec.AMAZON
    }
}

dependencyLocking {
    lockAllConfigurations()
    lockMode = LockMode.STRICT
}

// The tests of both projects share one guard against calls that leave the machine.
sourceSets.named("test") {
    java.srcDir(rootProject.layout.projectDirectory.dir("test-support/java"))
    resources.srcDir(rootProject.layout.projectDirectory.dir("test-support/resources"))
}

dependencies {
    implementation(platform(catalog.findLibrary("spring-boot-bom").get()))
    implementation(platform(catalog.findLibrary("jackson-bom").get()))
    constraints {
        for (tomcat in listOf("tomcat-embed-core", "tomcat-embed-el", "tomcat-embed-websocket")) {
            implementation(catalog.findLibrary(tomcat).get())
        }
    }
    compileOnly("org.jspecify:jspecify")
    testCompileOnly("org.jspecify:jspecify")
    errorprone(catalog.findLibrary("errorprone-core").get())
    errorprone(catalog.findLibrary("nullaway").get())
    testImplementation(platform(catalog.findLibrary("junit-bom").get()))
    testImplementation("org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter-api")
    testImplementation("org.assertj:assertj-core")
    testImplementation(catalog.findLibrary("archunit-junit6-api").get())
    testRuntimeOnly("org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter-engine")
    testRuntimeOnly(catalog.findLibrary("archunit-junit6-engine").get())
    testRuntimeOnly("org.junit.platform:junit-platform-launcher")
}

tasks.withType<JavaCompile>().configureEach {
    options.compilerArgs.addAll(listOf("-Xlint:all", "-Werror"))
    options.errorprone {
        error("UnusedVariable", "UnusedMethod", "UnusedNestedClass", "NullAway")
        option("NullAway:OnlyNullMarked", "true")
    }
}

// A new seed on every run, printed, so that a test that depends on another one shows, and the run can be repeated.
val testSeed = providers.gradleProperty("testSeed").getOrElse(System.nanoTime().toString())

tasks.withType<Test>().configureEach {
    useJUnitPlatform()
    maxParallelForks = half
    // Every check runs its tests anew and no old report stays; coverage pays by running them again.
    dependsOn("clean${name.replaceFirstChar(Char::uppercase)}")
    systemProperty("junit.jupiter.testclass.order.default", "org.junit.jupiter.api.ClassOrderer\$Random")
    systemProperty("junit.jupiter.testmethod.order.default", "org.junit.jupiter.api.MethodOrderer\$Random")
    systemProperty("junit.jupiter.execution.order.random.seed", testSeed)
    testLogging {
        exceptionFormat = TestExceptionFormat.FULL
    }
    doFirst {
        logger.lifecycle("Test order seed $testSeed: repeat it with -PtestSeed=$testSeed")
    }
}

// The architecture rules run as a test task of their own, for their check.
tasks.test {
    useJUnitPlatform {
        excludeTags("architecture")
    }
}

tasks.register<Test>("architectureTest") {
    description = "Runs the architecture rules."
    testClassesDirs = sourceSets.test.get().output.classesDirs
    classpath = sourceSets.test.get().runtimeClasspath
    useJUnitPlatform {
        includeTags("architecture")
    }
}

checkstyle {
    toolVersion = catalog.findVersion("checkstyle").get().requiredVersion
    configDirectory = rootProject.layout.projectDirectory.dir("config/checkstyle")
}

pitest {
    pitestVersion = catalog.findVersion("pitest").get().requiredVersion
    junit5PluginVersion = catalog.findVersion("pitest-junit5").get().requiredVersion
    targetClasses = setOf("dev.metis.${project.name}.*")
    targetTests = setOf("dev.metis.${project.name}.*")
    mutators = setOf("STRONGER")
    threads = half
    outputFormats = setOf("XML", "HTML")
    timestampedReports = false
}
```

A configuration in strict mode resolves only against its lock state, and an artifact only against its checksum, so a change of the dependencies writes both again. `--rerun-tasks` runs every task for real: a task restored from the build cache resolves nothing, and its artifacts would miss their checksums.

```sh
./gradlew --console=plain --max-workers=5 --refresh-dependencies --write-locks --write-verification-metadata sha256 --rerun-tasks help spotlessCheck
```

```java
package dev.metis.core;

import static com.tngtech.archunit.base.DescribedPredicate.not;
import static com.tngtech.archunit.core.domain.JavaCall.Predicates.target;
import static com.tngtech.archunit.core.domain.properties.HasName.Predicates.nameMatching;
import static com.tngtech.archunit.core.domain.properties.HasOwner.Predicates.With.owner;
import static com.tngtech.archunit.core.domain.properties.HasParameterTypes.Predicates.rawParameterTypes;
import static com.tngtech.archunit.lang.syntax.ArchRuleDefinition.noClasses;

import com.tngtech.archunit.base.DescribedPredicate;
import com.tngtech.archunit.core.domain.JavaClass;
import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ImportOption;
import com.tngtech.archunit.junit.AnalyzeClasses;
import com.tngtech.archunit.junit.ArchTag;
import com.tngtech.archunit.junit.ArchTest;
import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.ArchRule;
import com.tngtech.archunit.library.GeneralCodingRules;
import dev.metis.testsupport.ArchitectureRules;
import java.time.Clock;

@ArchTag("architecture")
@AnalyzeClasses(packages = "dev.metis.core", importOptions = ImportOption.DoNotIncludeTests.class)
class ArchitectureTest {

  // The calls of java.time and of System that read the time or the zone of the machine.
  private static final DescribedPredicate<JavaClass> TIME =
      DescribedPredicate.describe(
          "java.time or java.lang.System",
          type -> type.getPackageName().equals("java.time") || type.isEquivalentTo(System.class));

  // The core has no field yet, so the rule checks nothing until it has.
  @ArchTest
  static final ArchRule constructorInjectionOnly =
      GeneralCodingRules.NO_CLASSES_SHOULD_USE_FIELD_INJECTION.allowEmptyShould(true);

  @ArchTest
  static final ArchRule logsGoThroughTheLogger =
      GeneralCodingRules.NO_CLASSES_SHOULD_ACCESS_STANDARD_STREAMS;

  // A clock given as a bean is the only time the core reads, so a test can fix the date.
  @ArchTest
  static final ArchRule noSystemClock =
      noClasses()
          .should()
          .callMethodWhere(
              target(owner(TIME))
                  .and(target(nameMatching("now|currentTimeMillis|system.*")))
                  .and(not(target(rawParameterTypes(Clock.class)))))
          .as("no classes should read the system clock or the system time zone");

  @ArchTest static final ArchRule nullMarked = ArchitectureRules.NULL_MARKED;

  @ArchTest static final ArchRule noLegacyDates = ArchitectureRules.LEGACY_DATES;
}
```

`test-support/java/dev/metis/testsupport/ArchitectureRules.java`:

```java
package dev.metis.testsupport;

import static com.tngtech.archunit.lang.syntax.ArchRuleDefinition.classes;
import static com.tngtech.archunit.lang.syntax.ArchRuleDefinition.noClasses;

import com.tngtech.archunit.core.domain.JavaClass;
import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.ArchCondition;
import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.ArchRule;
import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.ConditionEvents;
import com.tngtech.archunit.lang.SimpleConditionEvent;

/** The architecture rules both projects keep. */
public final class ArchitectureRules {

  // By name, since the annotation is needed to compile and not to run.
  private static final String NULL_MARK = "org.jspecify.annotations.NullMarked";

  /** NullAway checks only null-marked packages, so a package without the mark escapes it. */
  public static final ArchRule NULL_MARKED =
      classes()
          .should(
              new ArchCondition<JavaClass>("be in a null-marked package") {
                @Override
                public void check(JavaClass type, ConditionEvents events) {
                  boolean marked = type.getPackage().isAnnotatedWith(NULL_MARK);
                  String message = type.getName() + " is in a package without @NullMarked";
                  events.add(new SimpleConditionEvent(type, marked, message));
                }
              })
          .as("every class should be in a null-marked package");

  /** The legacy date types mix an instant, a zone and a calendar; java.time keeps them apart. */
  public static final ArchRule LEGACY_DATES =
      noClasses()
          .should()
          .dependOnClassesThat()
          .belongToAnyOf(
              java.util.Date.class,
              java.util.Calendar.class,
              java.util.GregorianCalendar.class,
              java.util.TimeZone.class,
              java.sql.Date.class,
              java.sql.Time.class,
              java.sql.Timestamp.class,
              java.text.DateFormat.class,
              java.text.SimpleDateFormat.class)
          .as("no classes should use the legacy date types");

  private ArchitectureRules() {}
}
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools.canary;

import java.util.List;

/** The counter-tests of the architecture check. */
final class ArchitectureCanaries {

  static final List<Canary> ALL =
      List.of(
          Canary.of("architecture-field-injection", "architecture", "use field injection")
              .writing(
                  Canaries.CORE + "CanaryInjected.java",
                  """
                  package dev.metis.core;

                  import org.jspecify.annotations.Nullable;
                  import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Autowired;
                  import org.springframework.core.env.Environment;
                  import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;

                  @Component
                  final class CanaryInjected {
                    @Autowired private @Nullable Environment environment;

                    String name() {
                      return environment == null ? "" : environment.getProperty("x", "");
                    }
                  }
                  """),
          Canary.of("architecture-system-clock", "architecture", "read the system clock")
              .writing(
                  Canaries.CORE + "CanaryClock.java",
                  """
                  package dev.metis.core;

                  import java.time.Instant;

                  final class CanaryClock {
                    private CanaryClock() {}

                    static Instant now() {
                      return Instant.now();
                    }
                  }
                  """),
          Canary.of("architecture-standard-output", "architecture", "access standard streams")
              .writing(
                  Canaries.CORE + "CanaryOutput.java",
                  """
                  package dev.metis.core;

                  final class CanaryOutput {
                    private CanaryOutput() {}

                    static void say(String text) {
                      System.out.println(text);
                    }
                  }
                  """),
          Canary.of("architecture-not-null-marked", "architecture", "package without @NullMarked")
              .writing(
                  Canaries.CORE + "canary/CanaryUnmarked.java",
                  """
                  package dev.metis.core.canary;

                  public final class CanaryUnmarked {
                    private CanaryUnmarked() {}
                  }
                  """),
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools.canary;

import java.util.List;
import java.util.stream.Stream;

/** Every counter-test, in the order ./canary all runs them. */
public final class Canaries {

  /** The folder of the core's own classes, where most canaries plant a class. */
  static final String CORE = "core/src/main/java/dev/metis/core/";

  /** Every counter-test, one list per check. */
  public static final List<Canary> ALL =
      Stream.of(
              FormatCanaries.ALL,
              CompileCanaries.ALL,
              LintCanaries.ALL,
              LanguageCanaries.ALL,
              ArchitectureCanaries.ALL,
              ToolingCanaries.ALL,
              UnitCanaries.ALL)
          .flatMap(List::stream)
          .toList();

  private Canaries() {}
}
```

```kotlin
plugins {

    mainClass = "dev.metis.tools.Main"
}

dependencies {
    implementation("tools.jackson.core:jackson-core")
    implementation("tools.jackson.core:jackson-databind")

// A command of the tool, run from the repository root, for a check of the root build to depend on.
fun tool(name: String, vararg arguments: String) =
    tasks.register<JavaExec>(name) {
        classpath = sourceSets.main.get().runtimeClasspath
        mainClass = application.mainClass
        workingDir = rootDir
        args(*arguments)
    }

tool("language", "language")
tool("marks", "marks")
// The judges of the test tasks, which run after the tests even when a test failed.
tool("judgeArchitecture", "tests", "architecture", "core/build/test-results/architectureTest", "tools/build/test-results/architectureTest")
    .configure { mustRunAfter(":core:architectureTest", tasks.named("architectureTest")) }
tool("judgeTooling", "tests", "tooling", "tools/build/test-results/test").configure { mustRunAfter(tasks.test) }
tool("judgeUnit", "tests", "unit", "core/build/test-results/test").configure { mustRunAfter(":core:test") }

// ./verify and ./canary start the tool with the Java and the classpath this task writes, and the tool
// learns from it the check tasks Gradle has in every project, however a build file declares them.
val launcher = tasks.register("launcher") {
    val executable = javaToolchains.launcherFor(java.toolchain).map { it.executablePath.asFile.path }
    val classpath = sourceSets.main.map { it.runtimeClasspath }
    val checks = rootProject.allprojects.flatMap { project ->
        val prefix = if (project == rootProject) "" else project.path + ":"
        project.tasks.names.filter { it.matches(Regex("check[A-Z]\\w*")) }.map { prefix + it }
    }
    val folder = layout.buildDirectory.dir("launcher")
    inputs.files(classpath)
    inputs.property("java", executable)
    inputs.property("checks", checks)
    outputs.dir(folder)
    doLast {
        folder.get().file("java").asFile.writeText(executable.get() + "\n")
        folder.get().file("args").asFile.writeText("-cp\n\"" + classpath.get().asPath + "\"\n")
        folder.get().file("checks").asFile.writeText(checks.joinToString("") { "$it\n" })
    }
}

// The tests of the counter-tests read the list of checks the launcher writes.
tasks.named("testClasses") { dependsOn(launcher) }
```

```kotlin
// A check whose judge did not run would pass on the exit of its tasks alone, so a check that owes
// facts fails without them; ./verify and ./canary clear the facts before each run of a check.
val factFree = setOf("checkFormat", "checkCompile", "checkDeps", "checkSecrets")
tasks.matching { it.name.matches(Regex("check[A-Z]\\w*")) && it.name !in factFree }.configureEach {
    val check = name.removePrefix("check").replaceFirstChar(Char::lowercase)
    val facts = layout.buildDirectory.file("facts/$check.txt")
    doLast {
        if (!facts.get().asFile.exists()) {
            throw GradleException("$name: its judge left no facts in build/facts/$check.txt")
        }
    }
}
```

### Task 12: The deadcode check

Unused code in four parts. Error Prone already fails an unused private member. The command `deadcode` walks the class files of each project with ArchUnit's importer from the entry points of `config/entry-points.txt` (a reason per entry, and an entry that names nothing is a problem too) and reports every class, method, constructor and field that nothing reaches; a second walk over the test classes starts from the tests themselves and reports an unused test helper. An override is reached once its class and the method above it are, in any order; a constant is checked by its name in the sources, since the compiler copies its value. The Dependency Analysis plugin fails a dependency that is declared and not used, or used and not declared; a starter stands only for the libraries of it the code uses, named one by one, so an unused library of Spring is reported like any other. A library a bundle names is never reported unused, so the task `bundledDeclared` refuses a project that declares one itself. `SettingsTest`, tagged `deadcode`, fails a key of any `application*.yml`, `.yaml` or `.properties` that neither Spring Boot nor the core defines.

**Files:**

- Test: `tools/src/test/java/dev/metis/tools/deadcode/Samples.java`
- Test: `tools/src/test/java/dev/metis/tools/deadcode/WalkTest.java`
- Test: `tools/src/test/java/dev/metis/tools/deadcode/WalkReportTest.java`
- Test: `tools/src/test/java/dev/metis/tools/deadcode/DeadcodeTest.java`
- Test: `core/src/test/java/dev/metis/core/SettingsTest.java`
- Create: `tools/src/main/java/dev/metis/tools/deadcode/package-info.java`
- Create: `tools/src/main/java/dev/metis/tools/deadcode/Walk.java`
- Create: `tools/src/main/java/dev/metis/tools/deadcode/Deadcode.java`
- Create: `config/entry-points.txt`
- Create: `tools/src/main/java/dev/metis/tools/canary/DeadcodeCanaries.java`
- Modify: `settings.gradle.kts`
- Modify: `build-logic/src/main/kotlin/metis.java-conventions.gradle.kts`
- Modify: `core/build.gradle.kts`
- Modify: `tools/build.gradle.kts`
- Modify: `build.gradle.kts`
- Modify: `tools/src/main/java/dev/metis/tools/canary/Canaries.java`
- Modify: `tools/src/main/java/dev/metis/tools/Cli.java`
- Modify: `test-floor.json`
- Generated by a command of this task: `settings-gradle.lockfile`, `gradle.lockfile`, `core/gradle.lockfile`, `tools/gradle.lockfile`, `gradle/verification-metadata.xml`

**Interfaces:**

- Consumes: `Context`, `Cli`, `TestContext`, `TestReports` (Tasks 6, 8 and 10); the counter-tests of Task 7.
- Produces: `Walk` (package-private): `Walk(JavaClasses classes)`; `static final Predicate<JavaMember> TESTS`; `Walk from(Predicate<JavaMember> roots)`; `int reached()`; `List<String> unused(String sources)`. `Deadcode`: `public final class Deadcode`; `public static int command(Context context, List<String> args) throws IOException`. The command `deadcode <file of entry points> <project> ...`, the Gradle tasks `:tools:deadcode`, `:core:deadcodeTest`, `:tools:judgeDeadcode` and `bundledDeclared`, the root task `checkDeadcode`, the file `config/entry-points.txt`, and the counter-tests deadcode-public-method, deadcode-test-only, deadcode-test-helper, deadcode-dependency, deadcode-spring-dependency, deadcode-bundle-member and deadcode-setting.
