`build-logic/src/main/kotlin/metis.java-conventions.gradle.kts`:

```kotlin
import net.ltgt.gradle.errorprone.errorprone
import org.gradle.api.tasks.testing.logging.TestExceptionFormat

plugins {
    java
    checkstyle
    id("net.ltgt.errorprone")
    id("info.solidsoft.pitest")
}

val catalog = the<VersionCatalogsExtension>().named("libs")

// Half the cores, so that tests and mutation testing never take the whole machine.
val half = (Runtime.getRuntime().availableProcessors() / 2).coerceAtLeast(1)

java {
    toolchain {
        languageVersion = JavaLanguageVersion.of(25)
        vendor = JvmVendorSpec.AMAZON
    }
}

dependencyLocking {
    lockAllConfigurations()
    lockMode = LockMode.STRICT
}

// The tests of both projects share one guard against calls that leave the machine.
sourceSets.named("test") {
    java.srcDir(rootProject.layout.projectDirectory.dir("test-support/java"))
    resources.srcDir(rootProject.layout.projectDirectory.dir("test-support/resources"))
}

dependencies {
    implementation(platform(catalog.findLibrary("spring-boot-bom").get()))
    implementation(platform(catalog.findLibrary("jackson-bom").get()))
    constraints {
        for (tomcat in listOf("tomcat-embed-core", "tomcat-embed-el", "tomcat-embed-websocket")) {
            implementation(catalog.findLibrary(tomcat).get())
        }
    }
    compileOnly("org.jspecify:jspecify")
    testCompileOnly("org.jspecify:jspecify")
    errorprone(catalog.findLibrary("errorprone-core").get())
    errorprone(catalog.findLibrary("nullaway").get())
    testImplementation(platform(catalog.findLibrary("junit-bom").get()))
    testImplementation("org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter-api")
    testImplementation("org.assertj:assertj-core")
    testImplementation(catalog.findLibrary("archunit-junit6-api").get())
    testRuntimeOnly("org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter-engine")
    testRuntimeOnly(catalog.findLibrary("archunit-junit6-engine").get())
    testRuntimeOnly("org.junit.platform:junit-platform-launcher")
}

tasks.withType<JavaCompile>().configureEach {
    options.compilerArgs.addAll(listOf("-Xlint:all", "-Werror"))
    options.errorprone {
        error("UnusedVariable", "UnusedMethod", "UnusedNestedClass", "NullAway")
        option("NullAway:OnlyNullMarked", "true")
    }
}

// A new seed on every run, printed, so that a test that depends on another one shows, and the run can be repeated.
val testSeed = providers.gradleProperty("testSeed").getOrElse(System.nanoTime().toString())

tasks.withType<Test>().configureEach {
    useJUnitPlatform()
    maxParallelForks = half
    // Every check runs its tests anew and no old report stays; coverage pays by running them again.
    dependsOn("clean${name.replaceFirstChar(Char::uppercase)}")
    systemProperty("junit.jupiter.testclass.order.default", "org.junit.jupiter.api.ClassOrderer\$Random")
    systemProperty("junit.jupiter.testmethod.order.default", "org.junit.jupiter.api.MethodOrderer\$Random")
    systemProperty("junit.jupiter.execution.order.random.seed", testSeed)
    testLogging {
        exceptionFormat = TestExceptionFormat.FULL
    }
    doFirst {
        logger.lifecycle("Test order seed $testSeed: repeat it with -PtestSeed=$testSeed")
    }
}

// The architecture rules and the test of the settings run as test tasks of their own, for their checks.
tasks.test {
    useJUnitPlatform {
        excludeTags("architecture", "deadcode")
    }
}

tasks.register<Test>("architectureTest") {
    description = "Runs the architecture rules."
    testClassesDirs = sourceSets.test.get().output.classesDirs
    classpath = sourceSets.test.get().runtimeClasspath
    useJUnitPlatform {
        includeTags("architecture")
    }
}

checkstyle {
    toolVersion = catalog.findVersion("checkstyle").get().requiredVersion
    configDirectory = rootProject.layout.projectDirectory.dir("config/checkstyle")
}

pitest {
    pitestVersion = catalog.findVersion("pitest").get().requiredVersion
    junit5PluginVersion = catalog.findVersion("pitest-junit5").get().requiredVersion
    targetClasses = setOf("dev.metis.${project.name}.*")
    targetTests = setOf("dev.metis.${project.name}.*")
    mutators = setOf("STRONGER")
    threads = half
    outputFormats = setOf("XML", "HTML")
    timestampedReports = false
}
```

```kotlin
            "org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-resttestclient",
            "org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-test",
            "org.springframework:spring-beans",
            "org.springframework:spring-core",
            "org.springframework:spring-test",
            "org.springframework:spring-web",
        ),
    )

configure<com.autonomousapps.DependencyAnalysisExtension> {
    structure {
        starters.forEach { (starter, libraries) ->
            bundle(starter.substringAfter(':')) {
                primary(starter)
                libraries.forEach { includeDependency(it) }
            }
        }
    }
    issues {
        all {
            onAny {
                severity("fail")
            }
        }
    }
}

val bundled = tasks.register("bundledDeclared") {
    description = "No project declares a library that a bundle names."
}

gradle.projectsEvaluated {
    val members = starters.values.flatten().toSet()
    val declared =
        subprojects.flatMap { project ->
            project.configurations.flatMap { configuration ->
                configuration.dependencies
                    .filter { "${it.group}:${it.name}" in members }
                    .map { "${it.group}:${it.name} in ${project.path} ${configuration.name}" }
            }
        }
    bundled.configure {
        doLast {
            if (declared.isNotEmpty()) {
                throw GradleException("a bundle names what a project declares, which it would never report: $declared")
            }
        }
    }
}
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Write the lock files and the checksums again**

A configuration in strict mode resolves only against its lock state, and an artifact only against its checksum, so a change of the dependencies writes both again. `--rerun-tasks` runs every task for real: a task restored from the build cache resolves nothing, and its artifacts would miss their checksums.

```sh
./gradlew --console=plain --max-workers=5 --refresh-dependencies --write-locks --write-verification-metadata sha256 --rerun-tasks help spotlessCheck
```

Expected: exit 0 (108.1 s in the trial run), and the output holds these lines:

```text
Persisted dependency lock state for project ':core'
Persisted dependency lock state for project ':tools'
BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 1m 48s
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools.deadcode;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

import com.tngtech.archunit.core.domain.JavaClasses;
import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ClassFileImporter;
import java.io.File;
import java.io.IOException;
import java.io.UncheckedIOException;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import javax.tools.ToolProvider;

/** Sample classes for the walk, compiled from their sources into a folder of class files. */
final class Samples {

  private Samples() {}

  /** Compiles the sources, keyed by their path under the folder, against the folders given. */
  static JavaClasses compile(Path dir, Map<String, String> sources, Path... classpath) {
    try {
      List<String> path = new ArrayList<>();
      for (Path folder : classpath) {
        path.add(folder.toString());
      }
      path.add(System.getProperty("java.class.path"));
      // The annotations of JUnit name a type that its classpath lacks, which is no matter here.
      List<String> args =
          new ArrayList<>(
              List.of(
                  "-d",
                  dir.toString(),
                  "-proc:none",
                  "-nowarn",
                  "-Xlint:none",
                  "-cp",
                  String.join(File.pathSeparator, path)));
      for (Map.Entry<String, String> source : sources.entrySet()) {
        Path file = dir.resolve(source.getKey());
        Files.createDirectories(file.getParent());
        Files.writeString(file, source.getValue());
        args.add(file.toString());
      }
      assertThat(
              ToolProvider.getSystemJavaCompiler()
                  .run(null, null, null, args.toArray(String[]::new)))
          .isZero();
      return new ClassFileImporter().importPath(dir);
    } catch (IOException failed) {
      throw new UncheckedIOException(failed);
    }
  }
}
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools.deadcode;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

import com.tngtech.archunit.core.domain.JavaMember;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.util.LinkedHashMap;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.function.Predicate;
import java.util.regex.Matcher;
import java.util.regex.Pattern;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.io.TempDir;

class WalkTest {

  static final Predicate<JavaMember> MAIN =
      member -> (member.getOwner().getName() + "." + member.getName()).equals("s.App.main");

  private static final Pattern TYPE = Pattern.compile("(?:class|interface|enum|record) (\\w+)");

  @TempDir Path dir;

  // Each source is a file of package s named after its first type, or its package-info if none.
  static List<String> unused(Path dir, Predicate<JavaMember> roots, String... sources) {
    Map<String, String> files = new LinkedHashMap<>();
    for (String source : sources) {
      Matcher type = TYPE.matcher(source);
      files.put(
          "s/" + (type.find() ? type.group(1) : "package-info") + ".java",
          type.find(0) ? "package s;\n" + source : source + "package s;\n");
    }
    return new Walk(Samples.compile(dir, files)).from(roots).unused(String.join("\n", sources));
  }

  private List<String> unused(String... sources) {
    return unused(dir, MAIN, sources);
  }

  @Test
  void whatTheEntryPointNeverReachesIsUnusedButAConstructorWithoutParametersIsNot() {
    assertThat(
            unused(
                "public class App { public static void main(String[] a) { new Used().run(); } }",
                "class Used { Used() {} Used(int n) {} void run() {} void idle() {} }",
                "class Dead { static void noop() {} }"))
        .containsExactly("class s.Dead", "constructor s.Used.<init>(int)", "method s.Used.idle()");
  }

  @Test
  void aFieldOnlyWrittenIsUnusedAndAFinalOfAPrimitiveOrAStringIsCheckedByItsName() {
    assertThat(
            unused(
                """
                class App {
                  static final String NAMED = "a";
                  static final int UNNAMED = 1;
                  private final int limit = 3;
                  static final java.util.regex.Pattern READ = java.util.regex.Pattern.compile("x");
                  static int twice;
                  private int written;
                  public static void main(String[] a) {
                    App app = new App();
                    app.written = 2;
                    int twice = app.limit;
                    System.out.println(NAMED + READ + twice);
                  }
                }
                """))
        .containsExactly("field s.App.UNNAMED", "field s.App.twice", "field s.App.written");
  }

  @Test
  void aMethodReferenceALambdaAndAStaticInitializerReachWhatTheyName() {
    assertThat(
            unused(
                """
                class App {
                  static final java.util.function.Supplier<String> NAME = Table::name;
                  public static void main(String[] a) {
                    java.util.List.of(1).forEach(n -> Table.count(n));
                    System.out.println(NAME.get());
                  }
                }
                """,
                """
                class Table {
                  static final String ROWS = rows();
                  static String name() { return "t" + ROWS; }
                  static void count(int n) {}
                  private static String rows() { return "r"; }
                  static void idle() {}
                }
                """))
        .containsExactly("method s.Table.idle()");
  }

  @Test
  void anOverrideOfATypeOutsideTheProjectIsReachedWithItsClassEvenThroughABridge() {
    assertThat(
            unused(
                "class App { public static void main(String[] a) { new Square(); } }",
                """
                class Square implements Comparable<Square> {
                  public int compareTo(Square other) { return 0; }
                  @Override public String toString() { return "square"; }
                }
                """))
        .isEmpty();
  }

  @Test
  void aMethodReachedThroughATypeReachesItsOverridesBelowWhicheverIsReachedFirst() {
    assertThat(
            unused(
                """
                class App {
                  public static void main(String[] a) {
                    Shape early = new Square();
                    System.out.println(early.area());
                    new Circle();
                  }
                }
                """,
                "interface Shape { int area(); default int sides() { return 0; } }",
                """
                class Square implements Shape {
                  public int area() { return 4; }
                  public int sides() { return 4; }
                }
                """,
                "class Circle implements Shape { public int area() { return 3; } }"))
        .containsExactly("method s.Shape.sides()", "method s.Square.sides()");
  }

  @Test
  void aSupertypeAnInterfaceAndAClassAnnotationAreUsedWithTheClassAndASelfAnnotationEndsTheWalk() {
    assertThat(
            unused(
                "class App { public static void main(String[] a) { Sub.one(); } }",
                "@Selfish class Sub extends Base implements Tag { static int one() { return 1; } }",
                "class Base {}",
                "interface Tag {}",
                "@Selfish @interface Selfish {}"))
        .isEmpty();
  }

  @Test
  void aTypeUsedOnlyInASignatureACatchALiteralAnAnnotationOrThroughASubclassIsUsed() {
    assertThat(
            unused(
                """
                class App {
                  @Marked public static void main(String[] a) throws Failure {
                    try { take(null); } catch (Caught e) { System.out.println(Literal.class); }
                    Object o = a; if (o instanceof Checked) { System.out.println(held); }
                    System.out.println(Sub.inherited());
                  }
                  static Box held;
                  static Returned take(Param p) throws Failure { return null; }
                }
                class Failure extends Exception {}
                class Caught extends RuntimeException {}
                class Literal {}
                class Checked {}
                class Returned {}
                class Param {}
                class Box {}
                class Base { static int inherited() { return 1; } }
                class Sub extends Base {}
                @interface Marked {}
                class Unused {}
                """))
        .containsExactly("class s.Unused");
  }

  @Test
  void callsInACycleAndTypesThatNameEachOtherEndTheWalk() {
    assertThat(
            unused(
                "class App { public static void main(String[] a) { Ping.ping(3); } }",
                """
                class Ping {
                  static Pong partner;
                  static void ping(int n) { if (n > 0) Pong.pong(n - 1); }
                }
                """,
                """
                class Pong {
                  static Ping partner;
                  static void pong(int n) { if (n > 0) Ping.ping(n - 1); }
                }
                """))
        .containsExactly("field s.Ping.partner", "field s.Pong.partner");
  }

  @Test
  void theCountOfReachedClassesHoldsOnlyClassesOfTheProject() {
    Map<String, String> files =
        Map.of(
            "s/App.java",
            "package s; class App { public static void main(String[] a) { System.out.println(a); } }",
            "s/Dead.java",
            "package s; class Dead {}");
    assertThat(new Walk(Samples.compile(dir, files)).from(MAIN).reached()).isEqualTo(1);
  }
}
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools.deadcode;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.util.List;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.io.TempDir;

// What the walk reports and what it leaves out: what the compiler writes, and code inside code.
class WalkReportTest {

  @TempDir Path dir;

  private List<String> unused(String... sources) {
    return WalkTest.unused(dir, WalkTest.MAIN, sources);
  }

  @Test
  void anEnumConstantIsCheckedByNameAndOnlyAnEnumHasItsTwoMethodsLeftOut() {
    assertThat(
            unused(
                """
                class App {
                  enum Kind { NAMED, UNNAMED; java.util.List<String> notes = null; void idle() {} }
                  public static void main(String[] a) {
                    System.out.println(Kind.NAMED + " " + Holder.SELF.values());
                  }
                  static String notes() { return "notes"; }
                }
                """,
                """
                class Holder {
                  static final Holder SELF = new Holder();
                  static final Holder OTHER = new Holder(); // OTHER
                  Object values() { return null; }
                  void valueOf() {}
                }
                """))
        .containsExactly(
            "field s.App$Kind.UNNAMED",
            "field s.App$Kind.notes",
            "field s.Holder.OTHER",
            "method s.App$Kind.idle()",
            "method s.App.notes()",
            "method s.Holder.valueOf()");
  }

  @Test
  void aRecordAccessorNobodyCallsIsUnusedForItsFieldButAStaticFieldOfARecordIsJudgedAlone() {
    assertThat(
            unused(
                """
                class App {
                  record Pair(int left, int right) { static int made; }
                  public static void main(String[] a) { System.out.println(new Pair(1, 2).left()); }
                }
                """))
        .containsExactly("field s.App$Pair.made", "method s.App$Pair.right()");
  }

  @Test
  void codeInsideAnUnusedMethodIsReportedAsThatMethodAlone() {
    assertThat(
            unused(
                """
                class App {
                  public static void main(String[] a) { System.out.println(a); }
                  static int idle() {
                    new Runnable() { public void run() {} }.run();
                    class Local {}
                    java.util.function.IntSupplier lambda = () -> 1;
                    return lambda.getAsInt() + new Local().hashCode();
                  }
                }
                """))
        .containsExactly("method s.App.idle()");
  }

  @Test
  void whatTheCompilerAddsItselfIsNotReported() {
    assertThat(
            unused(
                """
                class App {
                  class Inner { void hi() {} }
                  public static void main(String[] a) { new App().new Inner().hi(); }
                }
                """,
                "@Deprecated\n",
                "enum Side { LEFT, RIGHT }",
                """
                class User {
                  static int idle(Side side) {
                    switch (side) { case LEFT: return 1; case RIGHT: return 2; }
                    return 0;
                  }
                }
                """))
        .containsExactly("class s.Side", "class s.User");
  }

  @Test
  void anUnusedOverrideWithANarrowerTypeIsReportedOnceThoughTheCompilerAddsABridge() {
    assertThat(
            unused(
                "class App { public static void main(String[] a) { new Sub(); } }",
                "class Base { Object get() { return null; } }",
                "class Sub extends Base { String get() { return \"\"; } }"))
        .containsExactly("method s.Base.get()", "method s.Sub.get()");
  }

  @Test
  void theTestWalkStartsFromWhatATestEngineRunsOrFillsAndFromTheConstructorsOfTestClasses() {
    assertThat(
            WalkTest.unused(
                dir,
                Walk.TESTS,
                """
                class ATest {
                  @com.tngtech.archunit.junit.ArchTest
                  static final Object rule = Helper.rule();
                  private final String name;
                  ATest(String name) { this.name = name; }
                  @org.junit.jupiter.api.BeforeEach void setUp() { Helper.used(name); }
                  @org.junit.jupiter.api.Test void works() {}
                  @Deprecated void old() {}
                }
                """,
                """
                class Helper {
                  static Object rule() { return ""; }
                  static void used(String name) {}
                  static void idle() {}
                }
                """,
                "class Orphan { static void help() {} }"))
        .containsExactly("class s.Orphan", "method s.ATest.old()", "method s.Helper.idle()");
  }
}
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools.deadcode;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

import dev.metis.tools.TestContext;
import java.io.IOException;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.io.TempDir;

class DeadcodeTest {

  private static final String APP =
      "package s; public class App { public static void main(String[] a) { Used.run(); } }";
  private static final String USED =
      """
      package s;
      public class Used {
        static final String NAME = "used";
        static void run() { System.out.println(NAME); }
        public static void idle() {}
      }
      """;
  private static final String TEST =
      """
      package s;
      import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
      class UsedTest { @Test void runs() { Used.run(); Helper.help(); } }
      """;
  private static final String HELPER = "package s; class Helper { static void help() {} }";
  private static final String ORPHAN = "package s; class Orphan { static void help() {} }";

  @TempDir Path root;

  // A project with its sources under src and its classes where Gradle writes them.
  private void project(String name, Map<String, String> main, Map<String, String> tests)
      throws IOException {
    write(name + "/src/main/java", main);
    write(name + "/src/test/java", tests);
    Samples.compile(root.resolve(name + "/build/classes/java/main"), main);
    if (!tests.isEmpty()) {
      Path classes = root.resolve(name + "/build/classes/java/test");
      Samples.compile(classes, tests, root.resolve(name + "/build/classes/java/main"));
    }
  }

  private void write(String folder, Map<String, String> sources) throws IOException {
    for (Map.Entry<String, String> source : sources.entrySet()) {
      Path file = root.resolve(folder).resolve(source.getKey());
      Files.createDirectories(file.getParent());
      Files.writeString(file, source.getValue());
    }
  }

  private TestContext walk(String entries) throws IOException {
    Files.createDirectories(root.resolve("config"));
    Files.writeString(root.resolve("config/entry-points.txt"), entries);
    TestContext test = new TestContext(root);
    test.exit = Deadcode.command(test.context(), List.of("config/entry-points.txt", "core"));
    return test;
  }

  @Test
  void theProductionWalkStartsFromTheListAndTheTestWalkFromTheTests() throws IOException {
    project(
        "core",
        Map.of("s/App.java", APP, "s/Used.java", USED),
        Map.of("s/UsedTest.java", TEST, "s/Helper.java", HELPER, "s/Orphan.java", ORPHAN));
    TestContext test = walk("# Entry points.\n\ns.App.main: started by the JVM\n");
    assertThat(test.exit).isEqualTo(1);
    assertThat(test.printed().lines())
        .containsExactly(
            "core: method s.Used.idle() is never used",
            "core tests: class s.Orphan is never used",
            "deadcode: 2 problems");
  }

  @Test
  void aClassOfTheListIsUsedWholeAndTheCountAddsTheClassesBothWalksReached() throws IOException {
    project(
        "core",
        Map.of("s/App.java", APP, "s/Used.java", USED),
        Map.of("s/UsedTest.java", TEST, "s/Helper.java", HELPER));
    TestContext test = walk("s.App.main: started by the JVM\ns.Used: read by reflection\n");
    assertThat(test.exit).isZero();
    assertThat(test.printed()).isEqualTo("deadcode: clean (4 classes reached)\n");
  }

  @Test
  void aProjectWithoutTestsHasOnlyItsProductionWalk() throws IOException {
    project("core", Map.of("s/App.java", APP, "s/Used.java", USED), Map.of());
    TestContext test = walk("s.App.main: started by the JVM\ns.Used: read by reflection\n");
    assertThat(test.printed()).isEqualTo("deadcode: clean (2 classes reached)\n");
  }

  @Test
  void anEntryWithoutAReasonOrThatNamesNothingIsAProblemOfTheList() throws IOException {
    project("core", Map.of("s/App.java", APP, "s/Used.java", USED), Map.of());
    TestContext test =
        walk("s.App.main\ns.App.main: started\ns.Used: read\ns.Gone.run: removed long ago\n: x\n");
    assertThat(test.exit).isEqualTo(1);
    assertThat(test.printed().lines())
        .containsExactly(
            "config/entry-points.txt:1: no-reason: s.App.main",
            "config/entry-points.txt:5: no-reason: : x",
            "config/entry-points.txt:4: names nothing: s.Gone.run",
            "deadcode: 3 problems");
  }

  @Test
  void withoutAListAndAProjectItPrintsItsUsage() throws IOException {
    TestContext test = new TestContext(root);
    assertThat(Deadcode.command(test.context(), List.of("config/entry-points.txt"))).isEqualTo(2);
    assertThat(test.printed()).isEqualTo("usage: deadcode <file of entry points> <project> ...\n");
  }
}
```

```java
package dev.metis.core;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.io.InputStream;
import java.net.URL;
import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.Collections;
import java.util.HashSet;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.Objects;
import java.util.Properties;
import java.util.Set;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Tag;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.springframework.beans.factory.config.YamlPropertiesFactoryBean;
import org.springframework.boot.json.JsonParserFactory;
import org.springframework.core.io.Resource;
import org.springframework.core.io.support.PathMatchingResourcePatternResolver;
import org.springframework.core.io.support.PropertiesLoaderUtils;

// A setting nothing binds would sit in a settings file unseen, so the deadcode check runs this.
@Tag("deadcode")
class SettingsTest {

  @Test
  void everyKeyOfTheSettingsIsOneThatSpringBootOrTheCoreDefines() throws IOException {
    Set<String> known = new HashSet<>();
    Set<String> maps = new HashSet<>();
    ClassLoader loader = getClass().getClassLoader();
    for (URL file :
        Collections.list(loader.getResources("META-INF/spring-configuration-metadata.json"))) {
      try (InputStream in = file.openStream()) {
        String json = new String(in.readAllBytes(), StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
        Object properties = JsonParserFactory.getJsonParser().parseMap(json).get("properties");
        for (Object property : properties instanceof List<?> list ? list : List.of()) {
          Map<?, ?> setting = (Map<?, ?>) property;
          String name = String.valueOf(setting.get("name"));
          known.add(name);
          if (String.valueOf(setting.get("type")).startsWith("java.util.Map")) {
            maps.add(name);
          }
        }
      }
    }
    Properties settings = new Properties();
    List<Resource> files = settingsFiles();
    assertThat(files).as("settings files").isNotEmpty();
    for (Resource file : files) {
      if (String.valueOf(file.getFilename()).endsWith(".properties")) {
        settings.putAll(PropertiesLoaderUtils.loadProperties(file));
      } else {
        YamlPropertiesFactoryBean yaml = new YamlPropertiesFactoryBean();
        yaml.setResources(file);
        settings.putAll(Objects.requireNonNull(yaml.getObject()));
      }
    }
    List<String> unknown =
        settings.keySet().stream()
            .map(key -> String.valueOf(key).replaceAll("\\[\\d+]", ""))
            .filter(key -> !known.contains(key))
            .filter(key -> maps.stream().noneMatch(map -> key.startsWith(map + ".")))
            .sorted()
            .toList();
    assertThat(unknown).as("settings that nothing binds").isEmpty();
  }

  // Every file of settings, a profile's own included, since Spring Boot reads them all.
  private static List<Resource> settingsFiles() throws IOException {
    PathMatchingResourcePatternResolver resolver = new PathMatchingResourcePatternResolver();
    List<Resource> files = new ArrayList<>();
    for (String kind : List.of("yml", "yaml", "properties")) {
      files.addAll(List.of(resolver.getResources("classpath*:application*." + kind)));
    }
    return files;
  }
}
```

```java
import java.util.regex.Pattern;
import java.util.stream.Stream;

/** A walk over the class files of a project from its roots; what it never reaches is unused. */
final class Walk {

  /** The roots of a walk over tests: the members a test engine runs or fills. */
  static final Predicate<JavaMember> TESTS =
      member ->
          member.getAnnotations().stream()
              .map(annotation -> annotation.getRawType().getPackageName())
              .anyMatch(
                  name ->
                      name.startsWith("org.junit.")
                          || name.startsWith("com.tngtech.archunit.junit"));

  private final JavaClasses classes;
  private final Set<JavaClass> types = new HashSet<>();
  private final Set<JavaMember> members = new HashSet<>();
  private final Deque<JavaCodeUnit> pending = new ArrayDeque<>();

  Walk(JavaClasses classes) {
    this.classes = classes;
  }

  /** Walks from every member the predicate names a root. */
  Walk from(Predicate<JavaMember> roots) {
    for (JavaClass type : classes) {
      for (JavaMember member : type.getMembers()) {
        if (roots.test(member)) {
          reach(member);
          // A class that holds a root is made by whatever calls the root, its constructors too.
          type.getConstructors().forEach(this::reach);
        }
      }
    }
    // An override is used once its class is reached and the method above it is, in any order.
    int before;
    do {
      before = members.size();
      while (!pending.isEmpty()) {
        visit(pending.pop());
      }
      for (JavaClass type : List.copyOf(types)) {
        type.getMethods().stream().filter(method -> overrides(type, method)).forEach(this::reach);
      }
    } while (members.size() > before);
    return this;
  }

  /** How many classes of the project the walk reached. */
  int reached() {
    return types.size();
  }

  /** What the walk never reached, as kind and name, in name order; sources hold every name. */
  List<String> unused(String sources) {
    List<String> unused = new ArrayList<>();
    for (JavaClass type : classes) {
      if (!types.contains(type)) {
        if (reportable(type)) {
          unused.add("class " + type.getName());
        }
        continue;
      }
      type.getCodeUnits().stream()
          .filter(unit -> !members.contains(unit) && reportable(unit))
          .forEach(unit -> unused.add(kindOf(unit) + " " + unit.getFullName()));
      type.getFields().stream()
          .filter(field -> unusedField(field, sources))
          .forEach(field -> unused.add("field " + field.getFullName()));
    }
    return unused.stream().sorted().toList();
  }

  private void reach(JavaMember member) {
    if (!members.add(member)) {
      return;
    }
    reachType(member.getOwner());
    if (member instanceof JavaCodeUnit unit) {
      pending.push(unit);
    }
    if (member instanceof JavaField field) {
      reachType(field.getRawType());
    }
  }

  private void reachType(JavaClass type) {
    JavaClass base = type.getBaseComponentType();
    if (!classes.contain(base.getName()) || !types.add(base)) {
      return;
    }
    base.getStaticInitializer().ifPresent(this::reach);
    base.getRawSuperclass().ifPresent(this::reachType);
    base.getRawInterfaces().forEach(this::reachType);
    base.getAnnotations().forEach(annotation -> reachType(annotation.getRawType()));
  }

  // A method that overrides one of a type outside the walk, or one the walk reached, is used.
  private boolean overrides(JavaClass type, JavaMethod method) {
    return Stream.concat(type.getAllRawSuperclasses().stream(), type.getAllRawInterfaces().stream())
        .flatMap(above -> overrideIn(above, method).stream())
        .anyMatch(above -> !classes.contain(above.getOwner().getName()) || members.contains(above));
  }

  private static Optional<JavaMethod> overrideIn(JavaClass type, JavaMethod method) {
    String[] parameters =
        method.getRawParameterTypes().stream().map(JavaClass::getName).toArray(String[]::new);
    return type.tryGetMethod(method.getName(), parameters);
  }

  private void visit(JavaCodeUnit unit) {
    for (JavaAccess<?> access : unit.getAccessesFromSelf()) {
      // A call of an inherited method names the class it calls through as well.
      reachType(access.getTargetOwner());
      boolean written =
          access instanceof JavaFieldAccess field
              && field.getAccessType() == JavaFieldAccess.AccessType.SET;
      if (!written) {
        access.getTarget().resolveMember().ifPresent(this::reach);
      }
    }
    unit.getReferencedClassObjects().forEach(literal -> reachType(literal.getRawType()));
    unit.getInstanceofChecks().forEach(check -> reachType(check.getRawType()));
    unit.getRawParameterTypes().forEach(this::reachType);
    reachType(unit.getRawReturnType());
    unit.getThrowsClause().getTypes().forEach(this::reachType);
    unit.getAnnotations().stream().map(JavaAnnotation::getRawType).forEach(this::reachType);
    for (TryCatchBlock block : unit.getTryCatchBlocks()) {
      block.getCaughtThrowables().forEach(this::reachType);
    }
  }

  // No source holds a synthetic class; an anonymous or local class is reported as its maker.
  private static boolean reportable(JavaClass type) {
    return !type.getModifiers().contains(JavaModifier.SYNTHETIC)
        && !type.isAnonymousClass()
        && !type.isLocalClass();
  }

  // A constructor without parameters stops nothing, and an enum always has its two methods.
  private static boolean reportable(JavaCodeUnit unit) {
    boolean bare = unit instanceof JavaConstructor && unit.getRawParameterTypes().isEmpty();
    boolean listed =
        unit.getOwner().isEnum() && Set.of("values", "valueOf").contains(unit.getName());
    return !unit.getModifiers().contains(JavaModifier.SYNTHETIC) && !bare && !listed;
  }

  private static String kindOf(JavaCodeUnit unit) {
    return unit instanceof JavaConstructor ? "constructor" : "method";
  }

  private boolean unusedField(JavaField field, String sources) {
    // The accessor of a record speaks for its field, which equals and hashCode read unseen.
    boolean component =
        field.getOwner().isRecord() && !field.getModifiers().contains(JavaModifier.STATIC);
    if (field.getModifiers().contains(JavaModifier.SYNTHETIC) || component) {
      return false;
    }
    // A final field of a primitive or a string may be a constant, whose reads the compiler copies.
    // ponytail: two mentions of the name count as a read, comments too; parsing lifts it.
    boolean constant =
        field.getModifiers().contains(JavaModifier.FINAL)
            && (field.getRawType().isPrimitive()
                || field.getRawType().isEquivalentTo(String.class));
    boolean listed = field.getOwner().isEnum() && field.getRawType().equals(field.getOwner());
    if (constant || listed) {
      return Pattern.compile("\\b" + field.getName() + "\\b").matcher(sources).results().count()
          < 2;
    }
    return !members.contains(field);
  }
}
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools.deadcode;

import com.tngtech.archunit.core.domain.JavaClasses;
import com.tngtech.archunit.core.domain.JavaMember;
import com.tngtech.archunit.core.importer.ClassFileImporter;
import dev.metis.tools.Context;
import java.io.IOException;
import java.io.PrintStream;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.HashSet;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Set;
import java.util.function.Predicate;
import java.util.regex.Matcher;
import java.util.regex.Pattern;
import java.util.stream.Stream;

/** Walks each project from the listed entry points and its tests from themselves. */
public final class Deadcode {

  private static final String USAGE = "usage: deadcode <file of entry points> <project> ...";
  // The tests of both projects share the sources of this folder.
  private static final String SHARED_TESTS = "test-support/java";
  private static final Pattern ENTRY = Pattern.compile("([\\w.$]+): \\S.*");

  private Deadcode() {}

  /** One line of the list: a class, or a class and a member; its reason is only checked. */
  private record Entry(int line, String pattern) {

    boolean names(JavaMember member) {
      String owner = member.getOwner().getName();
      return pattern.equals(owner) || pattern.equals(owner + "." + member.getName());
    }
  }

  /** Walks each project and prints what nothing reaches. */
  public static int command(Context context, List<String> args) throws IOException {
    PrintStream out = context.out();
    if (args.size() < 2) {
      out.println(USAGE);
      return 2;
    }
    Path root = context.root();
    String list = args.getFirst();
    List<String> problems = new ArrayList<>();
    List<Entry> entries = entriesOf(root.resolve(list), list, problems);
    Set<Entry> used = new HashSet<>();
    Predicate<JavaMember> listed =
        member -> {
          List<Entry> naming = entries.stream().filter(entry -> entry.names(member)).toList();
          used.addAll(naming);
          return !naming.isEmpty();
        };
    int walked = 0;
    for (String project : args.subList(1, args.size())) {
      JavaClasses main = classesOf(root.resolve(project + "/build/classes/java/main"));
      JavaClasses tests = classesOf(root.resolve(project + "/build/classes/java/test"));
      String mainSources = sourcesOf(root.resolve(project + "/src/main/java"));
      String testSources =
          sourcesOf(root.resolve(project + "/src/test/java"))
              + sourcesOf(root.resolve(SHARED_TESTS));
      Walk production = new Walk(main).from(listed);
      Walk testing = new Walk(tests).from(Walk.TESTS.or(listed));
      walked += production.reached() + testing.reached();
      for (String line : production.unused(mainSources)) {
        problems.add(project + ": " + line + " is never used");
      }
      for (String line : testing.unused(testSources)) {
        problems.add(project + " tests: " + line + " is never used");
      }
    }
    entries.stream()
        .filter(entry -> !used.contains(entry))
        .forEach(
            entry ->
                problems.add(list + ":" + entry.line() + ": names nothing: " + entry.pattern()));
    problems.forEach(out::println);
    out.println(
        problems.isEmpty()
            ? "deadcode: clean (" + walked + " classes reached)"
            : "deadcode: " + problems.size() + " problems");
    return problems.isEmpty() ? 0 : 1;
  }

  private static List<Entry> entriesOf(Path file, String list, List<String> problems)
      throws IOException {
    List<String> lines = Files.readAllLines(file);
    List<Entry> entries = new ArrayList<>();
    for (int at = 0; at < lines.size(); at++) {
      String line = lines.get(at).strip();
      Matcher entry = ENTRY.matcher(line);
      if (entry.matches()) {
        entries.add(new Entry(at + 1, entry.group(1)));
      } else if (!line.isEmpty() && !line.startsWith("#")) {
        problems.add(list + ":" + (at + 1) + ": no-reason: " + line);
      }
    }
    return entries;
  }

  // A folder that does not exist holds no class.
  private static JavaClasses classesOf(Path folder) {
    return new ClassFileImporter().importPath(folder);
  }

  private static String sourcesOf(Path folder) throws IOException {
    if (!Files.isDirectory(folder)) {
      return "";
    }
    StringBuilder text = new StringBuilder();
    try (Stream<Path> files = Files.walk(folder)) {
      for (Path file : files.filter(path -> path.toString().endsWith(".java")).toList()) {
        text.append(Files.readString(file)).append('\n');
      }
    }
    return text.toString();
  }
}
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools.canary;

import java.util.List;

/** The counter-tests of the deadcode check. */
final class DeadcodeCanaries {

  private static final String TESTS = "core/src/test/java/dev/metis/core/";

  static final List<Canary> ALL =
      List.of(
          // An entry for the one method a canary class needs, so that its other method is unused.
          Canary.of("deadcode-public-method", "deadcode", "CanaryDead.idle() is never used")
              .writing(
                  Canaries.CORE + "CanaryDead.java",
                  """
                  package dev.metis.core;

                  public final class CanaryDead {
                    private CanaryDead() {}

                    public static int used() {
                      return 1;
                    }

                    public static int idle() {
                      return 2;
                    }
                  }
                  """)
              .appending("config/entry-points.txt", "dev.metis.core.CanaryDead.used: a canary\n"),
          Canary.of("deadcode-test-only", "deadcode", "core: class dev.metis.core.CanaryTestOnly")
              .writing(
                  Canaries.CORE + "CanaryTestOnly.java",
                  """
                  package dev.metis.core;

                  final class CanaryTestOnly {
                    private CanaryTestOnly() {}

                    static int one() {
                      return 1;
                    }
                  }
                  """)
              .writing(
                  TESTS + "CanaryTestOnlyTest.java",
                  """
                  package dev.metis.core;

                  import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

                  import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

                  class CanaryTestOnlyTest {
                    @Test
                    void one() {
                      assertThat(CanaryTestOnly.one()).isEqualTo(1);
                    }
                  }
                  """),
          Canary.of(
                  "deadcode-test-helper",
                  "deadcode",
                  "core tests: class dev.metis.core.CanaryHelper")
              .writing(
                  TESTS + "CanaryHelper.java",
                  """
                  package dev.metis.core;

                  final class CanaryHelper {
                    private CanaryHelper() {}

                    static String help() {
                      return "help";
                    }
                  }
                  """),
          // A library the tool declares and never uses, which no bundle of a starter names; the
          // advice of the plugin, which no error of the lock prints.
          Canary.of("deadcode-dependency", "deadcode", "implementation(\"org.slf4j:slf4j-api")
              .appending(
                  "tools/build.gradle.kts",
                  "\ndependencies {\n    implementation(\"org.slf4j:slf4j-api\")\n}\n"),
          // A library of Spring declared and never used, which no starter may stand for.
          Canary.of(
                  "deadcode-spring-dependency",
                  "deadcode",
                  "implementation(\"org.springframework:spring-expression")
              .appending(
                  "core/build.gradle.kts",
                  "\ndependencies {\n    implementation(\"org.springframework:spring-expression\")\n}\n"),
          // A library a bundle names, declared and unused by the code of the core, which the
          // bundle would hide.
          Canary.of("deadcode-bundle-member", "deadcode", "a bundle names what a project declares")
              .appending(
                  "core/build.gradle.kts",
                  "\ndependencies {\n    implementation(\"org.springframework:spring-web\")\n}\n"),
          // A file of settings of a profile, which Spring Boot reads as it reads application.yml.
          Canary.of("deadcode-setting", "deadcode", "metis.unread")
              .writing(
                  "core/src/main/resources/application-canary.yml", "metis:\n  unread: true\n"));

  private DeadcodeCanaries() {}
}
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools.canary;

import java.util.List;
import java.util.stream.Stream;

/** Every counter-test, in the order ./canary all runs them. */
public final class Canaries {

  /** The folder of the core's own classes, where most canaries plant a class. */
  static final String CORE = "core/src/main/java/dev/metis/core/";

  /** Every counter-test, one list per check. */
  public static final List<Canary> ALL =
      Stream.of(
              FormatCanaries.ALL,
              CompileCanaries.ALL,
              LintCanaries.ALL,
              LanguageCanaries.ALL,
              ArchitectureCanaries.ALL,
              DeadcodeCanaries.ALL,
              ToolingCanaries.ALL,
              UnitCanaries.ALL)
          .flatMap(List::stream)
          .toList();

  private Canaries() {}
}
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools;

import dev.metis.tools.canary.CanaryRun;
import dev.metis.tools.deadcode.Deadcode;
import dev.metis.tools.language.Language;
import dev.metis.tools.lint.Marks;
import dev.metis.tools.tests.TestReports;
import dev.metis.tools.verify.Verify;
import java.io.IOException;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import org.jspecify.annotations.Nullable;

/** The commands of the tool of the checks. */
public final class Cli {

  private static final Map<String, Command> COMMANDS =
      Map.of(
          "verify", Verify::command,
          "canary", CanaryRun::command,
          "language", Language::command,
          "marks", Marks::command,
          "tests", TestReports::command,
          "deadcode", Deadcode::command);

  private static final String USAGE =
      """
      usage: verify [--only <check>[,<check>]] [--fast] [--append]
             canary <name>|all
             language [<path> ...]
             marks
             tests <check> <folder of test reports> ...
             deadcode <file of entry points> <project> ...""";

  private Cli() {}

  /** Runs the command the arguments name and returns its exit code. */
  public static int run(Context context, List<String> args) throws IOException {
    @Nullable Command command = args.isEmpty() ? null : COMMANDS.get(args.getFirst());
    if (command == null) {
      context.out().println(USAGE);
      return 2;
    }
    return command.run(context, args.subList(1, args.size()));
  }
}
```

### Task 13: The coverage check

JaCoCo 0.8.15 over both projects. The command `coverage` judges the XML report of each project on its own: a missing report, or one that measured no line, is red, never counted as nothing to cover; every line and every branch must be covered, and each class that misses one is named. Each report is removed before it is made, so one an earlier run left never speaks for this one. The classes of `config/coverage-exclusions.txt` are left out of the reports, each with its reason.

**Files:**

- Test: `tools/src/test/java/dev/metis/tools/coverage/CoverageTest.java`

- Create: `tools/src/main/java/dev/metis/tools/canary/CoverageCanaries.java`

```kotlin
import net.ltgt.gradle.errorprone.errorprone
import org.gradle.api.tasks.testing.logging.TestExceptionFormat

plugins {
    java
    jacoco
    checkstyle
    id("net.ltgt.errorprone")
    id("info.solidsoft.pitest")
}

val catalog = the<VersionCatalogsExtension>().named("libs")

// Half the cores, so that tests and mutation testing never take the whole machine.
val half = (Runtime.getRuntime().availableProcessors() / 2).coerceAtLeast(1)

java {
    toolchain {
        languageVersion = JavaLanguageVersion.of(25)
        vendor = JvmVendorSpec.AMAZON
    }
}

dependencyLocking {
    lockAllConfigurations()
    lockMode = LockMode.STRICT
}

// The tests of both projects share one guard against calls that leave the machine.
sourceSets.named("test") {
    java.srcDir(rootProject.layout.projectDirectory.dir("test-support/java"))
    resources.srcDir(rootProject.layout.projectDirectory.dir("test-support/resources"))
}

dependencies {
    implementation(platform(catalog.findLibrary("spring-boot-bom").get()))
    implementation(platform(catalog.findLibrary("jackson-bom").get()))
    constraints {
        for (tomcat in listOf("tomcat-embed-core", "tomcat-embed-el", "tomcat-embed-websocket")) {
            implementation(catalog.findLibrary(tomcat).get())
        }
    }
    compileOnly("org.jspecify:jspecify")
    testCompileOnly("org.jspecify:jspecify")
    errorprone(catalog.findLibrary("errorprone-core").get())
    errorprone(catalog.findLibrary("nullaway").get())
    testImplementation(platform(catalog.findLibrary("junit-bom").get()))
    testImplementation("org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter-api")
    testImplementation("org.assertj:assertj-core")
    testImplementation(catalog.findLibrary("archunit-junit6-api").get())
    testRuntimeOnly("org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter-engine")
    testRuntimeOnly(catalog.findLibrary("archunit-junit6-engine").get())
    testRuntimeOnly("org.junit.platform:junit-platform-launcher")
}

tasks.withType<JavaCompile>().configureEach {
    options.compilerArgs.addAll(listOf("-Xlint:all", "-Werror"))
    options.errorprone {
        error("UnusedVariable", "UnusedMethod", "UnusedNestedClass", "NullAway")
        option("NullAway:OnlyNullMarked", "true")
    }
}

// A new seed on every run, printed, so that a test that depends on another one shows, and the run can be repeated.
val testSeed = providers.gradleProperty("testSeed").getOrElse(System.nanoTime().toString())

tasks.withType<Test>().configureEach {
    useJUnitPlatform()
    maxParallelForks = half
    // Every check runs its tests anew and no old report stays; coverage pays by running them again.
    dependsOn("clean${name.replaceFirstChar(Char::uppercase)}")
    systemProperty("junit.jupiter.testclass.order.default", "org.junit.jupiter.api.ClassOrderer\$Random")
    systemProperty("junit.jupiter.testmethod.order.default", "org.junit.jupiter.api.MethodOrderer\$Random")
    systemProperty("junit.jupiter.execution.order.random.seed", testSeed)
    testLogging {
        exceptionFormat = TestExceptionFormat.FULL
    }
    doFirst {
        logger.lifecycle("Test order seed $testSeed: repeat it with -PtestSeed=$testSeed")
    }
}

// The architecture rules and the test of the settings run as test tasks of their own, for their checks.
tasks.test {
    useJUnitPlatform {
        excludeTags("architecture", "deadcode")
    }
}

tasks.register<Test>("architectureTest") {
    description = "Runs the architecture rules."
    testClassesDirs = sourceSets.test.get().output.classesDirs
    classpath = sourceSets.test.get().runtimeClasspath
    useJUnitPlatform {
        includeTags("architecture")
    }
}

jacoco {
    toolVersion = catalog.findVersion("jacoco").get().requiredVersion
}

// The classes no test can run in the test process, each with its reason in the list.
val excluded =
    rootProject.file("config/coverage-exclusions.txt").readLines()
        .map { it.trim() }
        .filter { it.isNotEmpty() && !it.startsWith("#") }
        .map { it.substringBefore(":") }

tasks.jacocoTestReport {
    // A report an earlier run left behind must not speak for a run whose report task did not run.
    dependsOn("cleanJacocoTestReport", tasks.test)
    classDirectories.setFrom(
        sourceSets.main.get().output.classesDirs.asFileTree.matching {
            exclude(excluded.map { it.replace('.', '/') + ".class" })
        },
    )
    reports {
        xml.required = true
    }
}

checkstyle {
    toolVersion = catalog.findVersion("checkstyle").get().requiredVersion
    configDirectory = rootProject.layout.projectDirectory.dir("config/checkstyle")
}

pitest {
    pitestVersion = catalog.findVersion("pitest").get().requiredVersion
    junit5PluginVersion = catalog.findVersion("pitest-junit5").get().requiredVersion
    targetClasses = setOf("dev.metis.${project.name}.*")
    targetTests = setOf("dev.metis.${project.name}.*")
    mutators = setOf("STRONGER")
    threads = half
    outputFormats = setOf("XML", "HTML")
    timestampedReports = false
}
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Write the lock files and the checksums again**

A configuration in strict mode resolves only against its lock state, and an artifact only against its checksum, so a change of the dependencies writes both again. `--rerun-tasks` runs every task for real: a task restored from the build cache resolves nothing, and its artifacts would miss their checksums.

```sh
./gradlew --console=plain --max-workers=5 --refresh-dependencies --write-locks --write-verification-metadata sha256 --rerun-tasks help spotlessCheck
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools.coverage;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

import dev.metis.tools.Facts;
import dev.metis.tools.TestContext;
import java.io.IOException;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.util.List;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.io.TempDir;

class CoverageTest {

  private static final String CORE = "core/build/reports/jacoco/test/jacocoTestReport.xml";
  private static final String TOOLS = "tools/build/reports/jacoco/test/jacocoTestReport.xml";

  @TempDir Path root;

  private static String counter(String type, int missed, int covered) {
    return "<counter type=\"%s\" missed=\"%d\" covered=\"%d\"/>".formatted(type, missed, covered);
  }

  // A JaCoCo report of one class, its counters given, and the counters of the report beside it.
  private void report(String path, String type, String counters) throws IOException {
    Files.createDirectories(root.resolve(path).getParent());
    Files.writeString(
        root.resolve(path),
        """
        <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" standalone="yes"?>
        <!DOCTYPE report PUBLIC "-//JACOCO//DTD Report 1.1//EN" "report.dtd">
        <report name="core">
          <package name="dev/metis/core"><class name="%s" sourcefilename="A.java">\
        <method name="a" desc="()V" line="3">%s</method>%s</class></package>%s</report>
        """
            .formatted(type, counters, counters, counters));
  }

  private TestContext judge(String... reports) throws IOException {
    TestContext test = new TestContext(root);
    test.exit = Coverage.command(test.context(), List.of(reports));
    return test;
  }

  @Test
  void everyLineAndEveryBranchOfEveryReportCoveredIsGreenAndTheFactsNameEachProject()
      throws IOException {
    report(CORE, "dev/metis/core/A", counter("LINE", 0, 3) + counter("BRANCH", 0, 2));
    report(TOOLS, "dev/metis/tools/B", counter("INSTRUCTION", 1, 9) + counter("LINE", 0, 4));
    TestContext test = judge(CORE, TOOLS);
    assertThat(test.exit).isZero();
    String facts = "core lines 3 of 3, branches 2 of 2; tools lines 4 of 4, branches 0 of 0";
    assertThat(test.printed()).isEqualTo("coverage: " + facts + "\n");
    assertThat(Facts.read(root, "coverage")).hasValue(facts);
  }

  @Test
  void aReportThatMeasuredNoLineIsRedSinceAProjectWithCodeNeverCountsAsZero() throws IOException {
    report(CORE, "dev/metis/core/A", counter("LINE", 0, 3));
    report(TOOLS, "dev/metis/tools/B", counter("INSTRUCTION", 0, 0));
    TestContext test = judge(CORE, TOOLS);
    assertThat(test.exit).isEqualTo(1);
    assertThat(test.printed().lines())
        .containsExactly(
            "coverage: tools measured no line",
            "coverage: core lines 3 of 3, branches 0 of 0; tools lines 0 of 0, branches 0 of 0");
  }

  @Test
  void aLineOrABranchNoTestRanIsRedAndNamesItsClass() throws IOException {
    report(CORE, "dev/metis/core/A", counter("LINE", 1, 2) + counter("BRANCH", 0, 2));
    TestContext lines = judge(CORE);
    assertThat(lines.exit).isEqualTo(1);
    assertThat(lines.printed().lines())
        .containsExactly(
            "coverage: dev.metis.core.A: 1 of 3 lines, 0 of 2 branches missed",
            "coverage: core lines 2 of 3, branches 2 of 2");
    report(TOOLS, "dev/metis/tools/B", counter("LINE", 0, 4) + counter("BRANCH", 1, 3));
    TestContext branches = judge(TOOLS);
    assertThat(branches.exit).isEqualTo(1);
    assertThat(branches.printed().lines())
        .containsExactly(
            "coverage: dev.metis.tools.B: 0 of 4 lines, 1 of 4 branches missed",
            "coverage: tools lines 4 of 4, branches 3 of 4");
    assertThat(Facts.read(root, "coverage")).hasValue("tools lines 4 of 4, branches 3 of 4");
  }

  @Test
  void aMissingOrMalformedReportIsRedAndLeavesNoFacts() throws IOException {
    TestContext missing = judge(CORE);
    assertThat(missing.exit).isEqualTo(1);
    assertThat(missing.printed()).isEqualTo("coverage: no coverage report " + CORE + "\n");
    Files.createDirectories(root.resolve(CORE).getParent());
    Files.writeString(root.resolve(CORE), "<report");
    TestContext broken = judge(CORE);
    assertThat(broken.exit).isEqualTo(1);
    assertThat(broken.printed()).startsWith("coverage: jacocoTestReport.xml is no XML: ");
    assertThat(Facts.read(root, "coverage")).isEmpty();
  }

  @Test
  void withoutAReportItPrintsItsUsage() throws IOException {
    TestContext test = judge();
    assertThat(test.exit).isEqualTo(2);
    assertThat(test.printed()).isEqualTo("usage: coverage <JaCoCo XML report> ...\n");
  }
}
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools.coverage;

import dev.metis.tools.Context;
import dev.metis.tools.Facts;
import dev.metis.tools.Xml;
import java.io.IOException;
import java.io.PrintStream;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import org.w3c.dom.Element;
import org.w3c.dom.Node;
import org.w3c.dom.NodeList;

/** Every line and branch JaCoCo measured ran in a test; the exclusion list shapes the report. */
public final class Coverage {

  private static final String USAGE = "usage: coverage <JaCoCo XML report> ...";
  private static final List<String> KINDS = List.of("LINE", "BRANCH");

  private Coverage() {}

  /** Lines and branches, missed and in all, of a report or a class. */
  private record Counts(int linesMissed, int lines, int branchesMissed, int branches) {

    // The counters right under the element hold its sums; another child names no kind.
    static Counts of(Element owner) {
      int[] counts = new int[4];
      for (Node child = owner.getFirstChild(); child != null; child = child.getNextSibling()) {
        if (child instanceof Element counter) {
          int kind = KINDS.indexOf(counter.getAttribute("type"));
          if (kind >= 0) {
            int missed = Integer.parseInt(counter.getAttribute("missed"));
            counts[2 * kind] += missed;
            counts[2 * kind + 1] += missed + Integer.parseInt(counter.getAttribute("covered"));
          }
        }
      }
      return new Counts(counts[0], counts[1], counts[2], counts[3]);
    }

    boolean complete() {
      return linesMissed == 0 && branchesMissed == 0;
    }
  }

  /** Judges each report on its own and leaves the counts of each project as facts. */
  public static int command(Context context, List<String> args) throws IOException {
    PrintStream out = context.out();
    if (args.isEmpty()) {
      out.println(USAGE);
      return 2;
    }
    List<String> facts = new ArrayList<>();
    List<String> missed = new ArrayList<>();
    boolean complete = true;
    for (String report : args) {
      Path file = context.root().resolve(report);
      if (!Files.exists(file)) {
        out.println("coverage: no coverage report " + report);
        return 1;
      }
      Element top;
      try {
        top = Xml.read(file).getDocumentElement();
      } catch (IOException malformed) {
        out.println("coverage: " + malformed.getMessage());
        return 1;
      }
      Counts counts = Counts.of(top);
      // The report of a project with code that measured nothing proves nothing.
      String project = report.substring(0, report.indexOf('/'));
      if (counts.lines() == 0) {
        missed.add("coverage: " + project + " measured no line");
      }
      complete &= counts.complete() && counts.lines() > 0;
      facts.add(
          "%s lines %d of %d, branches %d of %d"
              .formatted(
                  project,
                  counts.lines() - counts.linesMissed(),
                  counts.lines(),
                  counts.branches() - counts.branchesMissed(),
                  counts.branches()));
      missed.addAll(missedIn(top));
    }
    missed.forEach(out::println);
    Facts.write(context.root(), "coverage", String.join("; ", facts));
    out.println("coverage: " + String.join("; ", facts));
    return complete ? 0 : 1;
  }

  private static List<String> missedIn(Element report) {
    List<String> missed = new ArrayList<>();
    NodeList classes = report.getElementsByTagName("class");
    for (int at = 0; at < classes.getLength(); at++) {
      Element type = (Element) classes.item(at);
      Counts counts = Counts.of(type);
      if (!counts.complete()) {
        missed.add(
            "coverage: %s: %d of %d lines, %d of %d branches missed"
                .formatted(
                    type.getAttribute("name").replace('/', '.'),
                    counts.linesMissed(),
                    counts.lines(),
                    counts.branchesMissed(),
                    counts.branches()));
      }
    }
    return missed;
  }
}
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools;

import dev.metis.tools.canary.CanaryRun;
import dev.metis.tools.coverage.Coverage;
import dev.metis.tools.deadcode.Deadcode;
import dev.metis.tools.language.Language;
import dev.metis.tools.lint.Marks;
import dev.metis.tools.tests.TestReports;
import dev.metis.tools.verify.Verify;
import java.io.IOException;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import org.jspecify.annotations.Nullable;

/** The commands of the tool of the checks. */
public final class Cli {

  private static final Map<String, Command> COMMANDS =
      Map.of(
          "verify", Verify::command,
          "canary", CanaryRun::command,
          "language", Language::command,
          "marks", Marks::command,
          "tests", TestReports::command,
          "deadcode", Deadcode::command,
          "coverage", Coverage::command);

  private static final String USAGE =
      """
      usage: verify [--only <check>[,<check>]] [--fast] [--append]
             canary <name>|all
             language [<path> ...]
             marks
             tests <check> <folder of test reports> ...
             deadcode <file of entry points> <project> ...
             coverage <JaCoCo XML report> ...""";

  private Cli() {}

  /** Runs the command the arguments name and returns its exit code. */
  public static int run(Context context, List<String> args) throws IOException {
    @Nullable Command command = args.isEmpty() ? null : COMMANDS.get(args.getFirst());
    if (command == null) {
      context.out().println(USAGE);
      return 2;
    }
    return command.run(context, args.subList(1, args.size()));
  }
}
```

```kotlin
// A command of the tool, run from the repository root, for a check of the root build to depend on.
fun tool(name: String, vararg arguments: String) =
    tasks.register<JavaExec>(name) {
        classpath = sourceSets.main.get().runtimeClasspath
        mainClass = application.mainClass
        workingDir = rootDir
        args(*arguments)
    }

tool("language", "language")
tool("marks", "marks")
// The walk resolves the types the classes of both projects extend, so it runs on their classpaths.
evaluationDependsOn(":core")
tool("deadcode", "deadcode", "config/entry-points.txt", "core", "tools").configure {
    val core = project(":core").the<SourceSetContainer>()
    classpath += core["test"].runtimeClasspath + sourceSets.test.get().runtimeClasspath
    dependsOn(":core:testClasses", tasks.testClasses)
}
// The judges of the test tasks, which run after the tests even when a test failed.
tool("judgeArchitecture", "tests", "architecture", "core/build/test-results/architectureTest", "tools/build/test-results/architectureTest")
    .configure { mustRunAfter(":core:architectureTest", tasks.named("architectureTest")) }
tool("judgeDeadcode", "tests", "deadcode", "core/build/test-results/deadcodeTest")
    .configure { mustRunAfter(":core:deadcodeTest") }
tool(
    "judgeCoverage", "coverage", "core/build/reports/jacoco/test/jacocoTestReport.xml",
    "tools/build/reports/jacoco/test/jacocoTestReport.xml",
).configure { mustRunAfter(":core:jacocoTestReport", tasks.jacocoTestReport) }
tool("judgeTooling", "tests", "tooling", "tools/build/test-results/test").configure { mustRunAfter(tasks.test) }
tool("judgeUnit", "tests", "unit", "core/build/test-results/test").configure { mustRunAfter(":core:test") }

// ./verify and ./canary start the tool with the Java and the classpath this task writes, and the tool
// learns from it the check tasks Gradle has in every project, however a build file declares them.
val launcher = tasks.register("launcher") {
    val executable = javaToolchains.launcherFor(java.toolchain).map { it.executablePath.asFile.path }
    val classpath = sourceSets.main.map { it.runtimeClasspath }
    val checks = rootProject.allprojects.flatMap { project ->
        val prefix = if (project == rootProject) "" else project.path + ":"
        project.tasks.names.filter { it.matches(Regex("check[A-Z]\\w*")) }.map { prefix + it }
    }
    val folder = layout.buildDirectory.dir("launcher")
    inputs.files(classpath)
    inputs.property("java", executable)
    inputs.property("checks", checks)
    outputs.dir(folder)
    doLast {
        folder.get().file("java").asFile.writeText(executable.get() + "\n")
        folder.get().file("args").asFile.writeText("-cp\n\"" + classpath.get().asPath + "\"\n")
        folder.get().file("checks").asFile.writeText(checks.joinToString("") { "$it\n" })
    }
}

// The tests of the counter-tests read the list of checks the launcher writes.
tasks.named("testClasses") { dependsOn(launcher) }
```

```kotlin
// A check whose judge did not run would pass on the exit of its tasks alone, so a check that owes
// facts fails without them; ./verify and ./canary clear the facts before each run of a check.
val factFree = setOf("checkFormat", "checkCompile", "checkDeps", "checkSecrets")

configure<com.autonomousapps.DependencyAnalysisExtension> {

gradle.projectsEvaluated {

    val declared =
        subprojects.flatMap { project ->
            project.configurations.flatMap { configuration ->

                    .filter { "${it.group}:${it.name}" in members }
                    .map { "${it.group}:${it.name} in ${project.path} ${configuration.name}" }
            }
        }
    bundled.configure {
        doLast {
            if (declared.isNotEmpty()) {
                throw GradleException("a bundle names what a project declares, which it would never report: $declared")
            }
        }
    }
}
```

### Task 14: The mutation check

PIT 1.30.0 with the mutator group STRONGER over both projects, without its threshold: the command `mutation` judges each project of the scope on its own and requires every mutant detected, none SURVIVED and none NO_COVERAGE. PIT writes no file at all for classes without a mutant, as the core's are today, so its task leaves a trace, `build/reports/pitest/ran`; a project of the scope without that trace is red, never counted as one without mutants, and a full run without a mutant is red, since it proves nothing. Before each run the command `mutation-scope` writes `build/mutation/scope.properties`: the classes of `-Pmutate=<globs>`, else the classes changed since `MUTATION_BASE` (a changed source with its nested classes, the source a changed test stands for, every class of a project when a shared test or a test without a source changed), else every class. The scope removes the reports and the trace of an earlier run, and a project without a class in the scope skips PIT. Git learns `changedSince`, and a counter-test learns `arguments`, which keeps the mutation counter-tests to the core and one package of the tool.

```java
package dev.metis.tools;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThatThrownBy;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.io.UncheckedIOException;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.function.Function;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.io.TempDir;

class GitTest {

  private static final List<String> LIST =
      List.of("ls-files", "-co", "--exclude-standard", "-z", "--", ".");
  private static final List<String> STATUS =
      List.of("--no-optional-locks", "status", "--porcelain", "--", ".");
  private static final String PINNED = "pinned/brand/tokens.css";

  @TempDir Path root;

  // A git stand-in that answers each command it knows with its result and fails the test otherwise.
  private static Function<List<String>, Processes.Result> answering(
      Map<List<String>, Processes.Result> answers) {
    return args -> {
      assertThat(answers).containsKey(args);
      return answers.get(args);
    };
  }

  private static Processes.Result ok(String output) {
    return new Processes.Result(0, output);
  }

  private static String listed(String... paths) {
    return String.join("\0", paths) + "\0";
  }

  private Git gitListing(String listing, String status) {
    return new Git(root, answering(Map.of(LIST, ok(listing), STATUS, ok(status))));
  }

  private void write(String path, String text) throws IOException {
    Files.createDirectories(root.resolve(path).getParent());
    Files.writeString(root.resolve(path), text);
  }

  @Test
  void theTreeHashesThePathAndBytesOfEachListedFileAndCountsTheChanges() throws IOException {
    write("a.txt", "a\n");
    write("src/b.txt", "b\n");
    write("notes.txt", "not listed\n");
    write(PINNED, ":root {}\n");
    String status = "?? a.txt\n M src/b.txt\n";
    String tree = gitListing(listed("src/b.txt", "a.txt", PINNED), status).tree();
    assertThat(tree).matches("[0-9a-f]{12} \\(2 uncommitted\\)");
    // Listing order, a path listed twice, a deleted file and unlisted files leave the hash alone.
    Git same = gitListing(listed("a.txt", PINNED, "src/b.txt", "a.txt", "gone.txt"), status);
    write("notes.txt", "edited\n");
    assertThat(same.tree()).isEqualTo(tree);
    for (String file : List.of("src/b.txt", PINNED)) {
      String before = Files.readString(root.resolve(file));
      write(file, "changed\n");
      assertThat(same.tree()).as(file).isNotEqualTo(tree);
      write(file, before);
    }
    assertThat(same.tree()).isEqualTo(tree);
  }

  @Test
  void aPathIsPartOfTheHashSoTheSameBytesUnderAnotherNameAreAnotherTree() throws IOException {
    write("a.txt", "x\n");
    write("b.txt", "x\n");
    assertThat(gitListing(listed("a.txt"), "").tree())
        .isNotEqualTo(gitListing(listed("b.txt"), "").tree());
  }

  @Test
  void theBytesOfOneFileCannotPassForTheNameOfTheNext() throws IOException {
    write("a.txt", "x");
    write("b.txt", "y");
    String two = gitListing(listed("a.txt", "b.txt"), "").tree();
    write("a.txt", "xb.txt\0y");
    assertThat(gitListing(listed("a.txt"), "").tree()).isNotEqualTo(two);
  }

  @Test
  void theTreeCountsEveryLineOfTheStatusAndNothingElse() throws IOException {
    write("a.txt", "a\n");
    String clean = gitListing(listed("a.txt"), "").tree();
    assertThat(clean).endsWith(" (0 uncommitted)");
    assertThat(gitListing(listed("a.txt"), " M a.txt\n").tree())
        .isEqualTo(clean.replace("(0", "(1"));
  }

  @Test
  void theFilesAreTheListedOnesThatExistInPathOrder() throws IOException {
    write("b.txt", "");
    write("a/c.txt", "");
    Files.createDirectories(root.resolve("folder"));
    Git git = gitListing(listed("b.txt", "gone.txt", "a/c.txt", "b.txt", "folder"), "");
    assertThat(git.files()).contains(List.of("a/c.txt", "b.txt"));
  }

  @Test
  void whereGitCannotListTheFilesTheTreeIsUnknownAndThereAreNoFiles() throws IOException {
    write("a.txt", "a\n");
    Processes.Result failed = new Processes.Result(128, "fatal: not a git repository");
    List<Git> lost =
        List.of(
            new Git(root, answering(Map.of(LIST, failed, STATUS, ok("")))),
            new Git(root, answering(Map.of(LIST, ok(listed("a.txt")), STATUS, failed))),
            new Git(
                root,
                args -> {
                  throw new UncheckedIOException(new IOException("git: not found"));
                }));
    for (Git git : lost) {
      assertThat(git.tree()).isEqualTo(Git.UNKNOWN);
    }
    assertThat(lost.getFirst().files()).isEmpty();
    assertThat(lost.getLast().files()).isEmpty();
  }

  @Test
  void aListedFileThatCannotBeReadMakesTheTreeUnknown() throws IOException {
    write("a.txt", "a\n");
    Git git = gitListing(listed("a.txt"), "");
    assertThat(root.resolve("a.txt").toFile().setReadable(false)).isTrue();
    try {
      assertThat(git.tree()).isEqualTo(Git.UNKNOWN);
    } finally {
      assertThat(root.resolve("a.txt").toFile().setReadable(true)).isTrue();
    }
  }

  @Test
  void theCommitIsHeadOrNoneBeforeTheFirstCommit() {
    List<String> head = List.of("rev-parse", "HEAD");
    assertThat(new Git(root, answering(Map.of(head, ok("abc123\n")))).commit()).isEqualTo("abc123");
    Processes.Result none = new Processes.Result(128, "fatal: ambiguous argument 'HEAD'");
    assertThat(new Git(root, answering(Map.of(head, none))).commit()).isEqualTo("none");
  }

  @Test
  void theChangesSinceABaseAreThePathsTheDiffNames() throws IOException {
    List<String> diff = List.of("diff", "--name-only", "-z", "--relative", "origin/main...HEAD");
    Git git = new Git(root, answering(Map.of(diff, ok(listed("a.txt", "src/b.txt")))));
    assertThat(git.changedSince("origin/main")).containsExactly("a.txt", "src/b.txt");
    Git none = new Git(root, answering(Map.of(diff, ok(""))));
    assertThat(none.changedSince("origin/main")).isEmpty();
    Git bad = new Git(root, answering(Map.of(diff, new Processes.Result(128, "fatal: bad\n"))));
    assertThatThrownBy(() -> bad.changedSince("origin/main"))
        .isInstanceOf(IOException.class)
        .hasMessage("cannot list the changes since origin/main: fatal: bad");
  }

  @Test
  void aBaseTheRealGitCannotReadFailsWithTheReasonGitGives() {
    assertThat(Processes.run(root, List.of("git", "init", "-q")).status()).isZero();
    Git git =
        new Git(
            root,
            args -> {
              List<String> command = new ArrayList<>(List.of("git"));
              command.addAll(args);
              return Processes.quiet(root, command);
            });
    assertThatThrownBy(() -> git.changedSince("origin/no-such-branch"))
        .isInstanceOf(IOException.class)
        .hasMessageStartingWith("cannot list the changes since origin/no-such-branch: fatal: ");
  }

  @Test
  void withTheRealGitTheTreeNamesTheFilesItWouldCommit() throws IOException {
    List<List<String>> asked = new ArrayList<>();
    Git git =
        new Git(
            root,
            args -> {
              asked.add(args);
              List<String> command = new ArrayList<>(List.of("git"));
              command.addAll(args);
              return Processes.run(root, command);
            });
    assertThat(git.tree()).isEqualTo(Git.UNKNOWN);
    assertThat(Processes.run(root, List.of("git", "init", "-q")).status()).isZero();
    write(".gitignore", "build/\n");
    write("a.txt", "a\n");
    write("build/out.txt", "ignored\n");
    assertThat(git.files()).contains(List.of(".gitignore", "a.txt"));
    assertThat(git.tree()).matches("[0-9a-f]{12} \\(2 uncommitted\\)");
    assertThat(git.commit()).isEqualTo("none");
    assertThat(asked).contains(LIST, STATUS, List.of("rev-parse", "HEAD"));
  }
}
```
