`tools/src/main/java/dev/metis/tools/canary/DepsCanaries.java`:

```java
package dev.metis.tools.canary;

import java.util.List;

/** The counter-tests of the deps check. */
final class DepsCanaries {

  static final List<Canary> ALL =
      List.of(
          // A line of the lock file names the library, so Trivy needs no build to see it.
          Canary.of("deps-vulnerability", "deps", "CVE-2021-44228")
              .appending(
                  "core/gradle.lockfile",
                  "org.apache.logging.log4j:log4j-core:2.14.1=runtimeClasspath\n"),
          // A library the build asks for and the lock file of the core does not hold.
          Canary.of("deps-lock", "deps", "not part of the dependency lock state")
              .appending(
                  "core/build.gradle.kts",
                  "\ndependencies {\n    implementation(libs.archunit)\n}\n"),
          // A checksum that no longer matches a library only the tests of the core resolve, so the
          // check's own resolution, not the plugins of the build, must find it.
          Canary.of(
                  "deps-checksum", "deps", "One artifact failed verification: awaitility-4.3.0.jar")
              .replacing(
                  "gradle/verification-metadata.xml",
                  "ee58568ea5945dcf988551501655183dc184e23e45a8e013fdfd9036194e6f7b",
                  "0".repeat(64)),
          // A list that no longer allows a licence a shipped library carries.
          Canary.of("deps-licence", "deps", "do not declare at least one allowed license")
              .writing(
                  "config/allowed-licenses.json",
                  """
                  {
                    "allowedLicenses": [
                      { "moduleLicense": "Apache-2.0" }
                    ]
                  }
                  """));

  private DepsCanaries() {}
}
```

`tools/src/main/java/dev/metis/tools/canary/SecretsCanaries.java`:

```java
package dev.metis.tools.canary;

import java.util.List;

/** The counter-tests of the secrets check. */
final class SecretsCanaries {

  // Joined from pieces, so that this file holds no key gitleaks would find.
  private static final String KEY =
      "-----BEGIN "
          + "PRIVATE KEY-----\n"
          + "MIIEvQIBADANBgkqhkiG9w0BAQEFAASCBKcwggSjAgEAAoIBAQC7".repeat(2)
          + "\n-----END "
          + "PRIVATE KEY-----\n";

  static final List<Canary> ALL =
      List.of(
          Canary.of("secrets-private-key", "secrets", "private-key")
              .writing("core/src/main/resources/canary.pem", KEY),
          // A key in a package named like the folder a build writes, which only Gradle's own are.
          Canary.of("secrets-nested-build", "secrets", "dev/metis/core/build/canary.pem")
              .writing(Canaries.CORE + "build/canary.pem", KEY));

  private SecretsCanaries() {}
}
```

`tools/src/main/java/dev/metis/tools/canary/Canaries.java`:

```java
package dev.metis.tools.canary;

import java.util.List;
import java.util.stream.Stream;

/** Every counter-test, in the order ./canary all runs them. */
public final class Canaries {

  /** The folder of the core's own classes, where most canaries plant a class. */
  static final String CORE = "core/src/main/java/dev/metis/core/";

  /** Every counter-test, one list per check. */
  public static final List<Canary> ALL =
      Stream.of(
              FormatCanaries.ALL,
              CompileCanaries.ALL,
              LintCanaries.ALL,
              LanguageCanaries.ALL,
              ArchitectureCanaries.ALL,
              DeadcodeCanaries.ALL,
              ToolingCanaries.ALL,
              UnitCanaries.ALL,
              CoverageCanaries.ALL,
              MutationCanaries.ALL,
              DepsCanaries.ALL,
              SecretsCanaries.ALL)
          .flatMap(List::stream)
          .toList();

  private Canaries() {}
```

### Task 16: The container

The image of the core, built from the sources with Docker alone, in two stages. The build stage (Corretto 25 on Amazon Linux 2023) runs the wrapper's own class, since that image lacks the `xargs` that `gradlew` needs, builds `:core:bootJar` with half the processors and the Gradle cache in a cache mount, and extracts the layers of the jar. The runtime stage (the headless Corretto 25) applies the security fixes of the Amazon Linux release `2023.12.20261013`, pinned so that every build installs the same packages (the base reads its own, older release), copies the four layers, runs as the user 10001 and starts the JVM as the first process. When the image scan turns red, the release is bumped together with the digest of the base, as the Global Constraints say. `stack/compose.yaml` runs the core alone, locked down; it is the one description of how the image runs, and the image check of Task 17 runs the image from it, with the image, a free port and a time zone that is not UTC given through `METIS_IMAGE`, `METIS_PORT` and `METIS_TIME_ZONE`.

**Files:**

- Create: `stack/compose.yaml`
- Create: `.dockerignore`
- Create: `core/Dockerfile`

**Interfaces:**

- Consumes: the application of Task 2; the settings, catalog, convention plugin, lock files, checksums and configuration of Tasks 1 to 15, which the build stage copies to build the same jar.
- Produces: the image `metis-core:local`, built by `docker compose --file stack/compose.yaml up --build --wait`.

`stack/compose.yaml`:

```yaml
# The local stack runs the image as a deployment runs it: docker compose -f stack/compose.yaml up --build --wait
name: metis

services:
  core:
    build:
      context: ..
      dockerfile: core/Dockerfile
    image: ${METIS_IMAGE:-metis-core:local}
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:${METIS_PORT-8080}:8080"
    environment:
      TZ: ${METIS_TIME_ZONE:-UTC}
    read_only: true
    tmpfs:
      - /tmp
    cap_drop:
      - ALL
    security_opt:
      - no-new-privileges:true
    cpus: 1
    mem_limit: 2g
    stop_grace_period: 30s
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "curl", "--fail", "--silent", "http://localhost:8080/actuator/health/readiness"]
      interval: 2s
      timeout: 2s
      retries: 30
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Write the image**

`.dockerignore`:

```text

**/.gradle
**/.kotlin
build
*/build
.claude
.git
reports
```

`core/Dockerfile`:

```dockerfile
# Built from the sources with Docker alone: docker build -f core/Dockerfile .
FROM amazoncorretto:25-al2023@sha256:06f99cdfd01c26ed2a5b03dc85385d36c17aa81ddfcaf8500f641ab556a985d6 AS build
WORKDIR /workspace
COPY gradlew gradle.properties settings.gradle.kts settings-gradle.lockfile build.gradle.kts gradle.lockfile ./
COPY gradle gradle
COPY build-logic build-logic
COPY config config
COPY tools/build.gradle.kts tools/gradle.lockfile tools/
COPY core core
# The wrapper's own class runs Gradle, since gradlew needs xargs; the cache keeps Gradle between builds.
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.gradle \
    java -cp gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.jar org.gradle.wrapper.GradleWrapperMain --no-daemon --console=plain \
        --max-workers="$(( ($(nproc) + 1) / 2 ))" :core:bootJar \
    && java -Djarmode=tools -jar core/build/libs/core.jar extract --layers --destination extracted

FROM amazoncorretto:25-al2023-headless@sha256:2cffa0f4e8eaf0d1473e1eb5b484d178f00c73444360dccd35758bcef0847224
# The security fixes of one later release, pinned so that every build installs the same packages.
RUN dnf upgrade --assumeyes --releasever=2023.12.20261013 --security && dnf clean all
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=build /workspace/extracted/dependencies/ ./
COPY --from=build /workspace/extracted/spring-boot-loader/ ./
COPY --from=build /workspace/extracted/snapshot-dependencies/ ./
COPY --from=build /workspace/extracted/application/ ./
USER 10001:10001
EXPOSE 8080
# The heap follows the memory limit of the container, and an out-of-memory error ends the process so that the platform restarts it.
ENTRYPOINT ["java", "-XX:MaxRAMPercentage=75", "-XX:+ExitOnOutOfMemoryError", "-jar", "core.jar"]
```

### Task 17: The image check

The command `image` checks the image the way a deployment runs it, from `stack/compose.yaml`, under a project of its own on a free port, so a local stack that runs is left alone, and starts and ends with `down --volumes`, so each run starts from nothing. The container the stack starts runs, as `docker inspect` reads it back, with a read-only root file system, one temporary folder, no capability and none added, no privileged mode, no mount, no new privilege, one processor, 2 GB and 30 seconds of grace, in the time zone Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh. Inside the running core, whatever the image or the compose file say, `id -u` does not print 0, the JVM holds no capability, effective or bounding, the root is mounted read-only and no build tool (`javac`, `jar`, `gradle`, `mvn`) is found; a probe that fails or prints no user is red. Readiness answers `{"status":"UP"}` within 60 seconds and liveness answers the same; a stop signal ends the JVM inside the grace period with the exit code 143. The content size of the image, the seconds to ready and the memory in use go into the facts. `checkImage` also runs hadolint on the Dockerfile and Trivy on an archive of the image, so no scanner gets a hand on the Docker daemon. Plan two adds PostgreSQL and the migration job to the compose file, and the check keeps its shape.

`tools/src/test/java/dev/metis/tools/TestContext.java`:

```java
package dev.metis.tools;

import java.io.ByteArrayOutputStream;
import java.io.PrintStream;
import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.time.Instant;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.function.BiFunction;
import java.util.function.ToIntBiFunction;

/** A context for the tests of a command: its output is kept, and an edge not given fails. */
public final class TestContext {

  /** The time of the first stamp; each stamp is a second later than the one before. */
  public static final Instant START = Instant.parse("2026-10-14T00:00:00Z");

  /** The exit code a test keeps beside the context, for a helper that runs the command. */
  public int exit;

  private final ByteArrayOutputStream printed = new ByteArrayOutputStream();
  private final Path root;
  private BiFunction<Path, List<String>, Processes.Result> run = TestContext::unexpected;
  private ToIntBiFunction<Path, List<String>> inherit =
      (dir, command) -> unexpected(dir, command).status();
  private long step = 1_500_000_000L;
  private long nanos;
  private long stamps;

  public TestContext(Path root) {
    this.root = root;
  }

  private static Processes.Result unexpected(Path dir, List<String> command) {
    throw new AssertionError("unexpected command in " + dir + ": " + command);
  }

  public TestContext run(BiFunction<Path, List<String>, Processes.Result> run) {
    this.run = run;
    return this;
  }

  public TestContext inherit(ToIntBiFunction<Path, List<String>> inherit) {
    this.inherit = inherit;
    return this;
  }

  /** The nanoseconds the clock moves on each read. */
  public TestContext step(long nanos) {
    this.step = nanos;
    return this;
  }

  /** The context, whose clock moves 1.5 seconds on each read unless a step is given. */
  public Context context() {
    return new Context(
        root,
        new PrintStream(printed, true, StandardCharsets.UTF_8),
        run,
        run,
        inherit,
        () -> nanos += step,
        () -> START.plusSeconds(stamps++),
        3);
  }

  /** What the command printed. */
  public String printed() {
    return printed.toString(StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
  }
}
```

`tools/src/test/java/dev/metis/tools/image/ImageCheckTest.java`:

```java
package dev.metis.tools.image;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

import dev.metis.tools.Facts;
import dev.metis.tools.Processes;
import dev.metis.tools.TestContext;
import java.io.IOException;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.HashMap;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.io.TempDir;

class ImageCheckTest {

  private static final String IMAGE = "metis-core:check";
  private static final String UP = "{\"status\":\"UP\"}";
  private static final String LOCKED =
      "true|[\"ALL\"]|[\"no-new-privileges:true\"]|2147483648|1000000000|{\"/tmp\":\"\"}|30"
          + "|null|false|[]";
  private static final String INSIDE =
      "10001\nCapEff:\t0000000000000000\nCapBnd:\t0000000000000000\noverlay / overlay ro,relatime 0 0\n";
  private static final List<String> COMPOSE =
      List.of(
          "env",
          "METIS_IMAGE=" + IMAGE,
          "METIS_PORT=",
          "METIS_TIME_ZONE=Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh",
          "docker",
          "compose",
          "--project-name",
          "metis-check",
          "--file",
          "stack/compose.yaml");

  @TempDir Path root;

  private final List<List<String>> calls = new ArrayList<>();
  // What each docker command answers, by its verb and the word that tells it apart.
  private final Map<String, Processes.Result> answers =
      new HashMap<>(
          Map.ofEntries(
              Map.entry("image inspect", ok("182886790\n")),
              Map.entry("exec probe", ok(INSIDE)),
              Map.entry("compose down", ok("")),
              Map.entry("compose up", ok("")),
              Map.entry("compose stop", ok("")),
              Map.entry("compose logs", ok("core-1  | {\"message\":\"Started\"}\n")),
              Map.entry("inspect lockdown", ok(LOCKED + "\n")),
              Map.entry("exec readiness", ok(UP)),
              Map.entry("exec liveness", ok(UP)),
              Map.entry("stats --no-stream", ok("123.6MiB / 2GiB\n")),
              Map.entry("inspect exit", ok("143\n"))));

  private static Processes.Result ok(String output) {
    return new Processes.Result(0, output);
  }

  private static String key(List<String> command) {
    List<String> words =
        command.stream().dropWhile(word -> word.equals("env") || word.contains("=")).toList();
    assertThat(words.getFirst()).isEqualTo("docker");
    return switch (words.get(1)) {
      case "compose" -> "compose " + words.get(6);
      case "exec" ->
          words.contains("curl")
              ? "exec " + (words.getLast().endsWith("readiness") ? "readiness" : "liveness")
              : "exec probe";
      case "inspect" -> words.get(3).contains("Readonly") ? "inspect lockdown" : "inspect exit";
      default -> words.get(1) + " " + words.get(2);
    };
  }

  private TestContext check(String... args) throws IOException {
    return check(1_500_000_000L, args);
  }

  private TestContext check(long step, String... args) throws IOException {
    TestContext test =
        new TestContext(root)
            .step(step)
            .run(
                (dir, command) -> {
                  calls.add(command);
                  String key = key(command);
                  return answers.getOrDefault(key, new Processes.Result(99, "unexpected " + key));
                });
    test.exit = ImageCheck.command(test.context(), List.of(args));
    return test;
  }

  private static List<String> compose(String... args) {
    List<String> command = new ArrayList<>(COMPOSE);
    command.addAll(List.of(args));
    return command;
  }

  @Test
  void anImageTheStackRunsLockedDownThatAnswersItsProbesAndStopsIsGreenWithItsMeasures()
      throws IOException {
    TestContext test = check(IMAGE);
    assertThat(test.exit).isZero();
    String facts = "image content 182.9 MB, ready in 1.5 s, memory 123.6MiB";
    assertThat(test.printed()).isEqualTo("image: " + facts + "\n");
    assertThat(Facts.read(root, "image")).hasValue(facts);
    assertThat(calls.get(1)).isEqualTo(compose("down", "--volumes"));
    assertThat(calls)
        .contains(
            compose("up", "--detach", "--no-build"),
            compose("stop"),
            List.of(
                "docker",
                "stats",
                "--no-stream",
                "--format",
                "{{.MemUsage}}",
                "metis-check-core-1"));
    assertThat(calls.getLast()).isEqualTo(compose("down", "--volumes"));
  }

  @Test
  void aCoreThatRunsAsRootHoldsACapabilityHasAWritableRootOrABuildToolIsRed() throws IOException {
    answers.put("exec probe", ok(INSIDE.replaceFirst("10001", "0")));
    assertThat(check(IMAGE).printed()).startsWith("image: the core runs as root\n");
    answers.put(
        "exec probe", ok(INSIDE.replace("CapBnd:\t0000000000000000", "CapBnd:\t0000000000002000")));
    assertThat(check(IMAGE).printed())
        .startsWith(
            "image: the core runs with a capability: CapEff: 0000000000000000, CapBnd:"
                + " 0000000000002000\n");
    answers.put(
        "exec probe", ok(INSIDE.replace("CapEff:\t0000000000000000", "CapEff:\t0000000000000400")));
    assertThat(check(IMAGE).printed()).startsWith("image: the core runs with a capability: ");
    answers.put("exec probe", ok(INSIDE.replace(" ro,relatime", " rw,relatime,lowerdir=/a:/b")));
    assertThat(check(IMAGE).printed())
        .startsWith("image: the root file system of the core is writable: rw\n");
    answers.put("exec probe", ok(INSIDE + "/usr/bin/javac\n/usr/bin/jar\n"));
    TestContext tools = check(IMAGE);
    assertThat(tools.exit).isEqualTo(1);
    assertThat(tools.printed())
        .startsWith("image: the image holds a build tool: /usr/bin/javac /usr/bin/jar\n");
  }

  @Test
  void aProbeOfTheCoreThatFailsOrPrintsNoUserProvesNothingAndIsRed() throws IOException {
    for (Processes.Result probe :
        List.of(
            new Processes.Result(1, "sh: line 1: id: command not found\n"),
            new Processes.Result(1, INSIDE),
            ok(INSIDE.substring(0, INSIDE.indexOf("overlay"))),
            ok("x\n" + INSIDE.substring(INSIDE.indexOf('\n') + 1)),
            ok("10001\nCapEff:\t0000000000000000\n"),
            ok(INSIDE.replace("overlay / overlay ro,relatime 0 0", "none")))) {
      answers.put("exec probe", probe);
      TestContext test = check(IMAGE);
      assertThat(test.exit).as(probe.output()).isEqualTo(1);
      assertThat(test.printed())
          .as(probe.output())
          .startsWith("image: cannot read the user and the capabilities of the core: ");
    }
  }

  @Test
  void aStackThatDoesNotRunTheCoreLockedDownIsRedWithWhatItRunsWith() throws IOException {
    String writable = LOCKED.replace("null|false", "[\"CAP_NET_RAW\"]|false");
    answers.put("inspect lockdown", ok(writable + "\n"));
    TestContext test = check(IMAGE);
    assertThat(test.exit).isEqualTo(1);
    assertThat(test.printed())
        .startsWith("image: the stack does not run the core locked down: " + writable + "\n");
  }

  @Test
  void aContainerThatIsNeverReadyIsRedAndItsLastLinesOfLogShow() throws IOException {
    answers.put("exec readiness", new Processes.Result(1, "Error: container is not running"));
    answers.put(
        "compose logs", ok("core-1  | touch: cannot touch '/started': Read-only file system\n"));
    TestContext test = check(IMAGE);
    assertThat(test.exit).isEqualTo(1);
    assertThat(test.printed())
        .isEqualTo(
            """
            image: the container was never ready
            image: core-1  | touch: cannot touch '/started': Read-only file system
            image: image content 182.9 MB, never ready
            """);
    assertThat(calls.getLast()).isEqualTo(compose("down", "--volumes"));
  }

  @Test
  void aProbeThatAnswersWithDetailOrAStackThatDoesNotStartIsRed() throws IOException {
    answers.put("exec liveness", ok("{\"status\":\"UP\",\"components\":{}}"));
    assertThat(check(IMAGE).printed())
        .startsWith("image: liveness answered {\"status\":\"UP\",\"components\":{}}\n");
    answers.put("compose up", new Processes.Result(1, "Error response from daemon\n"));
    TestContext start = check(IMAGE);
    assertThat(start.exit).isEqualTo(1);
    assertThat(start.printed())
        .isEqualTo(
            """
            image: the stack did not start: Error response from daemon
            image: image content 182.9 MB, never started
            """);
  }

  @Test
  void aReadinessThatFailsOrAnswersAnythingButUpIsNeverReadyAndSixtySecondsAreInTime()
      throws IOException {
    answers.put("exec readiness", ok("{\"status\":\"DOWN\"}"));
    assertThat(check(IMAGE).printed()).startsWith("image: the container was never ready\n");
    answers.put("exec readiness", new Processes.Result(28, UP));
    assertThat(check(IMAGE).printed()).startsWith("image: the container was never ready\n");
    answers.put("exec readiness", ok(UP));
    assertThat(check(60_000_000_000L, IMAGE).printed()).doesNotContain("past 60 s");
  }

  @Test
  void aContainerReadyAfterTheMinuteOrStoppedAfterTheGracePeriodIsRed() throws IOException {
    TestContext slow = check(61_000_000_000L, IMAGE);
    assertThat(slow.exit).isEqualTo(1);
    assertThat(slow.printed())
        .isEqualTo(
            """
            image: ready after 61.0 s, past 60 s
            image: a stop signal did not end the JVM inside the grace period: exit 143 after 61.0 s
            image: image content 182.9 MB, ready in 61.0 s, memory 123.6MiB
            """);
    TestContext grace = check(30_000_000_000L, IMAGE);
    assertThat(grace.printed())
        .startsWith(
            "image: a stop signal did not end the JVM inside the grace period: exit 143 after 30.0 s\n");
  }

  @Test
  void aStopSignalThatDoesNotEndTheJvmInsideTheGracePeriodIsRed() throws IOException {
    answers.put("inspect exit", ok("137\n"));
    TestContext test = check(IMAGE);
    assertThat(test.exit).isEqualTo(1);
    assertThat(test.printed())
        .startsWith(
            "image: a stop signal did not end the JVM inside the grace period: exit 137 after 1.5 s\n");
  }

  @Test
  void aMissingImageOrNoImageNamedStopsTheCheck() throws IOException {
    answers.put("image inspect", new Processes.Result(1, "Error: No such image\n"));
    TestContext missing = check(IMAGE);
    assertThat(missing.exit).isEqualTo(1);
    assertThat(missing.printed())
        .isEqualTo("image: no image metis-core:check: Error: No such image\n");
    TestContext usage = check();
    assertThat(usage.exit).isEqualTo(2);
    assertThat(usage.printed()).isEqualTo("usage: image <image>\n");
  }
}
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools.image;

import dev.metis.tools.Context;
import dev.metis.tools.Facts;
import dev.metis.tools.Processes;
import java.io.IOException;
import java.io.PrintStream;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Locale;
import java.util.regex.Matcher;
import java.util.regex.Pattern;

/** Runs the image from the compose file of the stack, as a deployment does, and records it. */
public final class ImageCheck {

  // A project of its own on a free port, so a local stack that runs is left alone.
  private static final List<String> COMPOSE =
      List.of("docker", "compose", "--project-name", "metis-check", "--file", "stack/compose.yaml");
  private static final String CONTAINER = "metis-check-core-1";
  private static final String LOCKDOWN =
      "{{.HostConfig.ReadonlyRootfs}}|{{json .HostConfig.CapDrop}}|{{json .HostConfig.SecurityOpt}}"
          + "|{{.HostConfig.Memory}}|{{.HostConfig.NanoCpus}}|{{json .HostConfig.Tmpfs}}"
          + "|{{.Config.StopTimeout}}|{{json .HostConfig.CapAdd}}|{{.HostConfig.Privileged}}"
          + "|{{json .Mounts}}";
  // A read-only root with one temporary folder, no capability, no new privilege, 2 GB, one
  // processor, 30 seconds of grace, nothing added, no privileged mode and no mount, as compose
  // must say.
  private static final String LOCKED =
      "true|[\"ALL\"]|[\"no-new-privileges:true\"]|2147483648|1000000000|{\"/tmp\":\"\"}|30"
          + "|null|false|[]";
  private static final String UP = "{\"status\":\"UP\"}";
  private static final int READY_SECONDS = 60;
  private static final int GRACE_SECONDS = 30;
  // The running core itself: its user, its capabilities, its root mount and any build tool.
  private static final String PROBE =
      "id -u || exit 1; grep -E '^Cap(Eff|Bnd):' /proc/1/status || exit 1; grep ' / ' /proc/mounts"
          + " || exit 1; for tool in javac jar gradle mvn; do command -v \"$tool\"; done; exit 0";
  private static final Pattern NO_CAPABILITY = Pattern.compile("Cap(Eff|Bnd):\\s+0+");
  private static final Pattern ROOT_MOUNT = Pattern.compile("\\S+ / \\S+ (\\S+) .*");
  private final Context context;
  private final String image;
  private final List<String> problems = new ArrayList<>();

  private ImageCheck(Context context, String image) {
    this.context = context;
    this.image = image;
  }

  /** Checks the image the argument names and leaves its measures as facts. */
  public static int command(Context context, List<String> args) throws IOException {
    PrintStream out = context.out();
    if (args.size() != 1) {
      out.println("usage: image <image>");
      return 2;
    }
    ImageCheck check = new ImageCheck(context, args.getFirst());
    Processes.Result size = check.docker("image", "inspect", "--format", "{{.Size}}", check.image);
    if (size.status() != 0) {
      out.println("image: no image " + check.image + ": " + size.output().strip());
      return 1;
    }
    String facts =
        String.format(
                Locale.ROOT, "image content %.1f MB, ", Long.parseLong(size.output().strip()) / 1e6)
            + check.run();
    check.problems.forEach(problem -> out.println("image: " + problem));
    out.println("image: " + facts);
    Facts.write(context.root(), "image", facts);
    return check.problems.isEmpty() ? 0 : 1;
  }

  // Runs the stack with the image and gives the facts after the size; each run starts from
  // nothing, the volumes of the project included.
  private String run() {
    compose("down", "--volumes");
    Processes.Result started = compose("up", "--detach", "--no-build");
    try {
      if (started.status() != 0) {
        problems.add("the stack did not start: " + started.output().strip());
        return "never started";
      }
      return running();
    } finally {
      compose("down", "--volumes");
    }
  }

  private String running() {
    String locked = docker("inspect", "--format", LOCKDOWN, CONTAINER).output().strip();
    if (!locked.equals(LOCKED)) {
      problems.add("the stack does not run the core locked down: " + locked);
    }
    long start = context.nanos().getAsLong();
    Processes.Result ready = probe("readiness", READY_SECONDS);
    double seconds = (context.nanos().getAsLong() - start) / 1e9;
    if (ready.status() != 0 || !ready.output().strip().equals(UP)) {
      problems.add("the container was never ready");
      compose("logs", "--no-color", "--tail", "20").output().strip().lines().forEach(problems::add);
      return "never ready";
    }
    if (seconds > READY_SECONDS) {
      problems.add(
          String.format(Locale.ROOT, "ready after %.1f s, past %d s", seconds, READY_SECONDS));
    }
    inside();
    Processes.Result live = probe("liveness", 0);
    if (!live.output().strip().equals(UP)) {
      problems.add("liveness answered " + live.output().strip());
    }
    String memory =
        docker("stats", "--no-stream", "--format", "{{.MemUsage}}", CONTAINER).output().strip();
    stop();
    return String.format(
        Locale.ROOT, "ready in %.1f s, memory %s", seconds, memory.replaceAll(" /.*", ""));
  }

  // Whatever the image or the compose file say, the running core is not the user 0, holds no
  // capability, has a read-only root and no build tool; a probe that fails proves none of it.
  private void inside() {
    Processes.Result probe =
        context
            .quiet()
            .apply(context.root(), List.of("docker", "exec", CONTAINER, "sh", "-c", PROBE));
    List<String> lines = probe.output().strip().lines().toList();
    Matcher mount = ROOT_MOUNT.matcher(lines.size() > 3 ? lines.get(3) : "");
    if (probe.status() != 0 || !lines.getFirst().matches("\\d+") || !mount.matches()) {
      problems.add(
          "cannot read the user and the capabilities of the core: " + probe.output().strip());
      return;
    }
    if (lines.getFirst().equals("0")) {
      problems.add("the core runs as root");
    }
    if (!NO_CAPABILITY.matcher(lines.get(1)).matches()
        || !NO_CAPABILITY.matcher(lines.get(2)).matches()) {
      problems.add(
          "the core runs with a capability: "
              + (lines.get(1) + ", " + lines.get(2)).replaceAll("\\s+", " "));
    }
    // The first option of the mount says how it is mounted; the others name the layers.
    String mode = mount.group(1).replaceFirst(",.*", "");
    if (!mode.equals("ro")) {
      problems.add("the root file system of the core is writable: " + mode);
    }
    if (lines.size() > 4) {
      problems.add(
          "the image holds a build tool: " + String.join(" ", lines.subList(4, lines.size())));
    }
  }

  // The JVM runs as the first process, so the signal reaches it and it exits with 128 and 15.
  private void stop() {
    long start = context.nanos().getAsLong();
    compose("stop");
    double seconds = (context.nanos().getAsLong() - start) / 1e9;
    String exit = docker("inspect", "--format", "{{.State.ExitCode}}", CONTAINER).output().strip();
    if (!exit.equals("143") || seconds >= GRACE_SECONDS) {
      problems.add(
          String.format(
              Locale.ROOT,
              "a stop signal did not end the JVM inside the grace period: exit %s after %.1f s",
              exit,
              seconds));
    }
  }

  // curl waits between its tries inside the container, so the check keeps no clock of its own.
  // ponytail: the time to ready is known to the second; a shorter delay between tries lifts it.
  private Processes.Result probe(String probe, int tries) {
    return docker(
        "exec",
        CONTAINER,
        "curl",
        "--fail",
        "--silent",
        "--max-time",
        "2",
        "--retry",
        String.valueOf(tries),
        "--retry-delay",
        "1",
        "--retry-all-errors",
        "http://localhost:8080/actuator/health/" + probe);
  }

  // The stack runs the image under test, on a free port, in a time zone that is not UTC.
  private Processes.Result compose(String... args) {
    List<String> command =
        new ArrayList<>(
            List.of(
                "env", "METIS_IMAGE=" + image, "METIS_PORT=", "METIS_TIME_ZONE=Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh"));
    command.addAll(COMPOSE);
    command.addAll(List.of(args));
    return context.run().apply(context.root(), command);
  }

  private Processes.Result docker(String... args) {
    List<String> command = new ArrayList<>(List.of("docker"));
    command.addAll(List.of(args));
    return context.run().apply(context.root(), command);
  }
}
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools.canary;

import java.util.List;

/**
 * The counter-tests of the image check: a line added to the Dockerfile wins, or a change of stack.
 */
final class ImageCanaries {

  private static final String DOCKERFILE = "core/Dockerfile";

  static final List<Canary> ALL =
      List.of(
          Canary.of("image-root", "image", "the core runs as root")
              .appending(DOCKERFILE, "USER root\n"),
          // A shell running more than the JVM holds the stop signal back from it until grace ends.
          Canary.of("image-shell-entrypoint", "image", "inside the grace period")
              .appending(DOCKERFILE, "ENTRYPOINT java -jar core.jar && echo stopped\n"),
          Canary.of("image-root-write", "image", "Read-only file system")
              .appending(
                  DOCKERFILE,
                  "ENTRYPOINT [\"sh\", \"-c\", \"touch /started && exec java -jar core.jar\"]\n"),
          // The root user again, which the linter of the Dockerfile names on its own.
          Canary.of("image-hadolint", "image", "DL3002").appending(DOCKERFILE, "USER root\n"),
          // A library with a known vulnerability in the image, which only the scan of the image
          // sees.
          Canary.of("image-scan", "image", "CVE-2021-44228")
              .appending(
                  DOCKERFILE,
                  "ADD https://repo1.maven.org/maven2/org/apache/logging/log4j/log4j-core/2.14.1/"
                      + "log4j-core-2.14.1.jar /app/lib/\n"),
          // A writable root in the compose file, which the check reads back from the container.
          Canary.of("image-compose-writable", "image", "does not run the core locked down")
              .replacing("stack/compose.yaml", "    read_only: true\n", ""),
          // The root user in the compose file, which the image alone does not show.
          Canary.of("image-compose-root", "image", "the core runs as root")
              .replacing(
                  "stack/compose.yaml",
                  "    read_only: true\n",
                  "    user: \"0\"\n    read_only: true\n"),
          // A capability the compose file adds back, which the running core then holds.
          Canary.of("image-compose-capability", "image", "the core runs with a capability")
              .replacing(
                  "stack/compose.yaml",
                  "    cap_drop:\n      - ALL\n",
                  "    cap_add:\n      - NET_RAW\n    cap_drop:\n      - ALL\n"));

  private ImageCanaries() {}
}
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools;

import dev.metis.tools.canary.CanaryRun;
import dev.metis.tools.coverage.Coverage;
import dev.metis.tools.deadcode.Deadcode;
import dev.metis.tools.image.ImageCheck;
import dev.metis.tools.language.Language;
import dev.metis.tools.lint.Marks;
import dev.metis.tools.mutation.Mutations;
import dev.metis.tools.tests.TestReports;
import dev.metis.tools.verify.Verify;
import java.io.IOException;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import org.jspecify.annotations.Nullable;

/** The commands of the tool of the checks. */
public final class Cli {

  private static final Map<String, Command> COMMANDS =
      Map.of(
          "verify", Verify::command,
          "canary", CanaryRun::command,
          "language", Language::command,
          "marks", Marks::command,
          "tests", TestReports::command,
          "deadcode", Deadcode::command,
          "coverage", Coverage::command,
          "mutation-scope", Mutations::scope,
          "mutation", Mutations::judge,
          "image", ImageCheck::command);

  private static final String USAGE =
      """
      usage: verify [--only <check>[,<check>]] [--fast] [--append]
             canary <name>|all
             language [<path> ...]
             marks
             tests <check> <folder of test reports> ...
             deadcode <file of entry points> <project> ...
             coverage <JaCoCo XML report> ...
             mutation-scope [--given <globs> | --base <ref>] <project> ...
             mutation <project> ...
             image <image>""";

  private Cli() {}

  /** Runs the command the arguments name and returns its exit code. */
  public static int run(Context context, List<String> args) throws IOException {
    @Nullable Command command = args.isEmpty() ? null : COMMANDS.get(args.getFirst());
    if (command == null) {
      context.out().println(USAGE);
      return 2;
    }
    return command.run(context, args.subList(1, args.size()));
  }
}
```

`tools/build.gradle.kts`:

```kotlin
plugins {
    id("metis.java-conventions")
    application
}

application {
    mainClass = "dev.metis.tools.Main"
}

dependencies {
    implementation(libs.archunit)
    implementation("tools.jackson.core:jackson-core")
    implementation("tools.jackson.core:jackson-databind")
}

// A command of the tool, run from the repository root, for a check of the root build to depend on.
fun tool(name: String, vararg arguments: String) =
    tasks.register<JavaExec>(name) {
        classpath = sourceSets.main.get().runtimeClasspath
        mainClass = application.mainClass
        workingDir = rootDir
        args(*arguments)
    }

tool("language", "language")
tool("marks", "marks")
// The walk resolves the types the classes of both projects extend, so it runs on their classpaths.
evaluationDependsOn(":core")
tool("deadcode", "deadcode", "config/entry-points.txt", "core", "tools").configure {
    val core = project(":core").the<SourceSetContainer>()
    classpath += core["test"].runtimeClasspath + sourceSets.test.get().runtimeClasspath
    dependsOn(":core:testClasses", tasks.testClasses)
}
// The judges of the test tasks, which run after the tests even when a test failed.
tool("judgeArchitecture", "tests", "architecture", "core/build/test-results/architectureTest", "tools/build/test-results/architectureTest")
    .configure { mustRunAfter(":core:architectureTest", tasks.named("architectureTest")) }
tool("judgeDeadcode", "tests", "deadcode", "core/build/test-results/deadcodeTest")
    .configure { mustRunAfter(":core:deadcodeTest") }
tool(
    "judgeCoverage", "coverage", "core/build/reports/jacoco/test/jacocoTestReport.xml",
    "tools/build/reports/jacoco/test/jacocoTestReport.xml",
).configure { mustRunAfter(":core:jacocoTestReport", tasks.jacocoTestReport) }
// What PIT mutates: the classes of -Pmutate, else the classes changed since MUTATION_BASE, else all.
tool("mutationScope", "mutation-scope").configure {
    val given = providers.gradleProperty("mutate").map { listOf("--given", it) }
    val base = providers.environmentVariable("MUTATION_BASE").filter { it.isNotBlank() }.map { listOf("--base", it) }
    argumentProviders.add(CommandLineArgumentProvider { given.orElse(base).getOrElse(listOf()) + listOf("core", "tools") })
}
tool("judgeMutation", "mutation", "core", "tools").configure { mustRunAfter(":core:pitest", tasks.pitest) }
tool("imageRun", "image", "metis-core:check").configure { dependsOn(":imageBuild") }
tool("judgeTooling", "tests", "tooling", "tools/build/test-results/test").configure { mustRunAfter(tasks.test) }
tool("judgeUnit", "tests", "unit", "core/build/test-results/test").configure { mustRunAfter(":core:test") }

// ./verify and ./canary start the tool with the Java and the classpath this task writes, and the tool
// learns from it the check tasks Gradle has in every project, however a build file declares them.
val launcher = tasks.register("launcher") {
    val executable = javaToolchains.launcherFor(java.toolchain).map { it.executablePath.asFile.path }
    val classpath = sourceSets.main.map { it.runtimeClasspath }
    val checks = rootProject.allprojects.flatMap { project ->
        val prefix = if (project == rootProject) "" else project.path + ":"
        project.tasks.names.filter { it.matches(Regex("check[A-Z]\\w*")) }.map { prefix + it }
    }
    val folder = layout.buildDirectory.dir("launcher")
    inputs.files(classpath)
    inputs.property("java", executable)
    inputs.property("checks", checks)
    outputs.dir(folder)
    doLast {
        folder.get().file("java").asFile.writeText(executable.get() + "\n")
        folder.get().file("args").asFile.writeText("-cp\n\"" + classpath.get().asPath + "\"\n")
        folder.get().file("checks").asFile.writeText(checks.joinToString("") { "$it\n" })
    }
}

// The tests of the counter-tests read the list of checks the launcher writes.
tasks.named("testClasses") { dependsOn(launcher) }
```

`build.gradle.kts`:

```kotlin
plugins {
    alias(libs.plugins.spotless)
}

dependencyLocking {
    lockAllConfigurations()
}

spotless {
    java {
        target("core/src/**/*.java", "tools/src/**/*.java", "test-support/**/*.java")
        googleJavaFormat(libs.versions.google.java.format.get())
        removeUnusedImports()
    }
    format("misc") {
        target(
            "**/*.kts", "**/*.md", "**/*.yml", "**/*.yaml", "**/*.toml", "**/*.properties",
            "**/*.json", "**/*.xml", "**/*.txt", "**/Dockerfile", "**/.gitignore", ".dockerignore",
            "verify", "canary",
        )
        targetExclude("**/build/**", "**/.gradle/**", "**/.kotlin/**", "gradle/verification-metadata.xml")
        trimTrailingWhitespace()
        endWithNewline()
    }
}

// A scanner that is no Gradle plugin, run as its pinned image in the tree, which it reads only.
fun scanner(name: String, image: Provider<String>, options: List<String>, vararg arguments: String) =
    tasks.register<Exec>(name) {
        val tree = rootDir.absolutePath
        commandLine(
            listOf("docker", "run", "--rm", "--volume", "$tree:/work:ro", "--workdir", "/work") +
                options + listOf(image.get()) + arguments,
        )
    }

// Trivy keeps its database in a volume of its own, so a scan downloads it once a day at most.
val trivy = listOf("--volume", "metis-trivy-cache:/root/.cache")

scanner(
    "depsVulnerabilities", libs.versions.image.trivy, trivy,
    "fs", "--scanners", "vuln", "--exit-code", "1", "--quiet",
    "--skip-dirs", "/work/build", "--skip-dirs", "/work/**/build", "--skip-dirs", "/work/.gradle", "/work",
)

// A relative folder, so the paths the allow-list of .gitleaks.toml matches start at the root.
scanner(
    "secretsScan", libs.versions.image.gitleaks, listOf(),
    "dir", ".", "--no-banner", "--redact", "--verbose", "--config", ".gitleaks.toml",
)

// The image the image check builds from the sources, with Docker alone, as any platform would.
tasks.register<Exec>("imageBuild") {
    commandLine("docker", "build", "--file", "core/Dockerfile", "--tag", "metis-core:check", ".")
}

tasks.register<Exec>("imageLint") {
    val dockerfile = file("core/Dockerfile")
    commandLine("docker", "run", "--rm", "--interactive", libs.versions.image.hadolint.get(), "hadolint", "-")
    doFirst {
        standardInput = dockerfile.inputStream()
    }
}

// Trivy reads the image from an archive in the tree, so it needs no hand on the Docker daemon.
tasks.register<Exec>("imageSave") {
    dependsOn("imageBuild")
    val archive = layout.buildDirectory.file("image/core.tar")
    doFirst {
        archive.get().asFile.parentFile.mkdirs()
    }
    commandLine("docker", "save", "--output", archive.get().asFile.path, "metis-core:check")
}

scanner(
    "imageScan", libs.versions.image.trivy, trivy,
    "image", "--input", "/work/build/image/core.tar", "--scanners", "vuln", "--exit-code", "1", "--quiet",
).configure { dependsOn("imageSave") }

// The checks of ./verify, which runs them in the order of the list of the tool, Checks.ORDER.

tasks.register("checkFormat") {
    description = "Every source file is formatted."
    dependsOn("spotlessCheck")
}

tasks.register("checkCompile") {
    description = "The code compiles with every warning an error, no bug pattern and no null where none is allowed."
    dependsOn(":core:compileJava", ":core:compileTestJava", ":tools:compileJava", ":tools:compileTestJava")
}

tasks.register("checkLint") {
    description = "No method above a complexity of 10, no file above 300 lines, a reason on every mark."
    dependsOn(
        ":core:checkstyleMain", ":core:checkstyleTest", ":tools:checkstyleMain", ":tools:checkstyleTest",
        ":tools:marks",
    )
}

tasks.register("checkLanguage") {
    description = "English only, and no comment that cites a plan, a ruling, a task, a date or a line of a file."
    dependsOn(":tools:language")
}

tasks.register("checkArchitecture") {
    description = "The architecture rules of both projects hold."
    dependsOn(":core:architectureTest", ":tools:architectureTest", ":tools:judgeArchitecture")
}

tasks.register("checkDeadcode") {
    description = "Nothing unused: code, test helpers, dependencies and settings."
    dependsOn(
        ":core:projectHealth", ":tools:projectHealth", "bundledDeclared", ":tools:deadcode",
        ":core:deadcodeTest", ":tools:judgeDeadcode",
    )
}

tasks.register("checkTooling") {
    description = "The tests of the tool pass, and every check has a counter-test."
    dependsOn(":tools:test", ":tools:judgeTooling")
}

tasks.register("checkUnit") {
    description = "The tests of the core that need no container pass, none skipped, as many as the floor."
    dependsOn(":core:test", ":tools:judgeUnit")
}

tasks.register("checkCoverage") {
    description = "Every line and every branch of the core and the tool runs in a test."
    dependsOn(":core:jacocoTestReport", ":tools:jacocoTestReport", ":tools:judgeCoverage")
}

tasks.register("checkMutation") {
    description = "Every mutant PIT makes of the core and the tool is killed by a test."
    dependsOn(":core:pitest", ":tools:pitest", ":tools:judgeMutation")
}

tasks.register("checkDeps") {
    description = "No known vulnerability, only allowed licences, and current lock files and checksums."
    dependsOn("depsVulnerabilities", ":core:checkLicense", ":core:resolveLocked", ":tools:resolveLocked")
}

tasks.register("checkSecrets") {
    description = "No secret in the tree."
    dependsOn("secretsScan")
}

tasks.register("checkImage") {
    description = "The image builds from the sources, passes its linter and its scan, and runs locked down."
    dependsOn("imageLint", "imageBuild", "imageScan", ":tools:imageRun")
}

// A check whose judge did not run would pass on the exit of its tasks alone, so a check that owes
// facts fails without them; ./verify and ./canary clear the facts before each run of a check.
val factFree = setOf("checkFormat", "checkCompile", "checkDeps", "checkSecrets")
tasks.matching { it.name.matches(Regex("check[A-Z]\\w*")) && it.name !in factFree }.configureEach {
    val check = name.removePrefix("check").replaceFirstChar(Char::lowercase)
    val facts = layout.buildDirectory.file("facts/$check.txt")
    doLast {
        if (!facts.get().asFile.exists()) {
            throw GradleException("$name: its judge left no facts in build/facts/$check.txt")
        }
    }
}

// A starter stands for the libraries of it that the code uses, named one by one, which the plugin
// would otherwise ask to declare; a library a bundle names is never reported unused, so
// bundledDeclared refuses a project that declares one of them itself.
val starters =
    mapOf(
        "org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-webmvc" to listOf(
            "org.springframework.boot:spring-boot",
            "org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-autoconfigure",
            "org.springframework:spring-context",
        ),
        "org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-webmvc-test" to listOf(
            "org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-resttestclient",
            "org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-test",
            "org.springframework:spring-beans",
            "org.springframework:spring-core",
            "org.springframework:spring-test",
            "org.springframework:spring-web",
        ),
    )

configure<com.autonomousapps.DependencyAnalysisExtension> {
    structure {
        starters.forEach { (starter, libraries) ->
            bundle(starter.substringAfter(':')) {
                primary(starter)
                libraries.forEach { includeDependency(it) }
            }
        }
    }
    issues {
        all {
            onAny {
                severity("fail")
            }
        }
    }
}

val bundled = tasks.register("bundledDeclared") {
    description = "No project declares a library that a bundle names."
}

gradle.projectsEvaluated {
    val members = starters.values.flatten().toSet()
    val declared =
        subprojects.flatMap { project ->
            project.configurations.flatMap { configuration ->
                configuration.dependencies
                    .filter { "${it.group}:${it.name}" in members }
                    .map { "${it.group}:${it.name} in ${project.path} ${configuration.name}" }
            }
        }
    bundled.configure {
        doLast {
            if (declared.isNotEmpty()) {
                throw GradleException("a bundle names what a project declares, which it would never report: $declared")
            }
        }
    }
}
```

### Task 18: The CI workflow

The workflow only calls the launchers: the fast group on every push (`./verify --fast`), every check on a pull request with `MUTATION_BASE` set to the base branch, and every Monday `./verify --only deps` then `./canary all`; each job uploads `reports/verify.md`. Every action is pinned by the commit of its release, every checkout leaves no token behind, and the token may only read. `WorkflowTest` holds both rules; actionlint 1.7.12 joins the tooling check. CI has never run for this repository: it has no remote yet.

```java
package dev.metis.tools;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

import java.io.IOException;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.regex.Matcher;
import java.util.regex.Pattern;
import java.util.stream.Stream;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

// The rules of the workflow files of the repository, read on the files themselves.
class WorkflowTest {

  private static final Path WORKFLOWS = Path.of("../.github/workflows");
  private static final Pattern USES = Pattern.compile("uses:\\s*(\\S+)");

  private static List<String> workflows() throws IOException {
    try (Stream<Path> files = Files.list(WORKFLOWS)) {
      return files.sorted().map(WorkflowTest::read).toList();
    }
  }

  private static String read(Path file) {
    try {
      return Files.readString(file);
    } catch (IOException failed) {
      throw new AssertionError(failed);
    }
  }

  @Test
  void everyActionIsPinnedByTheCommitOfItsRelease() throws IOException {
    List<String> workflows = workflows();
    assertThat(workflows).isNotEmpty();
    for (String workflow : workflows) {
      Matcher uses = USES.matcher(workflow);
      while (uses.find()) {
        assertThat(uses.group(1))
            .as("is not pinned by commit")
            .matches("[\\w.-]+/[\\w.-]+@[0-9a-f]{40}");
      }
    }
  }

  @Test
  void everyCheckoutLeavesNoTokenBehindForTheStepsAfterIt() throws IOException {
    for (String workflow : workflows()) {
      long checkouts =
          workflow.lines().filter(line -> line.contains("uses: actions/checkout@")).count();
      long closed =
          workflow
              .lines()
              .filter(line -> line.strip().equals("persist-credentials: false"))
              .count();
      assertThat(closed).isEqualTo(checkouts);
    }
  }
}
```

`.github/workflows/check.yml`:

```yaml
# Every job calls ./verify or ./canary, so no check lives only here.
name: check

on:
  push:
    branches: ['**']
  pull_request:
  # By hand: the weekly cadence.
  workflow_dispatch:
  # Off the hour, because GitHub delays schedules that start on the hour.
  schedule:
    - cron: '17 3 * * 1'

# The least access of the token: read the code, write nothing.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  # Each push: the fast group, the checks from format to unit.
  fast:
    if: github.event_name == 'push'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      # The JDK that Gradle runs on; the build asks for this one, so it downloads none.
      - uses: actions/setup-java@de7274f081f381c8f8158605e0321c36c376e2e6 # v6.0.1
        with:
          distribution: corretto
          java-version: '25'
      - run: ./verify --fast
      - if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: verify-report
          path: reports/verify.md

  # Each pull request: every check, with mutation testing on the classes it changed.
  full:
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 90
    env:
      MUTATION_BASE: origin/${{ github.base_ref }}
    steps:
      # All history, so git finds where the pull request left its base branch.
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-java@de7274f081f381c8f8158605e0321c36c376e2e6 # v6.0.1
        with:
          distribution: corretto
          java-version: '25'
      - run: ./verify
      - if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: verify-report
          path: reports/verify.md

  # Weekly: the dependency check against new advisories, then every counter-test.
  weekly:
    if: github.event_name == 'schedule' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 120
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-java@de7274f081f381c8f8158605e0321c36c376e2e6 # v6.0.1
        with:
          distribution: corretto
          java-version: '25'
      - run: ./verify --only deps
      # A new advisory must not hide a blind check.
      - if: always()
        run: ./canary all
      - if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: verify-report
          path: reports/verify.md
```

```java
package dev.metis.tools.canary;

import java.util.List;

/** The counter-test of the tooling check. */
final class ToolingCanaries {

  static final List<Canary> ALL =
      List.of(
          // A check registered without a counter-test or a reason in NoCanary.
          Canary.of("tooling-no-counter-test", "tooling", "canary has neither a counter-test")
              .appending("build.gradle.kts", "\ntasks.register(\"checkCanary\")\n"),
          // A check registered in a project other than the root, which ./verify must see too.
          Canary.of("tooling-subproject-check", "tooling", ":core:checkIntegration")
              .appending("core/build.gradle.kts", "\ntasks.register(\"checkIntegration\")\n"),
          // A check registered with a type, which a reader of the text of the build would miss.
          Canary.of("tooling-typed-check", "tooling", "typed has neither a counter-test")
              .appending(
                  "build.gradle.kts",
                  "\ntasks.register<Exec>(\"checkTyped\") { commandLine(\"true\") }\n"),
          // An action pinned by a tag, which its owner can move to other code.
          Canary.of("tooling-unpinned-action", "tooling", "is not pinned by commit")
              .appending(
                  ".github/workflows/check.yml",
                  """

                    canary:
                      runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
                      steps:
                        - uses: actions/checkout@v7
                          with:
                            persist-credentials: false
                  """),
          // A job that reads a value no matrix defines, which only the workflow linter knows.
          Canary.of("tooling-actionlint", "tooling", "\"missing\" is not defined")
              .appending(
                  ".github/workflows/check.yml",
                  """

                    canary:
                      runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
                      steps:
                        - run: echo "${{ matrix.missing }}"
                  """));

  private ToolingCanaries() {}
}
```

`build.gradle.kts`:

```kotlin
plugins {
    alias(libs.plugins.spotless)
}

dependencyLocking {
    lockAllConfigurations()
}

spotless {
    java {
        target("core/src/**/*.java", "tools/src/**/*.java", "test-support/**/*.java")
        googleJavaFormat(libs.versions.google.java.format.get())
        removeUnusedImports()
    }
    format("misc") {
        target(
            "**/*.kts", "**/*.md", "**/*.yml", "**/*.yaml", "**/*.toml", "**/*.properties",
            "**/*.json", "**/*.xml", "**/*.txt", "**/Dockerfile", "**/.gitignore", ".dockerignore",
            "verify", "canary",
        )
        targetExclude("**/build/**", "**/.gradle/**", "**/.kotlin/**", "gradle/verification-metadata.xml")
        trimTrailingWhitespace()
        endWithNewline()
    }
}

// A scanner that is no Gradle plugin, run as its pinned image in the tree, which it reads only.
fun scanner(name: String, image: Provider<String>, options: List<String>, vararg arguments: String) =
    tasks.register<Exec>(name) {
        val tree = rootDir.absolutePath
        commandLine(
            listOf("docker", "run", "--rm", "--volume", "$tree:/work:ro", "--workdir", "/work") +
                options + listOf(image.get()) + arguments,
        )
    }

// Trivy keeps its database in a volume of its own, so a scan downloads it once a day at most.
val trivy = listOf("--volume", "metis-trivy-cache:/root/.cache")

scanner(
    "depsVulnerabilities", libs.versions.image.trivy, trivy,
    "fs", "--scanners", "vuln", "--exit-code", "1", "--quiet",
    "--skip-dirs", "/work/build", "--skip-dirs", "/work/**/build", "--skip-dirs", "/work/.gradle", "/work",
)

// A relative folder, so the paths the allow-list of .gitleaks.toml matches start at the root.
scanner(
    "secretsScan", libs.versions.image.gitleaks, listOf(),
    "dir", ".", "--no-banner", "--redact", "--verbose", "--config", ".gitleaks.toml",
)

// actionlint finds the workflows through .git, which the copy of a canary lacks, so each is named.
val workflows = file(".github/workflows").list().orEmpty().sorted().map { ".github/workflows/$it" }

scanner("workflowLint", libs.versions.image.actionlint, listOf(), "-color", *workflows.toTypedArray())

// The image the image check builds from the sources, with Docker alone, as any platform would.
tasks.register<Exec>("imageBuild") {
    commandLine("docker", "build", "--file", "core/Dockerfile", "--tag", "metis-core:check", ".")
}

tasks.register<Exec>("imageLint") {
    val dockerfile = file("core/Dockerfile")
    commandLine("docker", "run", "--rm", "--interactive", libs.versions.image.hadolint.get(), "hadolint", "-")
    doFirst {
        standardInput = dockerfile.inputStream()
    }
}

// Trivy reads the image from an archive in the tree, so it needs no hand on the Docker daemon.
tasks.register<Exec>("imageSave") {
    dependsOn("imageBuild")
    val archive = layout.buildDirectory.file("image/core.tar")
    doFirst {
        archive.get().asFile.parentFile.mkdirs()
    }
    commandLine("docker", "save", "--output", archive.get().asFile.path, "metis-core:check")
}

scanner(
    "imageScan", libs.versions.image.trivy, trivy,
    "image", "--input", "/work/build/image/core.tar", "--scanners", "vuln", "--exit-code", "1", "--quiet",
).configure { dependsOn("imageSave") }

// The checks of ./verify, which runs them in the order of the list of the tool, Checks.ORDER.

tasks.register("checkFormat") {
    description = "Every source file is formatted."
    dependsOn("spotlessCheck")
}

tasks.register("checkCompile") {
    description = "The code compiles with every warning an error, no bug pattern and no null where none is allowed."
    dependsOn(":core:compileJava", ":core:compileTestJava", ":tools:compileJava", ":tools:compileTestJava")
}

tasks.register("checkLint") {

    dependsOn(
        ":core:checkstyleMain", ":core:checkstyleTest", ":tools:checkstyleMain", ":tools:checkstyleTest",
        ":tools:marks",
    )
}

tasks.register("checkLanguage") {
    description = "English only, and no comment that cites a plan, a ruling, a task, a date or a line of a file."
    dependsOn(":tools:language")
}

tasks.register("checkArchitecture") {
    description = "The architecture rules of both projects hold."
    dependsOn(":core:architectureTest", ":tools:architectureTest", ":tools:judgeArchitecture")
}

tasks.register("checkDeadcode") {
    description = "Nothing unused: code, test helpers, dependencies and settings."
    dependsOn(
        ":core:projectHealth", ":tools:projectHealth", "bundledDeclared", ":tools:deadcode",
        ":core:deadcodeTest", ":tools:judgeDeadcode",
    )
}

tasks.register("checkTooling") {
    description = "The tests of the tool pass, every check has a counter-test, the workflow passes its linter."
    dependsOn(":tools:test", ":tools:judgeTooling", "workflowLint")
}

tasks.register("checkUnit") {
    description = "The tests of the core that need no container pass, none skipped, as many as the floor."
    dependsOn(":core:test", ":tools:judgeUnit")
}

tasks.register("checkCoverage") {
    description = "Every line and every branch of the core and the tool runs in a test."
    dependsOn(":core:jacocoTestReport", ":tools:jacocoTestReport", ":tools:judgeCoverage")
}

tasks.register("checkMutation") {
    description = "Every mutant PIT makes of the core and the tool is killed by a test."
    dependsOn(":core:pitest", ":tools:pitest", ":tools:judgeMutation")
}

tasks.register("checkDeps") {
    description = "No known vulnerability, only allowed licences, and current lock files and checksums."
    dependsOn("depsVulnerabilities", ":core:checkLicense", ":core:resolveLocked", ":tools:resolveLocked")
}

tasks.register("checkSecrets") {

    dependsOn("secretsScan")

tasks.register("checkImage") {
    description = "The image builds from the sources, passes its linter and its scan, and runs locked down."
    dependsOn("imageLint", "imageBuild", "imageScan", ":tools:imageRun")

// A check whose judge did not run would pass on the exit of its tasks alone, so a check that owes
// facts fails without them; ./verify and ./canary clear the facts before each run of a check.
val factFree = setOf("checkFormat", "checkCompile", "checkDeps", "checkSecrets")
tasks.matching { it.name.matches(Regex("check[A-Z]\\w*")) && it.name !in factFree }.configureEach {
    val check = name.removePrefix("check").replaceFirstChar(Char::lowercase)
    val facts = layout.buildDirectory.file("facts/$check.txt")
    doLast {
        if (!facts.get().asFile.exists()) {
            throw GradleException("$name: its judge left no facts in build/facts/$check.txt")
        }
    }
}

// A starter stands for the libraries of it that the code uses, named one by one, which the plugin
// would otherwise ask to declare; a library a bundle names is never reported unused, so
// bundledDeclared refuses a project that declares one of them itself.
val starters =
    mapOf(
        "org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-webmvc" to listOf(
            "org.springframework.boot:spring-boot",
            "org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-autoconfigure",

            "org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-resttestclient",
            "org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-test",
            "org.springframework:spring-beans",
            "org.springframework:spring-core",
            "org.springframework:spring-test",
            "org.springframework:spring-web",
        ),
    )

configure<com.autonomousapps.DependencyAnalysisExtension> {
    structure {
        starters.forEach { (starter, libraries) ->
            bundle(starter.substringAfter(':')) {
                primary(starter)
                libraries.forEach { includeDependency(it) }
            }
        }
    }
    issues {
        all {
            onAny {
                severity("fail")
            }
        }
    }
}

val bundled = tasks.register("bundledDeclared") {
    description = "No project declares a library that a bundle names."
}

gradle.projectsEvaluated {
    val members = starters.values.flatten().toSet()
    val declared =
        subprojects.flatMap { project ->
            project.configurations.flatMap { configuration ->
                configuration.dependencies
                    .filter { "${it.group}:${it.name}" in members }
                    .map { "${it.group}:${it.name} in ${project.path} ${configuration.name}" }
            }
        }
    bundled.configure {
        doLast {
            if (declared.isNotEmpty()) {
                throw GradleException("a bundle names what a project declares, which it would never report: $declared")
            }
        }
    }
}
```

- [ ] **Step 1: Write both files**

`README.md`:

```markdown
# metis-backend

The Metis backend: the business core (roles `api` and `worker`), the MCP gateway, the AI agent, the
Keycloak extensions and the sandbox images, built by the backend team. Today it holds the foundation:
the Gradle build, an empty core that builds as an image and runs in the local stack, and the tool
that runs every check and records the run.

Its documentation lives in the `metis-docs` repository: `architecture/` for how the parts fit and why,
and `components/core/`, `components/mcp-gateway/`, `components/agent/`, `components/keycloak/` and
`components/sandbox/` for each part.

## What a machine needs

Docker, and any JDK from 17 on to start Gradle, found through `JAVA_HOME` or the path. Gradle runs
itself and the build on Amazon Corretto 25, which it downloads on its first run.

## Commands

- `./verify` runs every check in order, goes on after a red one, and writes `reports/verify.json`
  and `reports/verify.md`; it exits 1 when a check is red.
- `./verify --fast` runs the fast group, the checks from format to unit, the set CI runs on every
  push.
- `./verify --only lint,unit --append` reruns some checks and adds their rows to the record.
- `./canary all` plants one defect per counter-test in a copy of the tree under `build/canary/` and
  requires each check to go red for it; `./canary lint-complexity` runs one.
- `./gradlew checkLint` runs one check; the checks are the tasks named `check` and a capital in
  `build.gradle.kts`.
- `docker build --file core/Dockerfile --tag metis-core:local .` builds the image from the sources.
- `docker compose --file stack/compose.yaml up --build --wait` starts the local stack, and
  `docker compose --file stack/compose.yaml down` stops it.
```

`AGENTS.md`:

```markdown
# AGENTS.md

Instructions for AI coding agents working in `metis-backend`.

## Read first

The documentation lives in the `metis-docs` repository, cloned beside this one as `../metis-docs`.
Read, in this order:

1. `../metis-docs/llms.txt`: the index of every current page.
2. `../metis-docs/architecture/overview.md`, then the folder under `../metis-docs/components/` of the
   part you work on: `core`, `mcp-gateway`, `agent`, `keycloak` or `sandbox`.
3. `../metis-docs/AGENTS.md` before you change any documentation.

`.claude/settings.json` lists `../metis-docs` under `permissions.additionalDirectories`. Once the
owner's probe confirms that Claude Code resolves that relative path from this folder, it reads the
clone without asking, after you accept the trust dialog for this folder. Until then, and wherever
it asks anyway, each developer adds the absolute path of their clone under the same key in
`.claude/settings.local.json`, which git ignores.

## Rules

- The pages about the backend that describe what is not built yet are drafts. Read the decision
  records in `../metis-docs/architecture/decisions/` before you choose a library or a pattern.
- Code, comments, test names, log messages and tool output are English. A letter outside ASCII is
  allowed only on the line after a `lang-exception` comment that gives its reason after the colon,
  and `./gradlew checkLanguage` rejects any other.
- A comment is one line that says why. It never names a plan, a ruling, a task, a date or a line of
  another file. A deliberate shortcut says `ponytail: <its ceiling>; <how to lift it>`.
- Every escape hatch gives its reason and is counted in `config/debt.json`: a suppressed warning,
  a method left out of mutation testing, an annotation whose name holds `Generated` (JaCoCo and PIT
  leave out what it marks), an excused line of the language check, a class left out of coverage in
  `config/coverage-exclusions.txt`. A walk entry in `config/entry-points.txt` gives its reason too.
- The number of tests that pass equals `test-floor.json`, so a change that adds or removes tests
  updates it; no test is skipped or disabled.
- Never edit what a command writes: `gradlew`, `gradle/wrapper/`, `gradle/gradle-daemon-jvm.properties`,
  the `gradle.lockfile` files and `gradle/verification-metadata.xml`. After a change of the
  dependencies, write the locks and the checksums again, with every task run for real, since a task
  restored from the build cache resolves nothing:
  `./gradlew --refresh-dependencies --write-locks --write-verification-metadata sha256 --rerun-tasks help spotlessCheck :core:checkLicense`.
- A new check is a task named `check` and a capital in the root `build.gradle.kts` and a row of
  `Checks.ORDER` in the tool, in the order of the spec; `./verify` refuses a check task the list
  lacks, in whatever project it is registered. It has its counter-test in
  `tools/src/main/java/dev/metis/tools/canary/` or its reason in the `NoCanary` table of the
  tool's tests, and `./gradlew checkTooling` fails a check that has neither. Its judge leaves
  facts in `build/facts/`, or the check fails, unless the root build names it in `factFree`.
- No project declares a library that a bundle of the root build names: a bundle stands for its
  starter, so a library it names is never reported unused, and `./gradlew checkDeadcode` refuses
  the declaration.
- Before you hand work back, run the fast checks, the set CI runs on every push: `./verify --fast`.
- A change of behaviour needs its documentation change in `metis-docs`.
```
