## Review round one

Three reviews of the delivered `metis-backend` (architecture, code, testability) found what follows. Each fix is folded into the tasks above, test first, and each fix that closes a blind spot has the counter-test that would have caught it.

| Finding | Fix | Proof |
|---|---|---|
| A1: the bundle of every Spring group hid an unused Spring library from the Dependency Analysis plugin | One bundle per starter that names, one by one, the libraries of it the code uses; the actuator starter is a dependency of the run only (Tasks 2 and 12). A library a bundle names still hides when it is declared alone and unused, so the bundles name nothing else, and round two refuses that declaration (A9) | Counter-tests deadcode-spring-dependency (`spring-expression` in the core) and deadcode-dependency (`slf4j-api` in the tool, outside every bundle) |
| A4, T3, C1: the checks were found by a pattern over the text of the build, blind to a typed task | The launcher writes the check tasks Gradle has; the tool keeps `Checks.ORDER`, and a check task it lacks stops `./verify`; `CanariesTest` reads the list of Gradle (Tasks 4, 6 and 10) | `ChecksTest`, `VerifyCommandTest`; counter-test tooling-typed-check |
| A3, C9: the fast group was every check before coverage | `Checks.FAST`, the first ten of the spec, format to unit (Task 4) | `ChecksTest.theFastGroupIsTheFirstTenChecksOfTheSpecWhichEndAtUnit`, `PlanTest.fastRunsTheFastGroupOfTheSpecSoAContainerCheckAfterUnitIsLeftOut` |
| A2: the run of the image was written twice, and only the copy in Java was checked | The image check runs the image from `stack/compose.yaml`, under its own project on a free port, and reads the lock-down back from the container (Tasks 16 and 17) | `ImageCheckTest.aStackThatDoesNotRunTheCoreLockedDownIsRedWithWhatItRunsWith`; counter-test image-compose-writable |
| C2, A5: a row was green on the exit of Gradle alone | Every check but format, compile, deps and secrets fails when its judge leaves no facts; `./verify` and `./canary` clear the facts before each run (Task 7) | Counter-test unit-no-judge; `CanaryRunTest.theFactsOfTheGreenRunAreGoneBeforeTheRunOnThePlantedDefect` |
| C3: the coverage and mutation judges added the projects up | Each report judged on its own: a report that measured no line is red and is removed before it is made; PIT leaves a trace for a project without mutants (Tasks 13 and 14) | `CoverageTest`, `MutationsTest`; counter-tests coverage-no-report and mutation-no-report; mutation-weak-test now plants in the core |
| T2, C4: an annotation named Generated left code out of JaCoCo and PIT unseen | Counted as the mark `Generated`, with its reason, in `config/debt.json`, held at 0 (Task 9) | `MarksTest`; counter-test lint-generated |
| T4, C5: a suppression counted only at the start of a line | Every mark in the code of a Java line, strings and comments left out by `Comments.javaCode` (Tasks 8 and 9) | `MarksTest`, `CommentsTest`; counter-test lint-parameter-suppression |
| C6: the language check never read SQL comments | A kind of file for SQL: `--` and `/* */`, strings stepped over (Task 8) | `CommentsTest`; counter-test language-sql-date |
| T1: nothing proved that tests run in a random order | `TestOrderTest` in `test-support`, run by both test tasks (Task 10) | Counter-test unit-fixed-order |
| T5: the settings test read `application.yml` alone | It reads every `application*.yml`, `.yaml` and `.properties` (Task 12) | Counter-test deadcode-setting, now on `application-canary.yml` |
| T6: five tools had no counter-test of their own | One each, expecting a text only that tool prints (Tasks 7, 15, 17 and 18) | Counter-tests format-misc, deps-lock, image-hadolint, image-scan, tooling-actionlint |
| T7: the test of a reverse lookup could not fail | `LocalResolver`, tried with a builtin resolver that records its calls (Task 10) | `LocalHostOnlyTest.aReverseLookupOffThisMachineFailsBeforeTheBuiltinResolverIsAsked` |
| T8: unit-failing expected a text a compile error also prints | It expects `CanaryFailingTest > one() FAILED` (Task 10) | The counter-test |
| T9: seven hidden endpoints were tried, not all | `ProbesTest` reads the discovery page, which names self, health and health-path alone (Task 2) | Counter-test unit-exposed-endpoint |
| C7: a file that is not UTF-8 was skipped | Only a NUL byte makes a file binary; the language check reports `not-utf8` (Tasks 8 and 9) | `LanguageCommandTest`, `TextFilesTest`, `MarksTest`; no counter-test, since a counter-test plants text, which is written as UTF-8 |
| C7, second part: the files are those of the folder, not those git lists | Not changed: the copy of a counter-test has no `.git`, so the checks read the folder; round two skips the folders a build writes by their exact place | None |
| C8: the output of git held its warnings | `Processes.quiet` keeps standard error out of what git prints, and `Context.git()` uses it (Tasks 3 and 6) | `ProcessesTest.quietKeepsTheStandardOutputAloneAndAddsTheErrorsOnlyToAFailure` |
| C10: Trivy had the Docker socket | `imageSave` writes an archive, which Trivy reads with `--input` (Task 17) | `checkImage` green; counter-test image-scan |
| C11: the root user was told by name | `id -u` must not print 0, inside the running core since round two (Task 17) | `ImageCheckTest.aCoreThatRunsAsRootHoldsACapabilityHasAWritableRootOrABuildToolIsRed`; counter-test image-root |
| A6: coverage runs the tests again | Named in the comment of the conventions; plan two chooses between the rerun and the execution data of the same run | The comment |
| A7: four shrinks | Done: one `ImageCheck` per run; the tasks of the tool take `application.mainClass`. Kept: `--only=<list>`, which the parser of the app also takes; `language <path>`, which lets a developer check one file and has its test | None |

## Review round two

The same three reviews read the fixes of round one and found ten things more. Each fix is folded into the tasks above, test first, and each hole has the counter-test that would have caught it.

| Finding | Fix | Proof |
|---|---|---|
| A2, C12: the image check read the lock-down from outside the stack, so `user: "0"` or `cap_add: [NET_RAW]` on the core service of `stack/compose.yaml` still read back as locked | The check probes the running core with `docker exec`: `id -u`, the effective and bounding capabilities of the JVM in `/proc/1/status`, the mount of the root in `/proc/mounts` and the build tools; the read-back of `docker inspect` also holds the capabilities added, privileged mode and the mounts (Task 17) | `ImageCheckTest.aCoreThatRunsAsRootHoldsACapabilityHasAWritableRootOrABuildToolIsRed`; counter-tests image-compose-root ("the core runs as root") and image-compose-capability ("the core runs with a capability: CapEff: 0000000000000000, CapBnd: 0000000000002000"); image-root now expects "the core runs as root" |
| C13, the regression of C11: the probe of the user ignored its exit status, and its standard error could pass for a build tool | The probe runs through `Processes.quiet`, must exit 0 and must print a user of digits alone and a mount of the root; anything else is red as "cannot read the user and the capabilities of the core" (Task 17) | `ImageCheckTest.aProbeOfTheCoreThatFailsOrPrintsNoUserProvesNothingAndIsRed` |
| A8: the teardown of the image check kept named volumes | `down --volumes` before and after each run, so each image check starts from nothing once plan two adds a database (Task 17) | `ImageCheckTest.anImageTheStackRunsLockedDownThatAnswersItsProbesAndStopsIsGreenWithItsMeasures` pins both calls |
| A9: a library a bundle names stayed hidden from the unused-dependency rule when declared directly, and the bundle of the web starter named Jackson, which the tool declares | Each bundle names only the libraries of its starter that the code uses: `spring-boot`, `spring-boot-autoconfigure` and `spring-context` for the web starter, six Spring libraries for the test starter; the task `bundledDeclared`, which `checkDeadcode` runs, refuses a project that declares a library a bundle names; AGENTS.md says so (Tasks 12 and 19) | Counter-test deadcode-bundle-member: `spring-web` declared in the core and unused, which the plugin itself did not report; only `bundledDeclared` failed |
| N1: a check task registered in a project other than the root was invisible to `./verify`, CI and the counter-test rule | The launcher writes the check tasks of every project; `Checks.of` refuses any the list lacks, but for the two tasks of the licence report plugin, which `checkDeps` runs (Tasks 4 and 6) | `ChecksTest.aCheckTaskTheListLacksIsAnErrorWhateverWayAndInWhateverProjectItWasDeclared`, `ChecksTest.aTaskOfAPluginThatACheckRunsIsNoCheckOfItsOwn`; counter-test tooling-subproject-check |
| N2: deadcode-dependency and deadcode-spring-dependency expected coordinates that a lock error also prints | They expect the advice of the plugin, `implementation("org.slf4j:slf4j-api` and `implementation("org.springframework:spring-expression`, which no error of the lock prints (Task 12) | The two counter-tests |
| N3: the checksum half of deps had no counter-test | deps-checksum replaces the sha256 of `awaitility-4.3.0.jar` in `gradle/verification-metadata.xml`, a library of the tests of the core and of no plugin of the build, so the tasks of the check find it: `:core:resolveLocked` fails on it, and `:tools:resolveLocked` fails on the same artifact after it in the same build, though alone it passes (Task 15) | The counter-test: "One artifact failed verification: awaitility-4.3.0.jar" |
| C3, what was left: an exclusion list that removed every class of the core still read "core 0" in mutation and passed | The coverage judge already fails a project that measured no line; `Marks` now refuses an exclusion list that leaves out every class under `src/main/java` of a project (Task 9). A full mutation run red for a project with code and no mutant waits for the first mutant of the core | `MarksTest.anExclusionListThatLeavesOutEveryProductionClassOfAProjectIsAProblem`; counter-test lint-whole-project-excluded |
| C7, what was left: a UTF-16 file was skipped as binary, and a folder named `reports` or `build` at any depth was skipped, so it hid marks and language problems | A file that opens with the byte order mark of UTF-16 is text, reported `not-utf8`; `.git` and `reports` are skipped at the root alone, and `build`, `.gradle` and `.kotlin` only beside a Gradle script; `.gitignore` and `.dockerignore` place `build` and `reports` the same way, so a package of that name is committed and reaches the image (Tasks 1, 8 and 16) | `TextFilesTest.aFolderNamedLikeOneABuildWritesIsReadWhereNoGradleScriptStandsBesideIt`, `TextFilesTest.aBinaryFileIsNoTextWhereverItsNulByteIsButAFileInAnotherEncodingIsText`, `LanguageCommandTest.aFileThatIsNotUtf8IsAProblemAndTheFactsCountTheFiles`; counter-test lint-nested-reports; none for UTF-16, since a counter-test writes its text as UTF-8 |
| C14, the regression of C8: a wrong mutation base failed without the reason git gave | `Processes.quiet` adds standard error to the output of a failure alone, read on a thread of its own so that neither stream waits for the other; `Git.changedSince` prints it (Tasks 3 and 6) | `ProcessesTest.quietKeepsTheStandardOutputAloneAndAddsTheErrorsOnlyToAFailure`, `GitTest.aBaseTheRealGitCannotReadFailsWithTheReasonGitGives` |

|---|---|---|
| C15: `.gitleaks.toml` allowed every folder named `build`, so a key in a package of that name, which git now keeps and the image now copies, was never scanned | The allow-list names `.git`, `reports/`, `build/` and the `build/` of each project, `.gradle` and `.kotlin` by their exact place, as `.gitignore` places them; gitleaks reads the tree as `.`, so the paths it matches start at the root (Task 15) | Counter-test secrets-nested-build: missed before the fix ("checkSecrets did NOT catch the planted defect"), red after it with `File: core/src/main/java/dev/metis/core/build/canary.pem` |

The final `./canary all` in the sandbox: 58 of 58 counter-tests went red because of their planted defect, in 10 min 42 s at nice 19; the command exited 0.

Not run, each with its reason: the CI workflow (the repository has no remote yet, so GitHub has never run it); the image for amd64 (this machine builds arm64 only); `MUTATION_BASE` against a real history (the repository has no commit, so only the tests of `Scope` and `Git.changedSince` prove it); a stop during a slow request inside the image (`ShutdownTest` proves it in the JVM).

## What the sandbox taught

- Gradle workers cannot be capped from the settings. Symptom: "Using 10 worker leases" after `startParameter.maxWorkerCount` was set in `settings.gradle.kts`. Cause: Gradle reads the start parameter before the settings run. Fix: the tool passes `--max-workers` with half the cores, and every command of this plan passes `--max-workers=5`.
- google-java-format 1.37.0 fails inside Spotless 8.10.4. Symptom: `NoSuchMethodError` on `JavaFormatterOptions$Style.valueOf`. Cause: the glue of Spotless 8.10.4 predates the change of that API. Fix: google-java-format 1.36.1, the nearest release that works.
- Spotless refuses google-java-format 1.36.1 on a daemon older than JDK 21. Symptom: "You are running Spotless on JVM 17, which limits you to google-java-format 1.28.0". Cause: the daemon ran on the JDK that started Gradle. Fix: `updateDaemonJvm` pins the daemon to Corretto 25 in `gradle/gradle-daemon-jvm.properties`.
- google-java-format 1.36.1 cannot parse `import module java.base;`, even on JDK 25 ("error: '.' expected"). Fix: no module import; statements before `super()` format fine.
- The Dependency Analysis plugin applied at the root does nothing. Symptom: "No project health reports found". Fix: the settings plugin `com.autonomousapps.build-health`; a project with the plain `java` plugin gets no `projectHealth`, so `tools` applies `application`; each Spring Boot starter stands for the libraries of it the code uses through a bundle that names them one by one.
- A library that a bundle of the Dependency Analysis plugin names is hidden when it is declared and not used, since the bundle stands for it. Symptom: the counter-test deadcode-dependency, which declared `jackson-databind` in the core, went blind once the bundles named the libraries of the starter. Fix: the bundles name only what each starter brings and the code uses, and the counter-tests plant libraries no bundle names.
- The licence report prints one licence per library, while `checkLicense` passes a library when one of its licences is allowed, so a library under two licences passes on either. The POMs name licences in many ways; the SPDX normaliser maps them, so the allow-list holds SPDX ids only.
- Checksums written on a warm cache miss parent POMs. Symptom: the build stage of the image failed on `kotlinx-coroutines-bom` 1.8.0, which the host had resolved long before. Fix: `--refresh-dependencies` with `--write-verification-metadata`, and the tasks that resolve when they run (`spotlessCheck`, `:core:checkLicense`) in the same command.
- A run that writes the checksums records only what it resolves. Symptom: in the replay of this page the counter-test deps-vulnerability said "checkDeps was already red before planting", with "Checksums are missing from verification metadata" for `jspecify-1.0.1.pom`. Cause: the licence report came from the build cache in the run that wrote the checksums, so the POMs it reads were never resolved there, while the copy under `build/canary` ran it for real. Fix: `--rerun-tasks` in that command.
- `amazoncorretto:25-al2023` has no `xargs`, which `gradlew` needs ("xargs is not available"). Fix: the build stage runs `org.gradle.wrapper.GradleWrapperMain` from the wrapper jar.
- Trivy found, in the first image, 26 HIGH vulnerabilities in packages of the operating system (libX11, libXrender, openssl, python3-pip-wheel among them), 3 CRITICAL in Tomcat 11.0.24 and HIGH ones in Jackson 3.1.5. `dnf upgrade --security` alone said "Nothing to do", since the pinned base reads its own release, `2023.12.20260930`. Fix: Tomcat 11.0.25, Jackson 3.1.7, and the security fixes of a later release. `--releasever=latest` made the image depend on the day of its build, so the release is pinned: on the day, the newest `system-release` the latest repository offered was `2023.12.20261013`, and both names resolved to the same repository (`guids/9418de15...`). Two builds without cache then installed the same packages (one `rpm -qa | sort` hash), and Trivy exits 0 on the image and on the lock files. The base keeps reading `2023.12.20260930` in `/etc/amazon-linux-release`, since `system-release` is no security update.
- Error Prone reports an unused local as `[UnnamedVariable]`, not `[UnusedVariable]`, on Java 25; the counter-test compile-unused-local expects that name.
- Mutants without effect, each removed by rewriting rather than marked: a `switch` on strings gives a mutant of its hash code, so `Cli` dispatches through a `Map`; Jackson 3 throws on a node of the wrong type, so a check of the type before `stringValue()` was redundant; a guard that the code after it repeats was dropped.
- PIT writes no file at all for classes without a mutant, the core's today: no `mutations.xml`, no page. An `index.html` the probe of Task 1 had left in the sandbox first passed for a report of the core. Fix: the pitest task leaves a trace, `build/reports/pitest/ran`, the scope removes the reports and the trace of an earlier run, the judge requires the trace for each project of the scope, and a full run without any mutant is red.
- curl's warnings between its tries went into the answer of the probe, which then never equalled `{"status":"UP"}`. Fix: `--silent` without `--show-error`.
- A shell entry point that runs one command execs it, so the JVM still runs as the first process; the counter-test image-shell-entrypoint uses `java -jar core.jar && echo stopped`, which keeps the shell first, and the check measured "exit 137 after 30.2 s".
- actionlint finds the workflows through `.git`, which the copy of a counter-test lacks. Symptom: both counter-tests of the tooling check said "checkTooling was already red before planting" in `./canary all`. Fix: the root build names each workflow file to actionlint.
- The verify command reads the root build to find the checks, so the root build exists from Task 6, with no check yet; the replay of this page found it.
- `--priority=low` under `nice -n 19` starts a daemon of its own at nice 20 on macOS, and the test executors inherit it; the normal daemon is left alone.
- The image a counter-test builds in its copy takes the tag `metis-core:check`, so after `./canary all` that tag holds the last planted image; the next `./verify` builds it again before it runs it.
- A record accessor read only inside its record counts as unused for the walk, which follows calls: `Context.git()` reads its edge through `quiet()`.
- `archunit-junit6-engine-api` 1.5.1 asks for `junit-platform-engine` 6.1.3, and JUnit's own alignment then raised the whole family to 6.1.3 on the test runtime classpath, while the compile classpath stayed on the 6.0.3 Spring Boot 4.1.1 manages. Fix: the catalog's `junit-bom` 6.1.3 as a platform of the tests, one version on both classpaths from Task 1 on.
- `docker images` shows the image unpacked (729MB in the trial run), while `docker image inspect` gives its content (182886911 bytes); the fact of the record says "image content" so the two are not confused.
- `SettingsTest` first missed boolean settings: `Properties.stringPropertyNames()` skips a value that is not a string, which the counter-test deadcode-setting found; the test reads `keySet()`.
- google-java-format wraps a line comment longer than 100 characters, which leaves a comment of two lines; every comment fits in one.
- `docker inspect` of a container compose started shows the user compose gave it only in `.Config.User`, and a separate `docker run` of the image shows the user of the image; only a probe inside the running container reads what the stack runs.
- A capability compose adds back to a user other than root is not effective in the JVM, `CapEff` stays 0, but it stays in the bounding set: `CapBnd` read `0000000000002000` for `NET_RAW`, so the probe reads both.
- `/proc/mounts` gives the options of the overlay root with the path of every layer; the check names only the first option, `ro` or `rw`.
- With `spring-web` declared in the core and unused, the Dependency Analysis plugin reported nothing, since a bundle named it; only `bundledDeclared` failed.
- gitleaks names the files of a scan of `/work` as `/work/...`, so a path of its allow-list anchored at the start matched nothing: `^reports/` never applied. The scan reads `.` instead, whose paths are relative, and every path of the allow-list is anchored.
- A failed dependency verification fails every later resolution of the same build: `:tools:resolveLocked` reported `awaitility-4.3.0.jar` on its `annotationProcessor` configuration, which does not hold it, after `:core:resolveLocked` failed, and passed when it ran alone.
- Tampering the checksum of a library that a plugin of the build also needs fails every Gradle command while the build configures, before any task runs: the first try of deps-checksum, on `jspecify-1.0.1.jar`, proved nothing of `resolveLocked`, so the counter-test tampers a library only the tests of the core resolve.

## Left for plan two

- The roots of the walk that Spring finds by itself: a controller, a bean or a listener reached by scanning. Today the one such class, `TestEndpoints`, is listed in `config/entry-points.txt`; the first module of plan two needs the walk to treat the Spring stereotypes as roots.
- `@DoNotMutate`: the rule and its debt count exist, the annotation does not, since no method needs it yet.
- The language check reads code comments only; a `@DisplayName` title would need its own rule, and no test has one.
- The clock bean, the first user of the rule against the system clock.
- A stop during a slow request inside the image, the latency budget of the image check, and the image for amd64.
- The first run of the CI workflow, once the repository has a remote, and `MUTATION_BASE` on a real history.
- A full mutation run red for a project with code and no mutant: the core has no mutant today, so the rule comes with its first one.
- `test-support` on the source set of the integration tests, so that `TestOrderTest` proves their random order too.
- The coverage and mutation judges name their projects, `core` and `tools`; a new Gradle project joins both lists.
- What section 2 of the spec leaves to plan two: PostgreSQL, Flyway, Testcontainers and the integration check, Spring Security, the modules, the contract, Keycloak and the demo data.
